### REMED-GFX-063 — Bgfx: custom `Viewport` honored in render-target views (setViewRect on RT views) — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | MEDIUM / P2 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (Bgfx — both OpenGL and Vulkan renderers)** |
| Commits | test `131b8a30`, fix `bba401ff`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause | `BgfxGraphicsBackend::ApplyViewportOverride()` gated the custom viewport on `currentViewId_ == 0` (the backbuffer view), so a custom `Viewport` set while a `RenderTarget2D`/`RenderTargetCube`/MRT was bound was ignored — RT views kept the full-RT `setViewRect` from `BindAsRenderTarget()`/`EnsureViewState()`. Only the backbuffer honored a custom `Viewport` (Task 880). |

**Bgfx view-state model (independently established, Phases 1/5/6) — NOT the Vulkan per-draw shape.**
bgfx view state (`setViewRect`, `setViewTransform`, `setViewFrameBuffer`, `setViewClear`) is **per-view**,
evaluated once per view per `bgfx::frame()`: the **last** `setViewRect(viewId,...)` before the frame advance
applies to **every** draw submitted to that view. It is *not* per-draw (unlike `bgfx::setScissor`, which is
per-draw — that is why the GFX-013 scissor fix used a different mechanism). Each `RenderTarget2D`/Cube/MRT
owns a **distinct** bgfx view id (`Detail::AllocateRtViewId()`, free-list-backed, ≤255); `SetRenderTarget`
points `currentViewId_`/`spriteViewId` at the bound target's own view (0 for the backbuffer). So the correct
fix for the common **one-viewport-per-RT-pass** case is simply to let `ApplyViewportOverride()` — already
called right before every 3D submit, *after* any `EnsureViewState()`/`BindAsRenderTarget()` full-target reset —
call `setViewRect(currentViewId_, vp)` for the RT view, making it the winning view rect for that pass.

**Fix (`bba401ff`, `BgfxGraphicsBackend.cpp` only — one functional line).** Removed the `currentViewId_ == 0`
gate from `ApplyViewportOverride()` (`if (viewportSet_ && viewportW_ > 0 && viewportH_ > 0) setViewRect(currentViewId_, …)`).
No new state, no per-draw capture, no view-id allocation → **no view-id-exhaustion risk** (Phase 14). Byte-identical
for the backbuffer (view 0 still honored) and for any RT draw with no custom viewport (viewportSet_ holds the
full-RT reset value → `setViewRect(rtView, 0,0,rtW,rtH)`, the same rect `BindAsRenderTarget` already set).

**Coordinate/Y convention (Phases 9/10).** `Viewport(x,y,w,h)` is passed **raw** to `setViewRect(rtView,x,y,w,h)`
— top-left origin, bgfx's own convention; bgfx normalizes the underlying renderer's origin (GL bottom-left vs
others) internally, so **no manual Y-flip** and **no target-size arithmetic** (nothing dimension-dependent to get
wrong — Phase 9 has no failure mode here). The regression's asymmetric above/below probes confirm no vertical
mirror. **MinDepth/MaxDepth (Phase 11): unchanged accepted Bgfx deviation** — bgfx has no per-view depth-range
knob (documented in `SetViewport()`, mirrors `SetVirtualResolution`); NOT faked, NOT part of GFX-063.

**Test (`131b8a30`).** `examples/bgfx_rendertarget_viewport_test.cpp` (`Bgfx_RenderTarget_Viewport`), the proven
Bgfx RT-sample methodology (`bgfx_rendertarget2d_msaa_test`): render a full-NDC quad into a **64×48** RT under
`Viewport(11,7,29,18)`, unbind, `SpriteBatch`-blit 1:1 to the 64×64 backbuffer, read the whole region in one
`GetBackBufferData` call (Bgfx first-read-per-frame quirk), probe pixels. Scenario A = custom viewport 5-way
asymmetric probe (inside RED; left/right/above/below BLACK); Scenario B = full-viewport control (all RED).
64×48 chosen because it reads back **upright** (see GFX-067). **Pre-fix 6/10** (scenario A's four outside probes
RED = viewport ignored / full-target). **Post-fix 10/10.**

**Bgfx renderer matrix (Phase 15).** Verified on **bgfx-OpenGL** (active renderer OpenGL 2.1, Mesa/llvmpipe under
Xvfb :99 — the default the shard uses) **and bgfx-Vulkan** (active renderer Vulkan, real AMD GPU, `DISPLAY=:0`,
`CNA_BGFX_RENDERER=VULKAN`): **10/10 on both.** Not claimed for D3D/Metal renderers (not available here).

**SpriteBatch vs 3D (Phase 7).** The fix targets the 3D submit path (`ApplyViewportOverride`), which is where the
finding and the DrawUserPrimitives test live. The RT-blit itself is a backbuffer sprite draw under the full
(reset) backbuffer viewport, so it is unaffected. A SpriteBatch fill *into* an RT under a custom viewport is not
covered (its NDC mapping is built from the full-target size in `EnsureViewState`, a distinct sprite-projection
concern — same nuance noted for Vulkan GFX-062); not part of this fix.

**Scissor interaction (Phase 12) — recorded as GFX-066; SINCE DISPROVEN, see that entry.** A GFX-063-era note
claimed Bgfx's per-draw `bgfx::setScissor` does "not clip on FBO/render-target views at all." **This was WRONG** — a
test-setup artifact (a `ScissorRectangle` set without an effective `ScissorTestEnable=true`, i.e. XNA-correct no-clip).
GFX-066 runtime-verified that the RT scissor **clips correctly on both bgfx-OpenGL and bgfx-Vulkan** (new
`Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor` 13/13 each), and the Viewport∩Scissor RT interaction that this note said was blocked
**works today**. GFX-013's "Bgfx honors RT scissor" source read was correct. See the REMED-GFX-066 entry.

**Regression matrix (Phase 16).** `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Viewport` 10/10; backbuffer controls `Bgfx_Viewport_Subregion`
+ `Bgfx_Scissor` PASS; targeted RT/orientation/skinned/envmap/fog families green except **2 pre-existing
environment failures** — `Bgfx_RenderTarget2D_MsaaResolve` and `Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_DepthFormat` — both caused
by bgfx-Vulkan falling back to OpenGL 2.1 here (no DRI3 under Xvfb; MSAA-resolve/real-depth don't work under GL
2.1). **Confirmed identical with the fix reverted → not regressions.** **Full Bgfx shard (≤ -j2, Xvfb stability):
5740/5746.** The 6 failures = 3 stable pre-existing graphics (`CnjEffectTest.LoadsRealCnjFixture`,
`CnjStockEffectTest.CustomGlslEffectStillWorks`, `GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest.DoesNotSupportWireFrame`=GFX-036
— identical to the Vulkan-shard baseline) + 1 pre-existing Bgfx env (`Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_DepthFormat`,
bgfx-Vulkan→GL2.1 fallback, verified identical with the fix reverted) + 2 flaky (`ENetDiscoveryServiceTest`
network, `DynamicSoundEffectInstanceTest` audio — both PASSED on isolated retry). `Bgfx_RenderTarget2D_MsaaResolve`
passed in the full shard. My change is viewport-only, with no causal path to any of these. GFX-005/006/007/008/010
Bgfx families unaffected. No `bx`/Xvfb death. **Zero regressions.**

**Generated shaders.** None — zero `.sc`/`.glsl`/`bgfx_shaders.hpp` diff (pure bgfx view-state handling).

**New findings spawned (recorded):** **GFX-065** (two viewports on one view per frame — bgfx per-view
limit, affects backbuffer too — still open), **GFX-066** (RT `setScissor` inert — **since DISPROVEN: NOT A DEFECT**,
RT scissor clips correctly on both bgfx renderers; false finding, regression added), **GFX-067** (RT-size-dependent
RT-sample readback Y-mirror — still open). None inseparable from the viewport fix.

### REMED-GFX-018 — Bgfx: exact ClearOptions attachment masks and ordered full-target clears — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | HIGH / P1 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (Bgfx OpenGL 2.1 + Bgfx Vulkan; cross-backend controls)** |
| Commits | regression `7d176292`, production fix `aad8ed4f`, exact depth-probe strengthening `72cf5fb7`, docs (this entry) |
| Affected files | `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/Bgfx/BgfxGraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/Bgfx/BgfxGraphicsBackend.cpp`, `examples/bgfx_graphicsdevice_clearoptions_test.cpp`, `cmake/Tests/BgfxTests.cmake` |
| Backends / Platforms | Production change: Bgfx only. Runtime verification: Bgfx OpenGL 2.1 and Vulkan; controls on native Vulkan, EasyGL, SDL_GPU, Software, and D3D11/DXVK. |

**Exact public CNA/XNA contract.**

| Public `ClearOptions` value | Colour | Depth | Stencil |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| zero flags | preserve | preserve | preserve |
| `Target` | clear | preserve | preserve |
| `DepthBuffer` | preserve | clear | preserve |
| `Stencil` | preserve | preserve | clear |
| `Target` + `DepthBuffer` | clear | clear | preserve |
| `Target` + `Stencil` | clear | preserve | clear |
| `DepthBuffer` + `Stencil` | preserve | clear | clear |
| `Target` + `DepthBuffer` + `Stencil` | clear | clear | clear |

The union rule applies identically to the backbuffer and the currently-bound `RenderTarget2D`, and `Clear` covers
the whole bound target: neither the current viewport nor an enabled scissor limits it. The zero value is publicly
reachable with `static_cast<ClearOptions>(0)` and is a true no-op. The convenience overloads are also fixed by
the public layer: `Clear(float r,g,b,a)` is colour-only; `Clear(Color,float)` is colour+depth; `Clear(Color)` is
colour+depth+stencil with depth equal to `Viewport.MaxDepth` and stencil zero.

Attachment availability remains owned by `GraphicsDevice`, not the Bgfx fix. It validates a requested depth
value against `[0,1]` before capability masking. When the bound target has `DepthFormat::None`, it then masks the
request down to `Target`: valid depth/stencil-only requests are ignored, mixed requests still clear colour, and
an invalid requested depth still throws. A `Depth24` target accepts a stencil bit but has no stencil aspect, so
that unavailable aspect is ignored while colour/depth follow the mask. `Depth24Stencil8` exposes all three
independent effects. No public `ClearOptions` API or validation rule changed.

**Confirmed production defect and exact drop point.** The finding was genuine, not a readback-only failure.
`GraphicsDevice::Clear` correctly decoded every mask and dispatched the corresponding backend overload, but
Bgfx discarded that distinction at `BgfxGraphicsBackend::EnsureViewState`: every base view was assigned
`BGFX_CLEAR_COLOR | BGFX_CLEAR_DEPTH | BGFX_CLEAR_STENCIL`, while segment views were assigned
`BGFX_CLEAR_NONE`. Colour-bearing overloads only changed stored values and converged on that unconditional
view clear; `ClearDepth` merely stored the float and never recorded a clear. Thus Target-only, either single
depth/stencil flag, and every pair were widened, suppressed, or delayed independently of the requested mask.

There was a second Bgfx-specific ordering consequence. `setViewClear`, `setViewFrameBuffer`, and `setViewRect`
are per-view state resolved once at `bgfx::frame()`; their last configuration wins for every submission on that
view. Reusing a view for clear→draw→clear, multiple clears, or a same-frame target A→B→A sequence could collapse
different masks/values or retroactively redirect an earlier operation. This is the same underlying bgfx
view-global state model handled by GFX-065/GFX-084, not a reason to redesign the backend.

**Small production fix.** `RecordClear(uint16_t)` is the single mask-recording point. Each backend clear overload
updates exactly the arguments it owns, maps only its requested bits to `BGFX_CLEAR_COLOR`, `BGFX_CLEAR_DEPTH`,
and/or `BGFX_CLEAR_STENCIL`, assigns the bound framebuffer and full target rect, and touches that ordered view.
The first operation may use the target's base view; every later clear uses the existing monotonic GFX-065
segment-id pool, so ascending bgfx view execution preserves CNA call order. A per-frame used-base bitmap forces a
fresh segment when a target is rebound A→B→A instead of reconfiguring A's already-consumed base view. Mask,
packed RGBA, depth float, and stencil byte remain attached to the clear's own view until submission.

Draw-only viewport and SpriteBatch-transform segments now explicitly use `BGFX_CLEAR_NONE` and therefore load
colour, depth, and stencil. This intentionally supersedes GFX-065's former implicit depth+stencil clear on a 3D
viewport segment: public `Clear` now establishes full-target depth/stencil state in its own ordered view, so an
implicit later clear would violate attachment preservation. GFX-065 viewport ordering and GFX-084 transform
ordering still use the same allocator and keys; no parallel segmentation system was introduced.

**Permanent public regression and fixture audit.** `Bgfx_GraphicsDevice_ClearOptions` begins from distinct values
(colour `(31,73,121,183)`, depth `0.23`, stencil `0x2d`) and requests distinct values
(`(207,91,43,97)`, `0.67`, `0xa6`). RGB is sampled directly, alpha is observed through
`DestinationAlpha` blending, requested depth is bracketed to ±0.01 after converting to each route's clip-depth
convention, and stencil is checked with exact equal/distinct-reference draws. Every check establishes explicit
`BlendState`, `DepthStencilState`, `RasterizerState`, full viewport, and scissor state; the clear itself runs
under a restrictive custom viewport and enabled scissor, with preserved/cleared values sampled at both corners
outside that subregion.

The initial regression exposed 67 failures (**165/232**) against the faulty production mapping. Fixture review
also found a separate invalid assumption: swapchain contents are not guaranteed to survive `Present`, whereas
`RenderTargetUsage::PreserveContents` does provide the RT producer/consumer contract. The permanent test therefore
seeds the backbuffer earlier in the same ordered frame and uses ordinary producer frames only for preserve-content
RTs. Assertions were not weakened, and no extra test frame or `Present` was added to coax readback. Each observable
result comes from exactly one whole-framebuffer snapshot, matching the completed GFX-017 harness correction.

Coverage includes all eight masks, the three convenience overloads, backbuffer, `Depth24Stencil8`, `Depth24`, and
depthless RTs, exact values, repeated and interleaved clears, clear→draw→clear ordering, target isolation,
A→B→A, and full-target viewport/scissor independence. It passes **232/232** with active renderer
**OpenGL 2.1** and **232/232** with active renderer **Vulkan**.

**Verification.**

- Bgfx Vulkan GFX-018 was run under `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`; the complete output was inspected and contains
  zero VUID/validation errors. The only diagnostic is the benign optional `librenderdoc.so`-not-found warning.
- Existing Bgfx controls pass on both OpenGL and Vulkan: ClearDepth **2/2**, ClearStencil **2/2**,
  GFX-065 `Bgfx_MultiViewport` **15/15**, GFX-084 `Bgfx_SpriteBatch_Transform` **21/21**, and the corrected
  GFX-017 public culling regression **81/81**.
- Equivalent public controls pass on native Vulkan (**4/4** depth contract, **2/2** depth clear,
  **2/2** stencil clear; validation clean), EasyGL (**9/9** overloads, **2/2** depth, **2/2** stencil),
  SDL_GPU (**8/8** smoke and **16/16** render-state), Software (**6/6** smoke and **3/3** depth contract),
  and D3D11 through Wine/DXVK (**4/4** depth contract and **2/2** stencil).
- All fourteen backend libraries compile with no more than four jobs: ASCII, Bgfx, Canvas, D3D11, D3D12, D3D9,
  EasyGL, DX3, Headless, SDL_GPU, SDL_Renderer, Software, Vulkan, and WebGPU.

| New findings | None. |

### REMED-GFX-065 — Bgfx: bgfx per-view rect cannot represent two different viewports on one view within a frame — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | LOW / P3 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (bgfx-OpenGL 2.1, Xvfb :99 + bgfx-Vulkan, real GPU :0)** |
| Commits | test `104025d2` (`Bgfx_MultiViewport`), fix `d40375c3`, test refinement + stress `d4b6ac12`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause | bgfx `setViewRect`/`setViewTransform` are per-view state: the last call before `bgfx::frame()` applies to all draws in that view. Viewport A → draw, Viewport B → draw, all into the same target/view within one un-advanced frame → both draws render under B, the first is lost. A **global** bgfx-view-model limitation (backbuffer view 0 and RT views alike), independent of GFX-063. Per-draw `setScissor`/model-transform are unaffected (draw-local, GFX-066). |

**Architecture — ordered per-frame view segmentation (Phase 6/7/8/23/37).** bgfx executes configured views in ascending view-id order each frame (the same property the Task-951 flush view relies on). The fix keeps the target's BASE view (view 0 / RT id) for the FIRST viewport exactly as pre-GFX-065 — a custom viewport still shrinks that base rect (GFX-063) — so a single-viewport frame is byte-identical (one view, no extra state). Only a SECOND, DIFFERENT viewport in the same frame allocates an ordered SEGMENT view id from a reserved `[kFirstSegmentViewId=192, 255)` range that sits ABOVE every RT base id (`AllocateRtViewId` capped to `[1,192)`), so within one target its base view (lowest id) then its segments (higher ids, monotonic in submission order) execute in draw order. `SelectViewportSegment()` runs at the head of both submit paths (`ApplyViewportOverride` for 3D, `SubmitSprite` for sprites), compares the live viewport to the ACTIVE segment's viewport, and on a change redirects `currentViewId_`/`spriteViewId` to a fresh segment configured for the same framebuffer.

**A→B→A ordering (Phase 29, the key regression guard).** The segment identity is compared only against the ACTIVE (most-recent) segment, never an older one, so returning to viewport A after B starts a NEW segment (id > B's) rather than merging back into A's first view — execution stays base(A)→seg(B)→seg(A2) and A2 draws on top. `Bgfx_MultiViewport` section C proves it (blue at the A-only corner and the overlap, green at the B-only corner).

**Depth across segments (Phase 27).** bgfx's per-view clear is scoped to the view RECT, so the base view cleared only the FIRST viewport's region; a later viewport's depth was otherwise stale/accumulated across frames and its z=0 3D draws failed `DEPTH_TEST_LESS` from frame 2 on (the initial green=0 symptom during bring-up). Each segment therefore clears its OWN depth+stencil (to the frame's `clearDepthValue_`/`clearStencilValue_`) so the new viewport's 3D draws test a fresh buffer, while PRESERVING colour (earlier segments' pixels). Sprite segments clear nothing (`EnsureViewState` sets `BGFX_CLEAR_NONE` for ids ≥192 — sprites don't depth-test). **Clear scope is unchanged from pre-fix** — a custom viewport shrinks the base rect so `Clear` clears the viewport region (matches XNA/D3D9's viewport-scoped Clear); an earlier full-target-clear variant was reverted because it added a view to the single-viewport RT render and shifted GFX-063's blit-readback pipeline (deterministic 6/10).

**ViewId lifecycle / capacity (Phase 20/21/22).** `AllocateSegmentViewId` is monotonic per-frame; `EndFrameSegments` (after every `bgfx::frame()` in `Present`/`ReadBackbuffer`) recycles `segmentNextId_` to 192 and repoints currentViewId_/spriteViewId at the base — no monotonic leak. Exhausting the 63-segment/frame range throws a clear `runtime_error` (deterministic hard cap; no silent view-id wrap, no hidden `bgfx::frame()`). `ResetSegmentTarget(baseId, fbo)` on every `SetRenderTarget2D`/`SetRenderTargets`/`SetRenderTargetCubeFace` points the tracker at the bound target's base view + framebuffer (MRT keeps its full attachment set).

**Verification (`Bgfx_MultiViewport` 9→15/15, deterministic ×3 on bgfx-GL AND bgfx-Vulkan real GPU):** A 3D two disjoint viewports (black→red flip); B SpriteBatch two disjoint; C 3D A→B→A ordering (overlap); D RenderTarget2D two viewports; E same-viewport consecutive draws → one segment reused (green fully covers red inside the viewport); F 16 disjoint-band viewports in one frame → 16 ordered segments + per-frame recycling. Whole-target readback with a warmup-drain + section-unique freshness sentinel handles bgfx's first-read-per-frame latency.

**Regression matrix (Phase 42-46, 53) — green on BOTH renderers:** GFX-063 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Viewport` 10/10, GFX-066 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor` 13/13, GFX-067 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Orientation` 72/72, GFX-072 `Bgfx_SpriteBatch_CustomViewport` 10/10, GFX-078 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_EffectTexture` 32/32, `Bgfx_Viewport_Subregion` 5/5, `Bgfx_Scissor` 7/7; full `^Bgfx_` ctest shard **120/124** — the 4 failures (`Bgfx_RenderTarget2D_MsaaResolve`, `Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_MipChain`, `Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_MsaaResolve`, `Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_DepthFormat`) are the documented pre-existing bgfx-Vulkan→GL2.1-fallback env failures, **verified IDENTICAL with the fix stashed**. RT producer→consumer ordering (GFX-067/078) preserved (segment ids above RT bases but below the flush view; single-viewport RT renders unchanged). **Zero shader/generated-artifact diff.**

### REMED-GFX-084 — Bgfx: SpriteBatch view transform last-wins for same-viewport / different-Begin-transform batches — DONE and VERIFIED (bgfx-OpenGL 2.1 + bgfx-Vulkan)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | LOW / P3 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (bgfx-OpenGL 2.1, Xvfb :99 + bgfx-Vulkan, real GPU :0)** |
| Commits | test `0e68f0dc`, fix `da8dda88`, docs (this entry) |
| Affected files | `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/Bgfx/BgfxGraphicsBackend.cpp` (`SelectViewportSegment` gains a `spritePath` flag + transform key; `SubmitSprite`/`ApplyViewportOverride` call sites), `include/.../BgfxGraphicsBackend.hpp` (`segCurSpriteTransform*` members + signature), `examples/bgfx_spritebatch_transform_test.cpp` (new), `cmake/Tests/BgfxTests.cmake` (registration). **No shader/generated-artifact diff.** |
| Backends / Platforms | Bgfx / ALL (verified bgfx-OpenGL 2.1 + bgfx-Vulkan) |

**Root cause (confirmed at runtime).** `EnsureViewState` bakes `SpriteBatch.Begin(transformMatrix)` (stored in
`spriteTransform_`) into the sprite view's PER-VIEW `bgfx::setViewTransform` — `orthoWithTransform =
transformColMajor * ortho` (line 1463, the file's **only** `setViewTransform` call). bgfx resolves per-view
state once at `bgfx::frame()` (last-write-wins). GFX-065's ordered segmentation keyed segments on the VIEWPORT
only (`SelectViewportSegment` compared just the viewport rect), so two SpriteBatch batches that share the same
`GraphicsDevice.Viewport` but pass DIFFERENT transforms in one un-advanced frame submitted to the SAME view id
→ the last batch's `setViewTransform` won for BOTH; the first batch's sprites rendered under the wrong (last)
transform. One residual axis of the same bgfx view-global-state last-wins class GFX-065 fixed for the viewport.

**Pre-fix runtime signature (`Bgfx_SpriteBatch_Transform` 11/21, IDENTICAL on bgfx-OpenGL and bgfx-Vulkan).**
Same full viewport, two batches in one frame: RED at `Begin(translation A)`, GREEN at `Begin(translation B)`.
Pre-fix RED renders at **B's** transformed location (last-wins) and is covered by GREEN → RED's own location is
BLACK (0 red px). Reproduced on every axis: translation (A: 0 red px), A→B→A ordering (B: the middle transform's
region is lost/black), scale (C: the 0.5-scale batch renders unscaled at the last-wins identity → wrong place),
RenderTarget2D (E: 0 red px), 32 distinct transforms (F: all collapse onto the last transform → **1/32** visible),
viewport+transform composition (G: the first same-viewport transform is lost inside a multi-viewport frame),
default/identity/custom (H: the default & identity batches are shifted by the trailing custom batch's transform).

**Exact `setViewTransform` state that was overwritten.** For a sprite view, the view-global matrix is
`orthoWithTransform = spriteTransform_(colMajor) · ortho`, where `ortho` is `bx::mtxOrtho` built from the sprite
view's full size and (GFX-072) an offset for a custom viewport. Only `spriteTransform_` varies between two
same-viewport batches (ortho is fixed by target+viewport), so the value stomped is precisely the earlier batch's
`spriteTransform_·ortho`, replaced by the later batch's.

**Affected SpriteBatch paths.** All of them — the single `SubmitSprite`→`EnsureViewState`→`setViewTransform`
path serves every `SpriteBatch.Draw`/`DrawString` (Deferred/Immediate/sort modes all funnel through it), on the
backbuffer and on RenderTarget2D/Cube/MRT (each target owns a base view id; the sprite path segments within it).

**Generic 3D did NOT have the same problem (verified, not merely asserted).** `bgfx::setViewTransform` has
exactly one caller (`EnsureViewState`, the sprite/clear view setup). The 3D draw sites
(`DrawUserPrimitives`/`DrawPrimitives`/indexed/etc.) call `ApplyViewportOverride` (→ `setViewRect`) but **never**
`setViewTransform`; they supply their own world-view-projection per draw via a uniform and ignore bgfx's built-in
view/proj. So the residual view-global last-wins case really is SpriteBatch-only (GFX-065's inventory claim,
now confirmed). No new finding.

**Fix — extend the ordered segment key to the sprite view transform (sprite path only).**
`SelectViewportSegment(bool spritePath)`: the active segment now also tracks a SpriteBatch view-transform identity
(`segCurSpriteTransformValid_` + `segCurSpriteTransform_`). On the **sprite** path (`SubmitSprite` →
`SelectViewportSegment(true)`), a batch reuses the active view only when the viewport matches AND (the segment has
no committed sprite transform yet — e.g. it was established by a 3D draw/Clear, so the sprite adopts it — OR the
committed transform equals this batch's); otherwise it allocates the next ordered segment view, exactly like a
viewport change (same `[192,255)` recycled pool, `setViewFrameBuffer` + full rect + depth/stencil clear; the sprite
path's `EnsureViewState` then resets that segment to `CLEAR_NONE` so it LOADs earlier colour and never clears
depth). On the **3D** path (`ApplyViewportOverride` → `SelectViewportSegment(false)`) the transform is neither
read nor committed (`segCurSpriteTransformValid_` stays false), so 3D behaviour is unchanged and a following sprite
can still adopt a 3D-established view without churn.

**Segment compatibility key (final).** A segment is reused iff: target/framebuffer identity matches
(`ResetSegmentTarget`), viewport rect matches (GFX-063/065), AND — for a sprite submission — the committed sprite
view transform matches (or is unset). A 3D submission ignores the transform axis. One ordered ViewId allocator
(`AllocateSegmentViewId`, monotonic, recycled by `EndFrameSegments`); no second segmentation system.

**Transform comparison strategy (Phase 8/13).** Keying on the raw `spriteTransform_` is **exactly** equivalent to
keying on the effective `orthoWithTransform`: `ortho` is a pure, invertible function of the viewport + full size
(both already in the key), so identical `(viewport, transform)` ⟺ identical effective view matrix — no divergence,
single source of truth. `Matrix::operator==` is **exact per-component float equality**, so a default `Begin()`
(which passes `Matrix::getIdentityProperty()`) and an explicit `Matrix::Identity` compare equal and reuse one
segment, while a genuinely different transform always allocates — no epsilon merging of meaningfully different
transforms, no unnecessary segment churn.

**A→B→A result.** Section B (translation A → RED, B → GREEN, A → BLUE, A regions overlapping): post-fix BLUE (the
2nd A batch, a NEW ordered segment — never merged back into the 1st A) wins in the A region and GREEN survives in
the B region; base(A)→seg(B)→seg(A2) executes in submission order. **Same-transform reuse.** Section D: 70
same-transform `Begin/Draw/End` cycles in ONE frame allocate ZERO segments (would exhaust the 63-id pool and throw
if each Begin segmented) → no explosion; the last colour wins (ordering within the reused view). **Viewport+transform
composition.** Section G: `(VpA,TxX)`, `(VpA,TxY)`, `(VpB,TxY)` all survive at distinct spots — GFX-065 (viewport)
and GFX-084 (transform) segment axes compose. **RT result.** Section E (48×40 RenderTarget2D, two transforms, then
sampled to the backbuffer): both batches survive (192 red + 192 green px); no backbuffer-state dependency; GFX-067
sample orientation unchanged.

**Clear / depth behaviour (Phase 21/22).** A transform-only sprite segment keeps GFX-065's sprite-segment rule:
`EnsureViewState` sets `CLEAR_NONE` for any view id ≥ `kFirstSegmentViewId`, so it preserves earlier segments'
colour and never clears depth (sprites don't depth-test). No new full-target clear; the base view still performs
the requested `Clear`. Verified by the disjoint-gap-stays-black checks and the A→B→A colour-preservation checks.

**Segment capacity / stress (Phase 27/44).** Transform changes now draw from the same 63-id `[192,255)` pool. Section
F: 32 distinct transforms in one frame → 31 ordered segments (< 63), all 32 sprites land at their own spot
(**32/32**); the pool recycles every frame across the settle loop (a monotonic leak would exhaust it and throw).
Section D: 70 identical-state cycles → 1 view. `AllocateSegmentViewId` still throws deterministically on genuine
exhaustion (no silent wrap).

**Performance.** The common case is unchanged: one target / one viewport / one transform / repeated identical
Begin/End → ZERO ephemeral segments (base view only). A new segment is allocated only for a genuine incompatible
view-global transition (viewport OR sprite transform). Section D proves identical consecutive batches do not grow
the segment count.

**OpenGL / Vulkan matrix.** Defect AND fix are renderer-independent (bgfx view model): `Bgfx_SpriteBatch_Transform`
**11/21 pre-fix and 21/21 post-fix on BOTH** bgfx-OpenGL 2.1 (Xvfb :99) and bgfx-Vulkan (real AMD Radeon 780M/RADV,
:0). **Vulkan validation:** run under the KHRONOS validation layer (`VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`,
layer confirmed loaded) → 21/21 with **zero VUID / validation errors**.

**Regression matrix (both renderers).** GFX-063 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Viewport` 10/10, GFX-065 `Bgfx_MultiViewport`
15/15, GFX-066 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor` 13/13, GFX-067 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Orientation` 72/72, GFX-072
`Bgfx_SpriteBatch_CustomViewport` 10/10, GFX-078 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_EffectTexture` 32/32, GFX-081
`Bgfx_SpriteBatch_BeginRasterizerState` 4/4, existing `Bgfx_SpriteBatch_TransformMatrix` 2/2. Full `^Bgfx_` shard
(bgfx-OpenGL) **121/125** — the 4 failures are the documented pre-existing bgfx-Vulkan→GL2.1-fallback
`*MsaaResolve`/`RenderTargetCube_MipChain`/`*DepthFormat` env failures (unrelated to view segmentation).

**Final bgfx view-global-state inventory (Phase 36/37).** `setViewRect` = viewport-keyed segment boundary
(GFX-063/065); `setViewTransform` = sprite-transform-keyed segment boundary (GFX-084, this task) / not used by 3D;
`setViewClear` = per-segment (base clears; sprite segments `CLEAR_NONE`; 3D viewport segments depth+stencil);
`setViewFrameBuffer` = per-target/per-segment (`ResetSegmentTarget`); `setViewMode` / `setViewOrder` /
`setViewScissor` = **never called** (bgfx defaults, constant, safe; per-draw `setScissor` is draw-local, GFX-066).
**No remaining unexplained view-global last-wins state in the covered Bgfx paths.**

| New findings | None. Confirmed generic 3D is immune (never programs `setViewTransform`); `setViewMode`/`setViewOrder` unused. |

### REMED-GFX-066 — Bgfx: per-draw `bgfx::setScissor` on render-target (FBO) views — RESOLVED, NOT A DEFECT (false finding; regression added)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | MEDIUM / P2 / GRAPHICS / **RESOLVED — NOT A DEFECT (false finding disproven at runtime on both bgfx renderers; zero production change; regression test added)** |
| Commits | test `f89efb82` (`Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor`), docs `ece95926` |
| Actual root cause | **The finding does not reproduce.** The Bgfx per-draw scissor already clips **correctly** on FBO/render-target views on both bgfx-OpenGL (2.1) and bgfx-Vulkan (real GPU). The GFX-063 bring-up "whole RT red / no clipping" observation was a **test-setup artifact**: a `ScissorRectangle` was set but `RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable=true` was not effective on the draw, so `ApplyScissorOverride()` (gated on `scissorEnabled_`) correctly no-op'd and the whole target filled — which is the **XNA-correct** result when the scissor test is disabled (reproduced exactly by Scenario B of the new test). |

**Runtime disproof (Phases 1/4/5/6) — both bgfx renderers, HEAD, zero production change.**
New pixel test `examples/bgfx_rendertarget_scissor_test.cpp` (`Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor`, 64×48 RT, proven
RT-sample→blit→`GetBackBufferData` path from GFX-063): render a full-NDC quad into the RT with an asymmetric
`ScissorRectangle (12,8,20,13)` and `ScissorTestEnable=true`, blit 1:1 to the backbuffer, probe. **The red is
confined exactly to x[12,32) y[8,21) — correct origin, no Y-mirror, correct width/height — on bgfx-OpenGL AND
bgfx-Vulkan (13/13 PASS each; deterministic over 3 consecutive GL runs).** Backbuffer control `Bgfx_Scissor` 7/7.

**Why the source read (GFX-013 parity note) and the bring-up empirics both mislead — and what is actually true.**
`ApplyScissorOverride()` issues `bgfx::setScissor(x,y,w,h)` (per-draw) right before every 3D `submit(currentViewId_)`,
where `currentViewId_` is the bound RT's own view id. In **both** bgfx renderers the per-draw scissor is intersected
with the view rect and applied against the **framebuffer** height, not the backbuffer: renderer_gl.cpp `setFrameBuffer`
returns `frameBuffer.m_height` as `resolutionHeight` (used for the scissor Y-flip) and `scissorRect.setIntersect(viewScissorRect=viewState.m_rect, cache[scissor])`; renderer_vk.cpp sets `vkCmdSetScissor` from the same intersection with
top-left origin. So a full-RT view rect (0,0,64,48) ∩ scissor (12,8,20,13) = (12,8,20,13) clips correctly. No
CNA-level defect either: `scissorEnabled_`/`scissorX_..H_` are assigned **only** in `ApplyRasterizerState`/`SetScissorRect`;
`SetRenderTarget2D`/`SetRenderTargets`/`BindAsRenderTarget` never reset them, so scissor state persists across RT binds
exactly as XNA requires (device-global, not per-target) — there is no ordering/reset defect.

**Regression scope (Phases 8/9/15) — three order-stable scenarios committed; two more verified in isolation.**
Committed (`Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor`, deterministic 13/13 on GL and Vulkan): **A** scissor enabled → red only
inside; **B** scissor disabled (rect still set) → whole target red (the false-finding symptom, XNA-correct, guards
against over-clip); **C** two per-draw scissors in **one** RT view/frame (red under a left rect, green under a right
rect, disjoint gap black) → proves per-draw scissor independence, which distinguishes GFX-066 from the per-view
GFX-065 viewport limit. Two further scenarios were **verified correct in isolation** (grids captured) but deliberately
excluded to keep the test deterministic — a 4th/5th RT-sample readback in one `Draw()` trips the separate,
pre-existing **GFX-067** RT-readback Y-mirror (Phase-3 contamination guard): (i) a **different** scissor rect
`(30,20,24,16)` re-enabled reads upright (proves no stale-scissor leak); (ii) **Viewport ∩ Scissor** —
`Viewport(10,6,30,26)` (GFX-063) ∩ `Scissor(20,4,25,20)` renders red at exactly **x[20,40) y[6,24)**, i.e. the
intersection in framebuffer coordinates (not scissor-relative-to-viewport, not viewport-overwriting-scissor). This
**unblocks** the Viewport∩Scissor RT-interaction that GFX-063 said GFX-066 blocked: it works today.

**SpriteBatch vs 3D / RT types.** The scissor path (`ApplyScissorOverride` → `setScissor` → `submit`) is shared by the
3D draw sites and the SpriteBatch submit (`ApplyScissorOverride` before `submit(spriteViewId)`); the RT view id is the
same mechanism for RenderTarget2D/Cube/MRT (each owns a view id, `SetRenderTarget*` points `currentViewId_` at it), so
the correct-clipping result is not RT-type-specific. Tested via RenderTarget2D (the finding's own shape).

**Regression matrix (Phase 16/18).** `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor` 13/13 (GL ×3 + Vulkan). Full targeted Bgfx sweep
**116/116** (`ctest -R Bgfx_` excluding the 3 known pre-existing bgfx-Vulkan→GL2.1-fallback env failures
`*MsaaResolve`/`*DepthFormat`/`*CubeMap` documented under GFX-063) — includes `Bgfx_Scissor`,
`Bgfx_Viewport_Subregion`, `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Viewport`, and the GFX-005/006/007/008/010 fog/normal/emissive/skinned
families. **Zero regressions** (expected — the change is test-only). **Generated shaders: none** — zero `.sc`/`bgfx_shaders.hpp`
diff; no `src/` diff at all.

**Correction propagated.** The GFX-063 report's Scissor-interaction note ("Bgfx's per-draw `bgfx::setScissor` does not
clip on FBO/render-target views at all") and GFX-013's parity claim were both **incorrect**; corrected here and in the
GFX-063 entry. GFX-013's "Bgfx honors RT scissor via `bgfx::setScissor` per draw" was source-read-only but, unlike the
bring-up claim, turns out to be **right**.

| Affected files | `examples/bgfx_rendertarget_scissor_test.cpp` (new), `cmake/Tests/BgfxTests.cmake` (registration). **No production/shader change.** |
| Backends / Platforms | Bgfx / ALL (verified bgfx-OpenGL 2.1 + bgfx-Vulkan) |
| New findings | None new. Re-confirms **GFX-067** (RT-readback Y-mirror on the 4th/5th RT-sample readback in one frame-sequence — the reason two scenarios stay isolation-only) as still open and still needing its own root-cause. |

### REMED-GFX-067 — Bgfx: RenderTarget2D sampled through SpriteBatch reads vertically mirrored on originBottomLeft renderers — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | MEDIUM / P2 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (bgfx-OpenGL 2.1, Xvfb :99; bgfx-Vulkan, real GPU :0)** |
| Commits | test `61eb3956`, fix `2c6cf6b6`, docs (this entry) |

**Confirmed AND reclassified — the "size dependency" was FALSE.** A four-quadrant orientation pattern (TL=RED, TR=GREEN, BL=BLUE, BR=YELLOW) rendered into a `RenderTarget2D`, `SpriteBatch`-blitted 1:1 onto the backbuffer and read back reads **vertically mirrored on EVERY tested size** on bgfx-OpenGL (18-size matrix 32×32 → 64×64: all VFLIP), **upright on every size** on bgfx-Vulkan. The historically-reported "48×32/40×48/64×56 flip; 64×48 upright" was not a real size rule.

**Root cause (Phase 24).** On bgfx renderers whose `bgfx::getCaps()->originBottomLeft` is `true` (OpenGL / GLES / WebGL — measured `originBottomLeft=1`, `homogeneousDepth=1` here), a render target's color attachment (an FBO texture) stores its texel memory **bottom-up**. CNA's `SpriteBatch` (and any sampler) samples with the ordinary top-down V (source-rect V0 at texel row 0), so RenderTarget2D content sampled back is **vertically mirrored**. An ordinary (SetData-uploaded) `Texture2D` is top-down and unaffected; the backbuffer readback is unaffected because `ReadBackbuffer`'s `requestScreenShot` reports `_yflip=1` and already row-flips the backbuffer's own bottom-up storage. bgfx-Vulkan/D3D/Metal (`originBottomLeft=false`) store the attachment top-down, so no flip — matching every other CNA backend's public XNA top-left orientation.

**Why it looked size-dependent (Phase 24 — the false trigger explained).** Three compounding artifacts, none of them size:
1. **Y-blind / position-only test content.** Every prior Bgfx RT pixel test used content that cannot observe a vertical mirror: solid fills, a diagonal-AA *presence* check (`bgfx_rendertarget2d_msaa_test` scans a row for intermediate pixels — no Y position), or a **uniform** viewport/scissor rectangle whose *position* is self-consistent (GFX-063/066). `setViewRect`/`setScissor` and the sample use the same bottom-up FBO memory space, so a uniform rect's numeric position round-trips "correctly" even though the geometry orientation within is mirrored.
2. **bgfx first-read-per-frame screenshot latency.** The very first `GetBackBufferData` per rendered content reads a transient (the second read is stable). Different sizes needed different retry counts, which made the flaky partial observations look size-correlated.
3. **Retry-until-upright loops.** GFX-063's `renderRTAndReadFrame` `break`s the moment the inside pixel is the expected colour — i.e. it loops *until it finds an upright frame*, so it passes even when steady-state is mirrored. A fixed-cycle read takes whatever parity it lands on.

**Stage isolation (Phases 4/5/6/18 — decisive, both renderers).** A dedicated four-quadrant harness with env-gated backend instrumentation (a temporary `ReadRenderTargetColorDirectEXT` reading the FBO color texture via `bgfx::blit`→`BGFX_TEXTURE_READ_BACK`→`bgfx::readTexture`, and a `ReadBackbuffer` caps/yflip dump — both removed after root-cause):

| Path | bgfx-OpenGL | bgfx-Vulkan |
|---|---|---|
| Backbuffer direct render (no RT), read back | UPRIGHT | UPRIGHT |
| Ordinary `Texture2D` (SetData, top-down), SpriteBatch-sampled | UPRIGHT (all sizes) | UPRIGHT |
| **RT color MEMORY** (direct `readTexture`, no SpriteBatch) | **VFLIP** | UPRIGHT |
| RT **SpriteBatch-sampled** to backbuffer | **VFLIP** | UPRIGHT |

`RTmem == RTsampled` in both renderers ⇒ the SpriteBatch sample is a faithful pass-through and the mirror lives in the **FBO memory itself** (render-into-FBO stores bottom-up on GL). The backbuffer-direct and ordinary-Texture2D controls being upright pinpoints the defect to **render-target-backed sources on `originBottomLeft` renderers**, not the readback and not generic sampling/UV. Order/parity (Phases 15/16): `A,A,A,A` / `A,B,A,B` / safe-problem-safe / 10 back-to-back single cycles were all steady-state VFLIP on GL (upright on Vulkan) — **not** order- or size-dependent once past the first-read latency.

**Fix (Phase 25 — narrowest correct, semantic not size-based).** `include/.../BgfxGraphicsBackend.hpp` + `src/.../BgfxGraphicsBackend.cpp` only. Added `IBgfxSamplable::IsRenderTargetColorSource()` (default `false`; `BgfxRenderTargetBackend` overrides `true`). `BgfxSpriteBatchBackend::Draw` reads it off the already-`dynamic_cast<IBgfxSamplable*>`ed source and threads it into `SubmitSprite`, which — after the `SpriteEffects::FlipVertically` swap, so the two compose (a user FlipVertically on an RT still flips) — does `std::swap(v1, v2)` **iff `sourceIsRenderTarget && bgfx::getCaps()->originBottomLeft`**. Byte-identical for ordinary textures (flag false), for every backbuffer sprite, and for **all** sources on Vulkan/D3D/Metal (`originBottomLeft` false). This is the same compensation EasyGL applies for its GL-bottom-left FBOs, done at the sample. **Not** a render-stage projection flip: that would also invert triangle winding (culling) for all 3D-into-RT draws and move the (correctly-placed) `setViewRect` viewport content — GFX-063/066 must stay green, and a sample-stage flip keeps them green while making the steady-state XNA-correct.

**SpriteBatch vs generic sampling (Phase 27).** Scoped to `SpriteBatch` deliberately: it is the **only working RT-sample consumer** on Bgfx. The generic 3D-effect texture path binds every sampler slot via `static_cast<const BgfxTextureBackend&>(*params.textureN)` — **UB for a `RenderTarget2D`** (a `BgfxRenderTargetBackend` is an unrelated sibling; reads the wrong pooled handle). So a RenderTarget2D set as a `BasicEffect`/etc. texture cannot be sampled correctly at all today — a distinct pre-existing cast-safety defect (Task 873's shape, never fixed for the 3D path). Recorded as **GFX-078**, not fixed here.

**Tests.** New `examples/bgfx_rendertarget_orientation_test.cpp` (`Bgfx_RenderTarget_Orientation`, `cmake/Tests/BgfxTests.cmake`), same proven RT-sample→blit→`GetBackBufferData` path as `bgfx_rendertarget_viewport_test`. Four-quadrant pattern that DOES observe vertical/horizontal/180 mirrors. **72 assertions**: (A) size-independence — 7 sizes incl. the historically "flipped" 48×32/40×48/64×56 and "upright" 64×48, plus 32×32/56×40/48×56 — each asserts TL=RED/TR=GREEN/BL=BLUE/BR=YELLOW **and** a top-band-is-R|G / bottom-band-is-B|Y vertical guard; (B) ordinary-`Texture2D` control (must stay upright — the fix must not flip ordinary textures); (C) **multiple RTs sampled within one frame sequence** (A,B,A,B — the exact scenario earlier RT tests routed around as GFX-067 "contamination"). Pre-fix the four-quadrant matrix was VFLIP on bgfx-OpenGL; **post-fix 72/72** on bgfx-OpenGL (deterministic ×3) AND bgfx-Vulkan (×3).

**Regression (Phase 31).** Full `ctest -R '^Bgfx_'` on bgfx-OpenGL (Xvfb :99): **119/121** — the only 2 failures are the documented pre-existing environment/known-finding cases, **confirmed unrelated to this change**: `Bgfx_RenderTarget2D_MsaaResolve` (registered `CNA_BGFX_RENDERER=VULKAN`, falls back to GL 2.1 under Xvfb where MSAA-resolve doesn't average — **passes 2/2 on real Vulkan :0**) and `Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_DepthFormat` (the pre-existing **Task 952** depth-on-cube-RT-face open finding; reads the cube back *directly* via `GetBackBufferData`, never touches `SubmitSprite`). GFX-063 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Viewport` 10/10 and GFX-066 `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor` 13/13 stay green on **both** renderers. GFX-005/006/007/008 (`Bgfx_BasicEffect_*`/`Bgfx_SkinnedEffect_*`/`Bgfx_EnvironmentMapEffect_*`) families green. All `Bgfx_SpriteBatch_*`/`Bgfx_SpriteEffects_Flip`/`Bgfx_SpriteFont_*` green (ordinary-texture sprites are byte-identical — flag false).

**Generated shaders.** None — zero `.sc`/`bgfx_shaders.hpp` diff (pure CPU texture-coordinate handling in `SubmitSprite`).

**Sanitizers.** Not warranted — the change is a conditional `std::swap` of two floats already computed; no new allocation, indexing, lifetime or arithmetic-UB surface (Phase: sanitizers optional unless lifetime/OOB, which this is not).

**RenderTargetCube (Phase 22).** Not modified. `SpriteBatch` cannot sample a cube; RenderTargetCube faces are consumed by the env-map 3D path via a reflection **direction** vector (not a 2D sprite V), whose orientation convention is separate and whose tests (GFX-007 env-map) pass. A per-face cube-attachment orientation on `originBottomLeft` renderers is a distinct open question, not this defect and not exercised by the sprite path; left untouched.

| Affected files | `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/Bgfx/BgfxGraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/Bgfx/BgfxGraphicsBackend.cpp`, `examples/bgfx_rendertarget_orientation_test.cpp`, `cmake/Tests/BgfxTests.cmake` |
| Backends / Platforms | Bgfx / originBottomLeft renderers (OpenGL/GLES/WebGL); no-op on Vulkan/D3D/Metal |
| New findings | **GFX-078** — Bgfx generic 3D-effect texture binding uses `static_cast<const BgfxTextureBackend&>` on every sampler slot (texture0/1, PBR maps, dual-texture, env-map 2D); UB for a `RenderTarget2D` source (the ONLY working RT-sample consumer on Bgfx is `SpriteBatch`). Same class as Task 873/907, never fixed for the 3D 2D-texture path. Source-identified, NOT fixed. |

### REMED-GFX-078 — Bgfx: generic 3D-effect texture binding static_cast is UB for RenderTarget2D sources — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | MEDIUM / P2 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (bgfx-OpenGL 2.1, Xvfb :99; bgfx-Vulkan, real GPU :0)** |
| Commits | test `c1c735cc`, fix `9ec687bf`, docs (this entry) |

**Root cause.** The Bgfx 3D-effect dispatch (`BindPbrTextures` + the `DrawPrimitivesEx`/`DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx` per-effect branches) bound **every** sampler slot with `static_cast<const BgfxTextureBackend&>(*params.textureN)` and read `.textureHandle` — **27 cast sites**: texture0 (18), the dual-texture second layer texture1 (4), and the 5 PBR maps (normal/metallic-roughness/emissive/occlusion + base). `IRenderTargetBackend : public ITextureBackend`, so a `RenderTarget2D` **is-a** `ITextureBackend` (legal to pass), but its backend object is a `BgfxRenderTargetBackend` — an **unrelated sibling** of `BgfxTextureBackend`, not a base/derived of it (its color handle is `colorTex`; it has **no** `textureHandle` member). Downcasting it to `BgfxTextureBackend&` is therefore C++ **undefined behaviour**, reading `.textureHandle` out of the wrong sibling's layout (the `fbo`/`colorTex` bytes). Identical bug class to Task 873 (fixed for `SpriteBatch` via `IBgfxSamplable`) and Task 907 (cube env-map via `IBgfxCubeSamplable`) — never fixed for the 3D **2D-texture** path, so `SpriteBatch` was the ONLY working RT-sample consumer on Bgfx (why GFX-067's fix is scoped there).

**Public/backend type matrix.**

| Public resource | Bgfx backend | valid as 2D sampler? | old cast | new path | safe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Texture2D` | `BgfxTextureBackend : ITextureBackend, IBgfxSamplable` | yes | `static_cast<BgfxTextureBackend&>` | `IBgfxSamplable::GetBgfxTextureHandle()` (returns `textureHandle`) | now safe (was already correct value, UB-free) |
| `RenderTarget2D` | `BgfxRenderTargetBackend : IRenderTargetBackend→ITextureBackend, IBgfxSamplable` | yes | `static_cast<BgfxTextureBackend&>` → **UB** | `IBgfxSamplable::GetBgfxTextureHandle()` (returns `colorTex`) + `IsRenderTargetColorSource()`=true | now safe |
| `TextureCube` | `BgfxTextureCubeBackend : ITextureCubeBackend, IBgfxCubeSamplable` | cube only | (already) `IBgfxCubeSamplable` | unchanged | safe (Task 907) |
| `RenderTargetCube` | `BgfxRenderTargetCubeBackend : IRenderTargetCubeBackend, IBgfxCubeSamplable` | cube only | (already) `IBgfxCubeSamplable` | unchanged | safe (Task 907) |

**UB evidence (Phase 27).** A self-contained repro mirroring the exact sibling hierarchy (`ITextureBackend`/`IRenderTargetBackend : ITextureBackend`/`IBgfxSamplable`; `BgfxTextureBackend` vs `BgfxRenderTargetBackend`), compiled `-fsanitize=undefined -fsanitize=vptr -fno-sanitize-recover=all`, on the `static_cast<const BgfxTextureBackend&>` of a real `BgfxRenderTargetBackend` reports: *"member access within address … which does not point to an object of type 'BgfxTextureBackend'; note: object is of type 'BgfxRenderTargetBackend'"* — the dump shows the `fbo`/`colorTex` bytes being read as `textureHandle`. (A full bgfx UBSan variant was not built — the CLAUDE.md's documented 400–900 MB expensive-sanitizer case — because the vptr diagnosis on the exact cast shape plus the runtime repro below are already decisive.)

**Runtime reproduction (Phases 4–7, both renderers).** New `Bgfx_RenderTarget_EffectTexture` (`examples/bgfx_rendertarget_effect_texture_test.cpp`): render a four-quadrant pattern (TL=RED TR=GREEN BL=BLUE BR=YELLOW) into an RT, unbind, then sample it through a full-screen textured quad with the standard XNA UV map (NDC top-left → UV(0,0)) via BasicEffect and DualTextureEffect, read the backbuffer, classify the four quadrants by hue.

| State (bgfx-OpenGL :99) | RT-through-effect | ordinary Texture2D control |
|---|---|---|
| **pre-fix** (UB cast) | **13/32** — every RT quadrant = OTHER (garbage: wrong pooled handle) | upright (PASS) |
| **cast-only** (handle fixed, no shader flip) | RT = clean **VERTICAL MIRROR** (TL=BLUE, BL=RED) | upright (PASS) |
| **full fix** | **32/32** upright | upright (PASS) |

The three-way split isolates the two independent defects cleanly: the UB (garbage → correct-but-mirrored once the handle is right) and the originBottomLeft orientation (mirrored → upright once the shader flip is applied). bgfx-Vulkan is **32/32** at every stage that builds — `originBottomLeft=false` keeps the per-slot flip flag at 0, so an unconditional flip would fail there (it does not).

**Fix (backend-local, no XNA API change).** `BgfxGraphicsBackend.hpp`/`.cpp` + the 10 2D-sampling fragment shaders + regenerated `bgfx_shaders.hpp`.
- **Cast safety.** New `BindSamplerSlot(slot, sampler, texture, fallback)` resolves the handle through `dynamic_cast<const IBgfxSamplable*>` (exactly as `SpriteBatch::Draw` does), falls back to the slot's "map absent" default when null, and binds it — replacing all **27** `static_cast` sites (`BindPbrTextures` collapses to 5 calls; the 18 slot-0 and 4 slot-1 blocks collapse to one call each via identical replacement). `grep` confirms **zero** remaining `static_cast<…BgfxTextureBackend…>` in the sampler paths.
- **Orientation.** The generic path receives mesh UVs (not SpriteBatch-generated UVs), so GFX-067's bottom-up-FBO compensation is applied **in-shader**. `BindSamplerSlot` records a render-target color source (`IsRenderTargetColorSource()`) for slots 0–3 into `rtFlipV_` **only when `bgfx::getCaps()->originBottomLeft`**; `SubmitViewProgram` uploads `u_rtFlipV` before each 3D submit and clears it after. Each 2D-sampling fragment shader flips V per slot: `mix(v, 1-v, u_rtFlipV.<slot>)`. `flip==0` (ordinary textures; every slot on Vulkan/D3D/Metal) yields the input V exactly, so ordinary-Texture2D output is byte-identical on all renderers.
- **Per-slot (Phase 12/24).** `fs_dual_texture3d` flips slot 0 via `.x` and slot 1 via `.y` **independently** — the two-slot discriminator (Tex2D+RT, RT+Tex2D, both patterned) is 32/32, so a single global "flip all UVs" flag is ruled out. PBR (`fs_pbr3d`) flips base/normal/MR/emissive via `.x/.y/.z/.w`; **occlusion (slot 4) is outside the vec4** and left un-V-compensated — a live `RenderTarget2D` as a PBR occlusion map is not a real material, and its bind is still made type-safe (no UB). This is the one documented residual, not a new finding.

**Effect/sampler inventory (Phase 2/13/26).** 2D sampler slots, all now via `BindSamplerSlot`: textured / colored-textured / lit-textured (per-pixel + vertex-lit) / skinned (per-pixel + vertex-lit) / alpha-test (+ colored) / dual-texture (2 slots) / env-map 2D base / PBR (5 slots). Cube slots (`params.envMap`) unchanged — already `IBgfxCubeSamplable`. `fs_colored3d`/`fs_instanced3d` sample no texture (untouched).

**Generated shaders (Phase 22/32).** No-change regeneration proven byte-identical first (same shaderc 1.19.150 that produced the checked-in header). After the edits, **exactly 40 arrays changed** = the 10 modified fragment shaders × 4 profiles (`glsl`/`essl`/`spirv`/`wgsl`); every vertex shader, `fs_colored3d`, and `fs_instanced3d` array is **byte-identical**. No generated data hand-edited.

**RenderTargetCube (Phase 18).** Classified **SAFE** — the cube env-map sampler already binds via `dynamic_cast<const IBgfxCubeSamplable*>(params.envMap)->GetBgfxCubeTextureHandle()` (Task 907), so a `RenderTargetCube` in a `TextureCube` slot is type-safe. Cube-face sampling orientation on originBottomLeft is a **separate** open question (a reflection **direction**, not a 2D V — already noted in GFX-067 Phase 22), not this defect and not the 2D static_cast root cause. No new finding.

**Regression (Phase 31).** Full `ctest -R '^Bgfx_'` on bgfx-OpenGL (:99, -j2): **120/122** — the only 2 failures are the documented pre-existing environment/known cases, **confirmed identical on the pristine tree**: `Bgfx_RenderTarget2D_MsaaResolve` (registered VULKAN, GL2.1-fallback MSAA under Xvfb) and `Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_DepthFormat` (Task 952). `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Orientation` (GFX-067), `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Viewport` (GFX-063), `Bgfx_RenderTarget_Scissor` (GFX-066), `Bgfx_SpriteBatch_CustomViewport` (GFX-072), and every BasicEffect/SkinnedEffect/EnvironmentMapEffect/DualTextureEffect/PBR/SpriteBatch family pass. On bgfx-Vulkan (:0) the GFX-078 test + GFX-067/063/066 + effect combined tests pass; one pre-existing bgfx-Vulkan-only discrepancy (`Bgfx_SkinnedEffect_Combined`, byte-identical values on the pristine tree — unrelated to this change) remains open.

**Sanitizers.** UB proven by `-fsanitize=vptr` on the isolated cast shape (above). No new allocation/indexing/lifetime surface introduced (the fix is a `dynamic_cast` + a conditional float write + one uniform upload).

| Affected files | `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/Bgfx/BgfxGraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/Bgfx/BgfxGraphicsBackend.cpp`, `fs_{textured3d,colored_textured3d,alpha_test3d,lit_textured3d,lit_textured3d_vertexlit,skinned3d,skinned3d_vertexlit,dual_texture3d,env_map3d,pbr3d}.sc`, `bgfx_shaders.hpp`, `examples/bgfx_rendertarget_effect_texture_test.cpp`, `cmake/Tests/BgfxTests.cmake` |

### REMED-GFX-064 — SdlGpu + D3D12: `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` wired to the GPU — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | MEDIUM / P2 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (both backends; SdlGpu runtime, D3D12 off-screen runtime under Wine+vkd3d-proton)** |
| Commits | SdlGpu test `dce6e9d2`, SdlGpu fix `4689cfcb`, D3D12 test `52908242`, D3D12 fix `963fbf23`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause (both) | Neither backend overrode the **no-op** base `IGraphicsBackend::SetViewport(...)` (`IGraphicsBackend.hpp:687`, empty `{}`). **SdlGpu** never called `SDL_SetGPUViewport` anywhere; **D3D12** hardcoded `D3D12_VIEWPORT{0,0,boundColorWidth_,boundColorHeight_,0,1}` at all four `RSSetViewports` sites plus the SpriteBatch flush. A custom `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` was a total no-op on **both** — backbuffer **and** RT — broader than GFX-062 (Vulkan RT-only). Hypothesis CONFIRMED for both; **not** the same root cause internally (see below), so treated as two independent slices under one ID. |

**The two backends needed DIFFERENT solutions (verified, not assumed — task Phase 5 caution honored).**

**SdlGpu — deferred, same shape as Vulkan GFX-062 → per-draw capture.** SdlGpu queues every draw (`drawOrder_`) and replays it at `Present()` inside a per-target render pass; `GraphicsDevice::SetRenderTarget` resets the frame-global `Viewport` to the target's full size on bind **and** unbind (`ResetViewportAndScissorForRenderTarget`). So a per-pass read of the live viewport (which is exactly how the existing SdlGpu scissor works) would apply the post-unbind full-**backbuffer** viewport to the RT pass. Fixed by capturing the viewport **per draw** at enqueue:
1. `SetViewport()` stores `viewportSet_/X_/Y_/W_/H_/minDepth/maxDepth` (store-only, never read back at set time).
2. `QueuedDrawRef` carries a viewport snapshot; new `PushDrawOrder()` (replacing all **9** raw `drawOrder_.push_back({Kind,idx})` sites — the 8 3D families + sprite) tags each queued draw with the live viewport.
3. `RenderQueuedDraws()` applies `SDL_SetGPUViewport` **per draw** via new `ApplyViewportForRef()`: the ref's captured sub-region if set (unclamped rect — a transform not a clip; top-left `y`, no extra flip since the sprite/3D shaders already handle SDL clip-space Y; depth clamped `[0,1]`), else the pass's full render-target extents (byte-identical to pre-fix = SDL's own default full-target viewport).

**D3D12 — immediate-per-draw → store + consume (NOT D3D11-copy, NOT capture/replay).** Every D3D12 draw re-records its own command list (`Reset`→record→`Close`→`ExecuteCommandListAndWaitEXT`), so there is no persistent context to `RSSetViewports` into at `SetViewport` time (D3D11's model) and no deferral needing capture/replay (Vulkan/SdlGpu's model). Fixed by:
1. `SetViewport()` stores the rect + depth range.
2. New `GetEffectiveViewportEXT()` returns the stored custom viewport if set (unclamped rect, top-left `TopLeftY`, depth clamped `[0,1]`), else the full bound-target rect (byte-identical to the old hardcode). Read at all four backend `RSSetViewports` sites (`DrawColoredPrimitives`, `DrawIndexedColoredPrimitives`, `DrawPrimitivesExImpl`, `DrawInstancedPrimitivesEx`) and the `D3D12SpriteBatch` flush (via `owner_`).
3. Target-change resets the stored viewport (`viewportSet_=false`) in `BindOffscreenColorTargetEXT`/`UnbindOffscreenColorTargetEXT` (covering MRT-bind + backbuffer-restore, which delegate through them) — mirrors XNA's `SetRenderTarget` reset (also driven by GraphicsDevice) and prevents a stale viewport leaking across targets in backend-direct callers.

**MinDepth/MaxDepth (Phase 16).** Inseparable from the fix on both backends: the stored viewport carries `minDepth/maxDepth`, clamped to `[0,1]` (SDL_GPUViewport / D3D12_VIEWPORT valid domain, = XNA's own valid range), and feeds the same viewport struct — so honoring the viewport necessarily honors its depth range. Both APIs expose a real configurable depth range (unlike some backends), so no deviation to record. Not separately depth-probed (a depth-range pixel test needs a depth buffer + Z-specific draw; same scope call as GFX-062), but wired and carried through — verified by code, matching the GFX-062 precedent.

**SpriteBatch (Phases 6/7).** The GPU viewport **rectangle** is now honored for sprite draws on both backends (SdlGpu sprite draws go through the same per-draw `ApplyViewportForRef`; D3D12 sprite flush reads `GetEffectiveViewportEXT`). The sprite **projection** `ViewportSize` uniform (used for the pixel→NDC ortho transform) is deliberately left at the full-target/virtual-resolution size on both — changing it to the viewport's W/H (which FNA `SpriteEffect.OnApply` and D3D11's `RSGetViewports`-readback both do) is a separate cross-backend sprite-projection parity nuance, byte-identical when no custom viewport is set, and out of scope for the GPU-viewport-rectangle wiring this task is about. Recorded here honestly; not a regression (existing sprite tests never set a custom viewport).

**Tests.**
- **SdlGpu** — new `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_viewport_test.cpp` (`SdlGpu_RenderTargetViewport`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake`). Asymmetric 80×60 `RenderTarget2D`, read back via `RenderTarget2D::GetData` (SdlGpu can't download the swapchain — SDLGPU-39). 3 frames / **14** checks: custom sub-region viewport (13,9,31,23) 5-way probe; full-viewport control; **two viewports in one frame** (the per-draw-capture crux — RED into A, GREEN into B, unbind, read; a per-pass read would leave the whole target GREEN).
- **D3D12** — new Check VP in `examples/d3d12_smoke_test.cpp` (the off-screen, plain-Wine-safe CTest). Asymmetric 80×60 off-screen RT via `BindOffscreenColorTargetEXT`, read back via the `ReadBackRenderTargetFull` READBACK-buffer technique. **11** checks: custom sub-region (5-way probe), full-viewport control, two viewports/two draws into one target.

**Pre-fix vs post-fix (runtime).** SdlGpu `SdlGpu_RenderTargetViewport` **7/14 → 14/14** (llvmpipe/Vulkan, Xvfb :99): pre-fix the custom viewport was fully ignored (all outside probes RED) and the two-viewport frame was entirely GREEN (last full-size draw wins). D3D12 Check VP **4/11 → 11/11** (Wine+vkd3d-proton, off-screen): identical failure signature pre-fix.

**Backbuffer (Phase 4).** SdlGpu backbuffer readback is blocked (SDLGPU-39) so the SdlGpu viewport is proven on an RT pass (which exercises the identical per-draw `ApplyViewportForRef` code path as the backbuffer pass). D3D12 has no windowed backbuffer under Wine (REMED-BUILD-012), so its viewport is proven on the off-screen target (identical `GetEffectiveViewportEXT` path as every draw). Both fixes are pass/target-agnostic by construction — the same code services backbuffer and RT.

**Regression.** SdlGpu full shard **28/28** (incl. RT/RTCube/MRT/sprite/orientation/scissor/effects — zero regressions). D3D12 `d3d12_smoke_test` **220/231**: the 11 FAILs (N3c/N5/O4/P4/Q4/S1/S2/S4/S5/U4/V2 — all DX-137 fog / DX-135 skinned) are **pre-existing and identical with the changes stashed** (measured both ways) — **zero regressions**; my change has no causal path to fog blending or bone skinning.

**Validation (Phase 10).** SdlGpu runs on SDL_gpu's Vulkan driver with debug mode enabled (`SDL_CreateGPUDevice` debug_mode); the new `SDL_SetGPUViewport` calls use non-negative, in-bounds-or-full-target rects (degenerate → full-target fallback) and produced no new validation output across the 28-test shard. REMED-GFX-059 (VUID-…-02684) is a separate, pre-existing SdlGpu item, not touched.

**Generated shaders.** None — zero `.glsl/.vert/.frag/.spv/.hlsl/.wgsl/.dxbc/bytecode` diff across all four commits (pure command/state handling; Viewport is rasterizer/command state).

**Sanitizers.** New arithmetic is float casts + `std::clamp(minDepth/maxDepth, 0, 1)` and a `w>0 && h>0` guard; degenerate/unset viewports fall back to the full target, so no negative/zero-extent viewport reaches SDL or D3D12. No new bounds arithmetic warranting a dedicated UBSan build (same reasoning as GFX-062).

**Cross-backend parity (Phase 19).** After GFX-062 (Vulkan) + GFX-063 (Bgfx) + this (SdlGpu, D3D12), all backends now honor a custom `GraphicsDevice.Viewport` in RT passes; EasyGL/D3D11/D3D9 already did (immediate), WebGPU per-pass. SdlGpu compared runtime directly (14/14); D3D12 compared at runtime off-screen (11/11) — the real-window path stays BUILD-012-blocked but the off-screen path executes the identical viewport code.

**New findings.** **GFX-068** (SdlGpu per-pass scissor reset-to-full-backbuffer on RT unbind) — surfaced when the viewport∩scissor frame could not isolate the intersection on SdlGpu (GetData requires unbind; unbind resets the per-pass scissor). Independent of the viewport wiring (scissor, per-pass vs per-draw), recorded below, not fixed. The viewport∩scissor **independence** itself is already proven on Vulkan (GFX-062 Frame 3), where both states are per-draw.

| Affected files | `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/SdlGpu/SdlGpuGraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/SdlGpu/SdlGpuGraphicsBackend.cpp`, `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_viewport_test.cpp`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake`, `include/CNA/Internal/Backends/D3D12/D3D12GraphicsBackend.hpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/D3D12/D3D12GraphicsBackend.cpp`, `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/D3D12/D3D12SpriteBatch.cpp`, `examples/d3d12_smoke_test.cpp` |
| Backends / Platforms | SdlGpu, D3D12 / ALL |

### REMED-GFX-068 — SdlGpu: `ScissorRectangle` now captured & replayed PER DRAW (per-pass reset-to-backbuffer on RT unbind) — DONE and VERIFIED

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Sev / Pri / Owner / Status | LOW / P3 / GRAPHICS / **DONE and VERIFIED (SdlGpu runtime, Xvfb :99, llvmpipe/Vulkan debug mode)** |
| Commits | test `38ffda25`, fix `9e65ac4e`, docs (this entry) |
| Root cause | SdlGpu applied `ScissorRectangle` **once per pass** from the live member state at `Present()` time (`ApplyScissorForPass(pass, targetW, targetH)`, gated on `scissorEnabled_`), unlike the **per-draw** viewport GFX-064 wired. In this deferred backend every draw is queued (`drawOrder_`) and replayed at Present in a per-target pass; a game that sets a scissor while a RenderTarget2D is bound and then unbinds it triggers `GraphicsDevice::ResetViewportAndScissorForRenderTarget` → `setScissorRectangleProperty(0,0,backbufferW,backbufferH)` — so by the time the RT pass replays, the live scissor rect is the full **backbuffer** (larger than the RT) and the scissor no longer clips. Exact deferred-model shape of Vulkan GFX-013 (scissor) and SdlGpu GFX-064 (viewport). |

**The fix (mirrors GFX-064's per-draw viewport capture).**
1. `QueuedDrawRef` carries a scissor snapshot (`scissorEnabled` + `scissorX/Y/W/H`), alongside the GFX-064 viewport snapshot.
2. `PushDrawOrder()` (the single centralized append point GFX-064 established across the 9 `drawOrder_.push_back` sites — 8 3D families + sprite) captures the live `scissorEnabled_` (from `ApplyRasterizerState`'s `ScissorTestEnable`) and `scissorX_/Y_/W_/H_` (from `SetScissorRect`) into each queued draw.
3. `RenderQueuedDraws()` applies `SDL_SetGPUScissor` **per draw** via new `ApplyScissorForRef()`, immediately after the existing `ApplyViewportForRef()` — so each draw honors the scissor it was enqueued under. The 3 per-pass `ApplyScissorForPass()` calls (swapchain / RenderToTarget / RenderToTargetCubeFace) are removed; SDL sets a default full-target scissor at pass begin which each draw then overrides.
4. `ApplyScissorForRef()` clamps the captured rect to the target's **physical extent** in int64 (a scissor is a **clip**, unlike the viewport's NDC→framebuffer transform which is passed unclamped) — offset ≥ 0, offset+extent within the target, no overflow — mirroring `VulkanGraphicsBackend::computeScissor` (GFX-013). `scissorEnabled=false` or a zero-size rect ⇒ full target (no clip), matching `RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable=false`.

**SDL GPU scissor API semantics (Phase 7/8).** `SDL_SetGPUScissor(render_pass, SDL_Rect*)` sets per-command-buffer scissor state that persists until changed — exactly like `SDL_SetGPUViewport` (so scissor *does* have a per-draw equivalent; the old header comment claiming it did not was wrong and is corrected). `SDL_BeginGPURenderPass` "automatically sets a default viewport and scissor" = the full target, so an unset/disabled scissor needs no explicit call. There is no separate "disable scissor" call — a disabled scissor is represented by the full-target rect.

**Coordinate / Y semantics (Phase 9).** `SDL_Rect` is top-left origin, matching XNA `ScissorRectangle` directly — **no Y-flip** (same as Vulkan `VkRect2D`, GFX-013; SDL_gpu normalizes framebuffer orientation across its Vulkan/Metal/D3D12 drivers). The test's asymmetric above/below probes (y=3 vs y=30 around a y[8,21) scissor) prove orientation.

**Physical target extent (Phase 10).** `ApplyScissorForRef` clamps to the pass's own render-target extents (`target.rt->width/height`, `cube->size`, or `physicalWidth_/Height_` for the swapchain) — never the backbuffer size while an RT is bound, never the viewport size. The test's 64×48 RT ≠ 96×72 backbuffer catches any dimension leak.

**Viewport interaction (Phase 11).** Both dynamic states are now per-draw and independent. Frame 3 uses non-coincident Viewport `(8,6,40,30)` and Scissor `(20,4,30,20)`: the visible region is exactly the intersection — a scissor-clipped-but-in-viewport probe and a viewport-clipped-but-in-scissor probe are both BLACK, the intersection interior RED.

**SpriteBatch vs 3D (Phase 12).** Covered by construction: `ApplyScissorForRef` runs for **every** `QueuedDrawRef` before the draw-kind switch, so all 8 3D families **and** the `Sprite` kind (which enqueues via the same `PushDrawOrder(DrawKind::Sprite,…)`) get the identical per-draw scissor — the same single code path GFX-064's viewport uses. The new test exercises the 3D path; the passing `SdlGpu_2D`/`SdlGpu_RenderState` shard exercises sprites through the same replay loop.

**Render-target types (Phase 13).** RenderTarget2D, RenderTargetCube, and MRT share the one `RenderQueuedDraws` replay path (each begins a pass then calls it), so the single `ApplyScissorForRef` change services all three. The regression targets RenderTarget2D directly; Cube/MRT are covered by construction + the passing `SdlGpu_RenderTargetCube`/`SdlGpu_MRT` shard.

**Backbuffer (Phase 14).** The swapchain pass uses the identical per-draw `ApplyScissorForRef` path (SdlGpu can't read the swapchain back — SDLGPU-39 — so it's proven on the RT pass, byte-identical code). Frame 1's scissor-OFF control guards against the fix over-applying a stored rect when `ScissorTestEnable=false`.

| Test | `examples/sdlgpu_rendertarget_scissor_test.cpp` (`SdlGpu_RenderTargetScissor`, `cmake/Tests/SdlGpuTests.cmake`). Asymmetric 64×48 `RenderTarget2D` (≠ 96×72 backbuffer), read back via `RenderTarget2D::GetData` **after unbind** (the realistic case the pre-existing `SdlGpu_RenderState` Check F structurally avoided by reading *before* unbind). 4 frames / **17** checks: F0 scissor ON 5-way probe; F1 scissor OFF control; F2 three scissor states in one pass (disabled-BLUE background + scissor-A-RED + scissor-B-GREEN — the per-draw-capture crux); F3 Viewport∩Scissor intersection. |
| Pre-fix vs post-fix (runtime) | **9/17 → 17/17.** Pre-fix: F0 left/right/above/below RED not BLACK (scissor inert on the RT after unbind); F2 entirely GREEN (all three draws share the post-unbind full-backbuffer scissor, last full draw wins); F3 scissor-clip probe RED not BLACK. Post-fix all 17 pass, stable across repeated runs. |
| Validation (Phase 18) | SdlGpu runs on SDL_gpu's Vulkan driver with `debug_mode`. Post-fix: **zero** validation errors across repeated runs of the new test (the clamped rects always satisfy the scissor VUIDs). REMED-GFX-059 (`VUID-vkCmdDraw-renderPass-02684`, depth-stencil attachment) is a separate pre-existing item — it appeared in the *pre-fix* run of this test but not post-fix; left classified separately, not touched. |
| Regression (Phase 19) | Full SdlGpu shard **29/29** (28 pre-existing + the new test): incl. `SdlGpu_RenderState` (scissor Check F, same path), `SdlGpu_RenderTargetViewport` (GFX-064), `SdlGpu_RenderTarget2D/Cube/MRT`, and the GFX-006 (`SdlGpu_SkinnedEffect_WorldNormal`) / GFX-007 (`SdlGpu_EnvMapEmissive`) / GFX-009 (`SdlGpu_*_Fog`) / GFX-010 (`SdlGpu_ViewSpace_Fog`) controls — zero regressions. |
| Cross-backend parity (Phase 20) | SdlGpu now honors RT scissor with identical XNA semantics to Vulkan (GFX-013, same 5-way probe + scissor-OFF control passes), Bgfx (GFX-066 NOT-A-DEFECT), EasyGL, D3D11. **Nuance:** GFX-013's assessment that "SdlGpu already honors RT scissor" was based on `SdlGpu_RenderState` Check F, which reads back *before* unbind and so structurally could not detect the deferred-replay-after-unbind bug; GFX-068 fixes the general (read-after-unbind, i.e. every real deferred-replay) case. |
| Generated shaders | None — zero `.glsl/.vert/.frag/.spv/.hlsl/.wgsl/.dxbc/bytecode` diff (pure command/state handling; scissor is rasterizer/command state). |
| Sanitizers | New arithmetic is the int64 clamp in `ApplyScissorForRef` (offset ≥ 0, offset+extent ≤ target, non-negative size — same shape as GFX-013's `computeScissor`, no negative/oversized rect reaches SDL) plus fixed-size POD snapshot fields (default-initialized in `QueuedDrawRef`). No new nontrivial arithmetic warranting a dedicated UBSan build (same reasoning as GFX-013/062/064). |
| New findings (Phase 21 sweep) | **GFX-069** — SdlGpu never applies `BlendState.BlendFactor` (the constant blend color): its pipeline maps `Blend.BlendFactor`(10)→`SDL_GPU_BLENDFACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR` and `InverseBlendFactor`(11)→`ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR`, but SdlGpu does **not** override the no-op base `SetBlendFactor` and never calls `SDL_SetGPUBlendConstants`, so constant-color blends use SDL's default (0,0,0,0). Blend-constant analog of GFX-064's "never overrode base `SetViewport`"; 6 other backends (Vulkan/EasyGL/Bgfx/D3D11/D3D9/WebGPU) implement it. When implemented it must be **per-draw captured** (same deferred-model reason as scissor/viewport/stencil-ref). Separable — recorded, NOT fixed. Stencil reference and blend equation/sampler state are already per-draw captured (not affected). |
