## REMED-GFX-176 — SDL_GPU Texture2D mip storage and upload (2026-07-31)

### The symptom, and the two things underneath it

REMED-GFX-175's contract fixture measured **SDL_GPU 55/87**, and the failing set was the tell: **all
nine ordinals** sampled level 0 at an exact 2x, 4x and 8x minification of a real four-level chain,
`LinearMipPoint`, `PointMipLinear` and the four `Min*Mag*` ordinals included. A filter fixture can
only ask which level the sampler chose. On this backend the honest answer was **the only one that
existed**, and no sampler change could have altered it — REMED-GFX-170 had already made the ordinal
table complete and correct here, which is why this was ticketed separately rather than absorbed.

**Mechanism 1 — ALLOCATION.** `SdlGpuTextureBackend`'s constructor set `createInfo.num_levels = 1`
as a literal and never read `ImageData::mipLevels`, the field `Texture2D`'s own constructor fills
from `CalculateMipLevels(w, h)`. A `mipMap=true` texture reported `LevelCount` 4 to the game and
owned a one-level GPU resource.

**Mechanism 2 — UPLOAD.** The class declared **no `UpdatePixelsLevel` override at all**, so it
inherited `ITextureBackend`'s default — an empty body. Every `SetData(level > 0, ...)` was accepted
by the shared layer, written into its CPU mip buffer, handed down and silently dropped. No error, no
warning, no pixel.

Both are measured, not inferred, by the new `CNA_SDLGPU_TEXTURE_TRACE`. Over the new fixture's run
against the unfixed backend: **77 native textures created, `nativeLevels=1` on every single one**
while `requestedLevels` ran up to 5, and **zero** `level>0` upload commands ever emitted. Post-fix
the same trace reads `nativeLevels == requestedLevels` on all 77 and **155** level>0 uploads.

**Mechanism 3 — CYCLE, which only became reachable once the first two were fixed, and which the new
fixture is what found.** The level-0 upload passed `cycle=true` to `SDL_UploadToGPUTexture`, whose
documented meaning is "swap to a fresh internal resource rather than stall on an in-flight read" —
and a fresh resource does not carry the levels this upload is not writing. Harmless for a one-level
texture; silently destructive for a chain. **A/B measured by retaining it:** the storage fixture
drops to **52/112** and GFX-175's fixture to **41/87 — BELOW the 55/87 this task started from.** A
fix that allocated the chain and uploaded the levels but kept `cycle=true` would have regressed the
backend while looking like progress on every storage check. `cycle` is now true only when
`levelCount_ == 1`, which keeps the ordinary `mipMap=false` path byte-identical, and false for a
chain — the same conclusion SDLGPU-40 reached on the cube path and REMED-GFX-135 on the volume path,
both already documented in this file for this exact reason.

This is why allocation and upload landed as **one** commit: allocating a chain while keeping the
old level-0-only upload leaves levels 1..N undefined and gives the sampler somewhere worse to go
than the single level it replaced. There is no useful intermediate state to bisect to.

### The fix

Both public entry points now share one `UploadLevel` path whose destination region, `mip_level`,
transfer size, row pitch and `pixels_per_row` all come from the **level's** dimensions rather than
the resource's, and which rejects a level whose supplied extent is not the one that level actually
has. A non-positive extent and a level count beyond what the dimensions can halve down to are both
rejected **before** `SDL_CreateGPUTexture` rather than surfacing as a device error or a silently
shortened chain.

**No mip generation was introduced.** `SDL_GenerateMipmapsForGPUTexture` is not called for a
`Texture2D` — construction allocates the declared levels and nothing but the caller writes them.
No CPU shadow, extra frame, `Present`, wait, retry or readback was added.

### Level count and dimension matrix

| dimensions | `mipMap=false` | `mipMap=true` levels | level extents |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x1  | 1 | 1 | 1x1 |
| 2x2  | 1 | 2 | 2x2, 1x1 |
| 4x4  | 1 | 3 | 4x4, 2x2, 1x1 |
| 8x8  | 1 | 4 | 8x8, 4x4, 2x2, 1x1 |
| 8x4  | 1 | 4 | 8x4, 4x2, 2x1, 1x1 |
| 16x2 | 1 | 5 | 16x2, 8x1, 4x1, 2x1, 1x1 |
| 3x2  | 1 | 2 | 3x2, 1x1 |
| 5x3  | 1 | 3 | 5x3, 2x1, 1x1 |
| 6x6  | 1 | 3 | 6x6, 3x3, 1x1 |
| 7x5  | 1 | 3 | 7x5, 3x2, 1x1 |

Public `LevelCount` and native `num_levels` now agree on every row, each axis clamps to at least
one, and every chain's final level is 1x1. No zero-dimensional level is ever created or uploaded.

### Results

**New `examples/sdlgpu_texture2d_mip_storage_test.cpp`, 112 checks over 11 legs: 45/112 -> 112/112.**
**REMED-GFX-175's own 87-check fixture: 55/87 -> 87/87**, joining the eight backends already there.

Per leg: A allocation over the matrix above plus a declared-but-unwritten chain; B every declared
level of every power-of-two chain read back **byte-exact** by rendering it at its own size under
Point, so content, orientation, row pitch and extent are asserted at once with no tolerance; C the
LOD ladder — Point selects each level exactly, Linear degenerates to one level at integer lambda and
blends only the two bracketing levels between them; D upload ordering (reverse, forward,
interleaved-with-rewrites, two concurrent chains, level 0 rewritten after the chain was complete);
E seven sub-rectangles of level 1 plus `startIndex` as a caller-array offset and four rejected
regions that leave the level untouched; F upload and sample in the same frame with no `Present`,
twice; G NPOT/odd/rectangular chains at every scale; H SpriteBatch, all three 3D submission routes,
and six stock textured families; I lifetime; J rejects and one-level completeness under all nine
ordinals; K the GetData boundary.

**Point selects exactly one level with no interpolation at every scale tested. Linear is byte-exact
at integer lambda and bounded to the two adjacent levels between them. All nine ordinals now run
against a real chain and REMED-GFX-170's table is unchanged.**

### GetData boundary

A plain `Texture2D`'s `GetData` is served by the shared layer's own CPU pixel shadow on **every**
backend and never reaches `ITextureBackend::GetData`, so it cannot witness GPU storage. It is stated
as leg K rather than left implied, and rendered sampling — not readback — is the content oracle
everywhere above. **No CPU shadow was added to make anything here pass.**

### Resource-type boundaries — Texture2D was the only one

Every other SDL_GPU resource class already passed a real level count and already had a level-aware
upload path, so none shares this root cause and none is absorbed:

| class | `num_levels` before this task | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `Texture2D` | hardcoded `1` | **the defect, fixed here** |
| `Texture3D` | `mipMap ? CalculateMipLevels : 1` | already correct, untouched |

| `RenderTargetCube` | `mipMap ? CalculateMipLevels : 1` | already correct, untouched |
| MSAA / depth attachments | `1` | correct — a resolve or depth target has no chain |

## REMED-GFX-173 — SDL_GPU EnvironmentMapEffect cube sampler (2026-07-31)

### The contract, and where it is read from

`EnvironmentMapEffect` samples **two** independently observable resources. The authoritative slot
mapping was read from source, not taken from the ticket:

* `src/CNA/Internal/Backends/SdlGpu/shaders/env_map3d.frag.glsl` declares
  `layout(set = 2, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D uTexture` and
  `layout(set = 2, binding = 1) uniform samplerCube uEnvMap`.
* `VulkanGraphicsBackend::GetOrCreateEnvMapDescSet`, corrected under REMED-GFX-169, writes
  `slotSamplers_[0]` into binding 0 and `slotSamplers_[1]` into binding 1.

So **`GraphicsDevice.SamplerStates[0]` filters `EnvironmentMapEffect.Texture` and
`SamplerStates[1]` filters `EnvironmentMapEffect.EnvironmentMap`.** An unset slot uses the
documented device default, `SamplerState::LinearWrap`.

### The defect: the ticket is right and names only half of it

**Mechanism 2, the half the ticket names.** `SdlGpuGraphicsBackend::IssueEnvMapDraw` bound

```cpp
samplerBindings[1].sampler = GetOrCreateSampler(/*textureFilter=*/0, /*addressU=*/1,
                                                /*addressV=*/1, kSpriteBatchMaxAnisotropy,
                                                "EnvironmentMap3D/cube");
```

— a literal LinearClamp — under a comment calling it "this project's other backends' fixed
reflection-map sampling convention".

**Mechanism 1, which it does not.** `QueueEnvMapDraw` captured only `samplerSlots_[0]`, so
`EnvMapDrawCommand` had **no field in which slot 1 could reach replay at all**.

Neither half alone is a fix, and that is why both are in one commit. Removing the constant without
adding the capture makes replay read *live* sampler state and breaks the deferred-snapshot contract
that legs E and F assert. Adding the capture without touching the binding changes nothing
observable. The comment was true when it was written and stopped being true under REMED-GFX-169.

### The oracle

The two slots are made **independently observable** rather than one being inferred from the other.
With `EnvironmentMapAmount = 1`, `FresnelFactor = 0` (which also clears `FresnelEnabled`, so `pow()`
never sees `0^0` at the quad centre), `EnvironmentMapSpecular = 0`, `DiffuseColor = White`,
`Alpha = 1` and an all-opaque base texture, the fragment shader's
`mix(baseColor, envSample.rgb * combinedAlpha, 1.0)` is **exactly** `envSample.rgb` — the base
texture cannot influence one bit. With `EnvironmentMapAmount = 0` and ambient-only white lighting it
is exactly `texColor.rgb` — the cube cannot influence one bit. Independence is therefore asserted as
**byte-identical versus byte-different images**, never as a tolerance.

Exactness comes from a generated palette in which every pair of entries is at least 20 apart in
L-inf and the midpoint of any two entries is at least 9 from *every* entry. **Both properties are
checked by the fixture itself (PAL2, PAL3), not assumed.** So "this pixel is a stored texel" and
"this pixel is an interpolation of two stored texels" are decidable byte-exactly, and a sampler
replaced by a constant shows up as a Point image full of colours stored in no texel at all.

The geometry keeps the cube magnified and face-stable without touching UVs or shaders. An
orthographic projection draws a screen-filling quad at `z = 0` while the view matrix places the eye
at `D = 4/3`, so `reflect(-E, N)` reduces to a direction proportional to `(x, y, D)` — linear in the
pixel coordinate and always +Z-major for `D > 1`. One 4x4 face therefore magnifies into a 4x4 grid
of blocks across the target. Tilting the vertex **normal** aims the same sweep at a different face.

### Results

`examples/envmap_cube_sampler_contract_test.cpp`, 104 checks over thirteen legs, A/B-measured by
narrowly restoring the two production files from `2a02548a`:

| | SDL_GPU |
|---|---|
| before | **62/104** (42 failures) |
| after | **104/104** |

Every pre-fix failure is a Point-mode check reporting the entire 1024-pixel image off-palette, and
`CNA_SDLGPU_SAMPLER_TRACE` names the cause exactly: **one** distinct native description for the cube
slot across **all 86** env-map bindings —
`family=EnvironmentMap3D/cube filter=0(Linear) mag=Linear min=Linear mip=Linear aniso=off/1.0
addrU=ClampToEdge addrV=ClampToEdge key=0x04010100` — against **three** for the base slot. After the
fix the cube slot expresses **twelve**, exactly the distinct sampler states the fixture uses.

### Filter ordinals 0..8 on the cube slot

All nine are driven and classified. The magnification partition is the one a one-level cube can
observe: ordinals **1, 4, 5, 6** magnify by Point and produce byte-exact stored texels; **0, 3, 7, 8**
magnify linearly and produce colours stored nowhere. Each group additionally agrees **byte-for-byte**
across its members, which is only possible when the minification and mipmap components really are
unobservable on a one-level texture. `TextureFilter::Anisotropic(2)` is asserted only for its
magnification class — its tap pattern is a per-GPU choice, the same boundary REMED-GFX-170 declared.
The public-to-native translation is REMED-GFX-170's `FillSdlGpuSamplerCreateInfo` and its
complete-description cache key; **no second table was introduced.**

### Mipmapped cube

`TextureCube` level-aware allocation and upload were **verified, not assumed**:
`SdlGpuTextureCubeBackend`'s constructor passes `num_levels = CalculateMipLevels(size, size)` and its
`SetData` writes `destination.mip_level = level` with `cycle=false`. REMED-GFX-176's boundary — that
`Texture2D` was the only affected class — holds.

A real six-level chain with one **flat marker per (face, level)** isolates the mipmap component:
inside a level the min filter has nothing to act on, so only the ordinal's mipmap half can change the
answer. Mip-Point ordinals (1, 3, 6, 8) read stored levels only and reach a level above 0; each
mip-Linear ordinal (0, 4, 5, 7) differs from the mip-Point answer and produces blends stored at no
level; a one-level cube minified identically still reads stored level-0 texels; and two aimed faces
select different markers, so levels are per-face.

**Declared:** the four mip-Linear ordinals are *not* required to agree byte-for-byte. Flat levels make
min/mag invisible *inside* a face, but a cube is filtered seamlessly *across* face edges where the
neighbouring face's own flat colour is a different value, so min/mag remain observable at the
boundary taps. That is a property of cube sampling, not of the sampler under test. Automatic mip
generation stayed out of scope.

### Address-mode boundary, classified honestly

A cube map is addressed by a direction, so U/V/W address modes are reachable only at face edges and a
driver with seamless cube filtering may render all three identically — which is exactly what happens
here: **Clamp vs Wrap and Clamp vs Mirror both differ in 0 pixels.** The fixture therefore asserts
only that no mode produces an off-palette or border fetch, including a reflection deliberately aimed
at a face boundary, and **invents no cube address-mode convention**. This is also why the
cache-distinctness legs vary the *filter* rather than the address mode.

### Cache and binding identity

A new env-gated `CNA_SDLGPU_ENVMAP_TRACE` prints the whole two-slot binding on one line at **both**
ends of the deferred pipeline — what the public draw call CAPTURED and what replay actually BOUND,
with both texture identities, both public slot states, both captured states and both native sampler
handles. `CNA_SDLGPU_SAMPLER_TRACE` reports one binding per line and cannot say which pair belonged
to the same draw.

Measured over the fixture's 86 env-map draws:

* the **same** cube texture under **12** distinct slot-1 descriptions receives **12** distinct native
  samplers;
* **no** native sampler serves two distinct slot-1 descriptions;
* of the **43** draws whose slot-0 and slot-1 descriptions differ, **none** shares one native sampler.

### Cardinality and performance

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| sampler applications (all families) | 178 | **178** |
| env-map bindings, base slot / cube slot | 86 / 86 | **86 / 86** |
| queued env-map draws / replayed | 86 / 86 | **86 / 86** |
| native samplers in the whole cache | 3 | **12** |
| distinct cube-slot cache keys | 1 | **12** |
| distinct base-slot cache keys | 3 | **3** |
| cube-slot creations / cache hits | 1 / 85 | **10 / 76** |

Twelve is exactly the number of distinct sampler states the fixture uses — the minimum — so nothing
is created per draw and the cache is still a cache. No draw, pass, submit, wait, frame or readback
was added.

### Draw-path coverage

All eight applicable paths, each byte-identical to the `DrawPrimitives` reference under Point and
interpolating under Linear: `DrawPrimitives`, `DrawIndexedPrimitives` with 16-bit and with 32-bit
indices, `DrawIndexedPrimitives` with **nonzero `startIndex` and nonzero `baseVertex`** (decoy
vertices and indices in front, so only honouring both is correct), `DrawUserPrimitives`,
`DrawUserIndexedPrimitives` 16-bit and 32-bit, and a **dynamic buffer written twice** so the draw
must read the second write. Ordinary `TextureCube` and `RenderTargetCube` both reach the same binding
under the same captured sampler; the RenderTargetCube faces are *painted* with a 1:1 textured blit
rather than cleared flat, so that leg cannot pass with a filter-invisible fill.

### Validation

`VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` **proven inserted** beneath SDL_GPU by the loader trace
(`Insert instance layer "VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation"`), with SDL_GPU debug mode on: **zero VUIDs**
over the whole 104-check run. No warning was suppressed.

### Sanitizers

Runtimes proven linked (`libasan.so.8`, `libubsan.so.1`). ASan+UBSan **104/104** and UBSan-only
**104/104**, with **zero AddressSanitizer errors and zero UBSan runtime errors** — no use-after-free,
no stale sampler or resource pointer, no invalid cache-key access, no binding-index overflow, no

same driver-side residual REMED-GFX-170 and REMED-GFX-176 recorded.

### False-positive audit

**Sixteen pre-existing SDL_GPU-registered fixtures drive `EnvironmentMapEffect`, and all sixteen
passed on the unfixed backend.** Classified:

## REMED-GFX-181 — Bgfx omitted `_flags` at the environment-map cube binding (DONE 2026-07-31)

`BgfxGraphicsBackend`'s two `EnvironmentMapEffect` submit sites called the FOUR-argument
`bgfx::setTexture(1, envMapSampler_, samplable->GetBgfxCubeTextureHandle())`, so
`GraphicsDevice.SamplerStates[1]` never reached the reflection cube. The ticket named that exactly,
and the correction is the two lines it implies. What the ticket could not say — and what the fix had
to be built on rather than inferred from output — is **what bgfx does with an omitted `_flags`**.

### The omitted-flags semantics, read from the installed bgfx source

`bgfx.h:1502` documents `_flags` as defaulting to `UINT32_MAX`, "uses texture sampling settings from
the texture". The mechanism is a **sentinel, not a flag word**:

* `EncoderImpl::setTexture` (`bgfx_p.h:3440`) stores
  `0 != (_flags & BGFX_SAMPLER_INTERNAL_DEFAULT) ? BGFX_SAMPLER_INTERNAL_DEFAULT : _flags`.
  `BGFX_SAMPLER_INTERNAL_DEFAULT` is `0x10000000` (`bgfx_p.h:220`), a bit `UINT32_MAX` necessarily
  carries — so the default argument collapses to the sentinel and any ordinary word is stored verbatim.
* Every renderer then resolves the binding as
  `0 == (BGFX_SAMPLER_INTERNAL_DEFAULT & _flags) ? _flags : m_flags`
  (`renderer_gl.cpp:6278` `getSamplerState`, `:6414` `TextureGL::commit`; `renderer_vk.cpp:4357`).

So an explicit word **REPLACES** the texture's own creation state outright — it never combines with
it. The bits a per-binding override may carry are `BGFX_SAMPLER_BITS_MASK`: U/V/W address,
MIN/MAG/MIP filter, and COMPARE. Border colour travels in its own `BGFX_SAMPLER_BORDER_COLOR_MASK`
field, read separately at commit. Anisotropy is representable
(`BGFX_SAMPLER_MIN_ANISOTROPIC`/`MAG_ANISOTROPIC`) but its *level* is a global reset flag, not a
per-binding one — the boundary REMED-GFX-170 already declared. Sampler state is encoded in
submission state; there is no native sampler object to key or cache.

### Authoritative slot mapping

`fs_env_map3d.sc` declares `SAMPLER2D(s_texColor, 0)` and `SAMPLERCUBE(s_envMap, 1)`. Slot 0 filters
`EnvironmentMapEffect.Texture`; slot 1 filters `EnvironmentMapEffect.EnvironmentMap`. An unset slot
means the documented device default, `SamplerState::LinearWrap`.

### Root cause

The translation was **already complete and already live**. `ApplySamplerState` carries REMED-GFX-170's
full nine-ordinal mapping onto bgfx's three independent MIN/MAG/MIP bits plus the address bits, and
`GraphicsDevice::applySamplerStatesToBackend` drives it for **every** slot. `samplerFlags_[1]`
therefore held the correct word the whole time and was **discarded one line before the submit**. The
base slot immediately above already passed `samplerFlags_[0]` through `BindSamplerSlot`, which is what
makes this a one-argument omission rather than a missing mechanism: no new state, no new capture, no
second translation table.

**The fix is the five-argument overload with that same captured word, at both sites — two lines of
behaviour in the entire task.**

### Affected submit-site inventory (the count really is two — verified, not assumed)

`grep setTexture` over the backend returns exactly four call sites: `BindSamplerSlot` (generic 3D
slots, already correct), the SpriteBatch bind (already correct), and these two.
`DrawInstancedPrimitivesEx` has **no env-map branch at all** — it always submits
`instanced3DProgram_` — so the instanced path never binds a cube.

| Path | Base binding | Cube binding | Stage | Sampler uniform | Explicit flags before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DrawPrimitivesEx` | `BindSamplerSlot(0, texColor3DSampler_, …)` | `setTexture(1, envMapSampler_, …)` | 1 | `s_envMap` | none (`UINT32_MAX`) | `samplerFlags_[1]` |
| `DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx` | `BindSamplerSlot(0, texColor3DSampler_, …)` | `setTexture(1, envMapSampler_, …)` | 1 | `s_envMap` | none (`UINT32_MAX`) | `samplerFlags_[1]` |

All eight public draw routes funnel through those two: DrawPrimitives, indexed 16-bit, indexed
32-bit, nonzero `startIndex`+`baseVertex`, DrawUser non-indexed, DrawUserIndexed 16- and 32-bit, and a
twice-written dynamic buffer. Both concrete cube classes reach the same binding through
`IBgfxCubeSamplable` — `BgfxTextureCubeBackend` and `BgfxRenderTargetCubeBackend`.

### Command-state capture model

Bgfx submits environment-map draws **immediately** (`SubmitViewProgram` → `bgfx::submit`), and **bgfx
itself** snapshots the encoder's bind state into the frame's command buffer at that call. Reading
`samplerFlags_[1]` at the binding therefore **IS** the per-draw capture — the identical model the base
slot has always used. There is no CNA-side deferred command struct on this backend and so no field to
add, which is exactly what separates this from REMED-GFX-173's SDL_GPU shape. Leg F1 — a draw queued
under PointClamp, kept after `SamplerStates[1]` changes twice — **proves** this rather than asserting
it, and leg E6 proves neither binding aliases the other.

### Native trace

New env-gated `CNA_BGFX_ENVMAP_TRACE` prints, once per env-map submit: draw ordinal, submit path,
view id, both captured public sampler words, both resources' bgfx creation flags, and each slot's
effective `_flags` rendered the way bgfx will read it. Reporting the creation flags needs them to
survive to draw time, so `IBgfxSamplable`/`IBgfxCubeSamplable` gained a `GetBgfxCreationFlagsEXT()`
accessor and the four concrete backends store the exact word they already handed to
`createTexture2D`/`createTextureCube` — the same expression, moved into a variable. Nothing in any
draw path branches on it.

Over the fixture's **86 environment-map binds** (76 `DrawPrimitivesEx` + 10
`DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx`, 4 views):

| | `captured1` distinct | `effective1` | `effective0` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **before** | **12** | `DEFAULT->creation` on **all 86**, 2 distinct (84x `0x00000000`, 2x `…000a`) | `EXPLICIT` on all 86, 3 distinct |
| **after** | 12 | `EXPLICIT` on **all 86**, **12** distinct, `captured1 == effective1` on every line (**0 mismatches**) | unchanged |

`0x00000000` is the ordinary `TextureCube`'s `BGFX_TEXTURE_NONE`; `…000a` is the
`RenderTargetCube`'s `U_CLAMP|V_CLAMP`. Both are linear. So the public sampler was computed, stored,
and then thrown away at the binding, while the base slot one line above was already correct.

### Oracle

REMED-GFX-173's `examples/envmap_cube_sampler_contract_test.cpp` reused **unweakened**: 104 checks over
thirteen legs. **BGFX 62/104 → 104/104.**

* **Why the failing set was exactly the Point-magnifying ordinals {1, 4, 5, 6}:** the fallback the
  omission selected is *linear*, which coincides with the four Linear-magnifying ordinals {0, 3, 7, 8}.
  Half the enum passed by accident. `D9`/`D10`'s byte-identity groupings held **trivially**, because
  every ordinal produced the same image.
* **Leg C1 passed even before the fix** (`differing=0`: changing `SamplerStates[0]` left the cube
  byte-identical). This was **never** slot-0 inheritance — that is what separates it from WebGPU's
  REMED-GFX-172, and it is measured, not inferred.
* **Ordinals 0–8, all nine classified post-fix:** the four Point-magnifying ones are byte-exact stored
  texels and agree byte-for-byte (D9); the four Linear-magnifying ones interpolate and agree
  byte-for-byte (D10); `Anisotropic(2)` is asserted only for its magnification class, REMED-GFX-170's
  declared per-GPU boundary.
* **Mipmapped cube (leg J):** a real 6-level chain with one flat marker per (face, level). mip-Point
  reads stored levels only and reaches a level above 0; each mip-Linear ordinal differs from the
  mip-Point answer; a one-level cube minified under mip-Point still reads stored level-0 texels; two
  aimed faces select different level markers, so mip levels are per-face and not aliased. No automatic
  mip generation. REMED-GFX-175 is preserved.
* **RenderTargetCube (leg L):** the other concrete cube class reaches the same binding and now honours
  slot 1 — L1 (Point stays on stored texels), L3 (Linear interpolates) and L4 (the two differ) all
  pass, with L2 proving the aimed face carries a real pattern rather than a flat fill. No readback or
  MSAA workaround was introduced; REMED-GFX-154's boundary is untouched.
* **Address-mode boundary, unchanged from GFX-173's finding:** on a direction-addressed cube
  Clamp/Wrap/Mirror render identically (0 differing pixels each), so the fixture asserts only that no
  mode produces an off-palette fetch, including a reflection aimed at a face boundary. **No cube
  address-mode convention is invented.** The one behavioural consequence is correct and intended: a
  `RenderTargetCube` under an **unset** slot 1 now samples LinearWrap — the documented default —
  instead of inheriting its creation `U_CLAMP|V_CLAMP`, which is 0-differing here.

### Cardinality and performance

Byte-identical pre- and post-fix: **86 env-map binds, 4 views, 76/10 path split, 86 `EXPLICIT` slot-0
bindings**. The only number that moves is flag-bearing slot-1 calls, **0 → 86** — exactly one explicit
value per affected draw. Zero texture creations changed, zero recreations, zero extra
draw/submit/view/pass/frame/wait/readback, zero per-draw allocation, no cache disabled, no change to
GFX-155/GFX-157 view ordering. One cube is sampled under twelve distinct public samplers without ever
being recreated.

### False-positive audit

**15 pre-existing Bgfx-registered fixtures drive `EnvironmentMapEffect` or the cube path, and all 15
passed on the unfixed backend.** The blind spot is one fact: **not one of them ever sets
`SamplerStates[1]`.**

* 11 also use a **1×1 solid-colour** `TextureCube` (`TextureCube(dev, 1, false, SurfaceFormat::Color)`),
  which cannot express a filter difference under any sampler:
  `bgfx_env_map_test`, `bgfx_environmentmapeffect_{amount_one,amount_zero,combined,eyeposition,fog,fresnel,multilight,specular,worldtransform}_test`,
  `environmentmapeffect_alphascaledlerp_test`.
* `stock_effect_sampler_contract_test` zeroes the cube's contribution outright
  (`setEnvironmentMapAmountProperty(0.0f)`) for its env-map leg.
* `bgfx_rendertargetcube_mip_test` and `bgfx_render_target_cube_sample_test` sample rendered/flat
  faces under the device default and never touch slot 1.
* `point_sampling_contract_test` drives **only** `SamplerStates[0]`, three times.

**None asserts anything false, so none was changed or weakened.** The gap was coverage, and
`envmap_cube_sampler_contract_test` closes it. **0 fixtures strengthened, 0 fixtures weakened.**

## REMED-GFX-182 — Software's cube sampler took no sampler state at all (DONE 2026-07-31)

`SoftwareGraphicsBackend::SampleCubeMap` had this signature:

```cpp
void SampleCubeMap(const SoftwareTextureCubeBackend& cube, const Vector3& dir,
                   float& r, float& g, float& b, float& a);
```

There is no sampler parameter, and that is the whole finding. After face selection it ended in

```cpp
const int px = std::clamp(static_cast<int>(s * static_cast<float>(size)), 0, size - 1);
const int py = std::clamp(static_cast<int>(t * static_cast<float>(size)), 0, size - 1);
const auto& pixels = cube.FacePixels(face);     // level 0, hardcoded
```

— one clamped texel of level 0 — so an `EnvironmentMapEffect` reflection cube was **always
point-sampled at level 0**, however `GraphicsDevice.SamplerStates[1]` was set. REMED-GFX-150
replaced exactly this shape on the ordinary 2D path with an authoritative `SampleTexture` that
separates filter selection, addressing and decode, and REMED-GFX-175 put mip selection in front of
it. Neither reached the cube path.

### Authoritative slot mapping

Unchanged from REMED-GFX-173 and REMED-GFX-181, and re-read from source rather than inherited:
`env_map3d.frag.glsl` declares `binding = 0 sampler2D uTexture` and `binding = 1 samplerCube
uEnvMap`; Vulkan's REMED-GFX-169-corrected `GetOrCreateEnvMapDescSet` writes `slotSamplers_[0]` into
binding 0 and `slotSamplers_[1]` into binding 1. **Slot 0 filters `EnvironmentMapEffect.Texture`,
slot 1 filters `EnvironmentMapEffect.EnvironmentMap`**, and an unset slot uses the documented device
default `SamplerState::LinearWrap`.

### Command capture — there was nothing to fix here

Software rasterizes **immediately**. `DrawPrimitivesEx` and `DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx` are the only
two functions that can reach a cube, and both already read `GetSamplerState(0)` and
`GetSamplerState(1)` **at the public draw call** and pass them BY VALUE down to
`RasterizeTriangleShaded`, which snapshots them into `ShadedContext`. `ShadedContext` therefore
already carried slot 1 — under the name `sampler1`, where `DualTextureEffect`'s second texture uses
it — and no fragment could consult a later live state. This is what separates the task from
REMED-GFX-173's SDL_GPU shape, where a whole command field had to be added: **the capture existed,
the consumption did not.** `SampleCubeMap` was called one line away from a correct, immutable
snapshot of the state it needed and did not take it. Legs F1/F2/F3 and N1 prove the immutability
rather than assuming it. There is no `DrawInstancedPrimitivesEx` on this backend, and the SpriteBatch
path passes its own `SpriteBatch.Begin` sampler for both slots and never binds a cube
(`params.envMapping` is false there).

### Root cause and the corrected architecture

The cube path is given **no filter code, no ordinal table and no address logic of its own**. A new
`CubeFaceSurface` presents the SELECTED face as the `SoftwareColorSurface` capability REMED-GFX-124
introduced, so the cube goes through `SampleTexture` — the same function every ordinary texture uses:

```cpp
void SampleCubeMap(const SoftwareTextureCubeBackend& cube, const SoftwareSamplerState& sampler,
                   bool magnify, float lambda, const Vector3& dir,
                   float& r, float& g, float& b, float& a);
```

Min/mag selection, mip level selection, level combination, texel addressing and decode are now
identical for a cube and a `Texture2D` **by construction**, and cannot drift apart later. The
parameter list deliberately mirrors `SampleTexture`'s. There is no `bool linear` shortcut: all three
components of the public filter act independently, which is what legs D, J and N5 measure.

Supporting changes, each required by that:

* **`SelectCubeFace` / `CubeFaceLocal`** — face selection and the per-face UV projection factored
  out of `SampleCubeMap` **verbatim**, so the per-triangle LOD estimate uses the SAME convention
  instead of a second copy of it. Stages 1 and 2 are otherwise untouched; the cube-face orientation
  convention is settled by REMED-GFX-134 and was not altered. One incidental consequence: a
  degenerate (all-zero) direction used to divide by a zero major axis and cast the resulting NaN to
  `int` — undefined behaviour the UBSan build's `-fsanitize=float-cast-overflow` traps — and now
  resolves to the face centre. Leg N7 covers it.
* **`SoftwareTextureCubeBackend::FaceLevelCount/FaceDim/FacePixels(face, level)`** — storage for the
  whole declared chain has existed since REMED-GFX-135, but it starts ZEROED, so a level counts as
  selectable only once its **full** face rectangle has been written and every level below it has
  too. That is REMED-GFX-175's `storedLevels_` semantics applied per cube face. A cube whose game
  wrote only level 0 therefore samples exactly as it did before, instead of minifying into
  transparent black nobody uploaded (leg N8). **Cube mip STORAGE itself was already complete** —
  REMED-GFX-135 allocates and stores every level and `SetData`/`GetData` agree at every one — so no
  separate ticket is owed; what was missing was only the sampler's access to it, which is the same
  helper this task replaced.
* **`TriangleCubeTexelRate`** — the cube's footprint, resolved ONCE per triangle from the same
  reflection expression the fragment path uses, through a shared `ScreenSpaceTexelRate` factored out
  of `TriangleTexelRate` (byte-identical arithmetic for the 2D path). No per-fragment derivative
  work and no allocation. A degenerate normal, a degenerate eye vector or a vertex outside the
  chosen face's hemisphere reports a rate of 1 — magnification, level 0 — the same "deterministic
  rather than clever" fallback a degenerate 2D triangle already gets.
* **`SampleLevel`'s bilinear rewritten as nested lerps** `a + (b-a)*t` instead of weighted sums
  `a*(1-t) + b*t`. Same four fetches, same algebra, but only this form is EXACT when the taps agree:
  `a + (a-a)*t` is `a` for every `t`, where the weighted sum can land one ULP below it and the
  framebuffer's **truncating** store then writes a byte one lower. This was measured, not guessed —
  ordinals 3 and 6 (the two mip-Point ordinals whose MIN half is Linear) produced `out=(26,48,167)`
  on 8 of 64 pixels where every other ordinal produced `(26,49,167)`, from a cube mip level that is
  a single flat colour. Real hardware filters in fixed point and returns the texel exactly for a
  uniform footprint; a linear filter over a uniform region must return that region's value.

### Address-mode classification — clamped face-locally, and honestly declared

A cube map is addressed by a **direction**: face selection consumes it and the face-local coordinate
that comes out is already in `[0,1]`, so U/V/W address modes are unreachable except exactly at a face
edge. REMED-GFX-173 and REMED-GFX-181 both **measured** Clamp/Wrap/Mirror as rendering a cube
identically on every GPU backend (0 differing pixels for each pair), because cube filtering is
seamless there and the modes never apply. This backend has no cross-face filtering — a long-standing,
explicit simplification — so the honest match to that measured behaviour is to address face-locally
with **Clamp**, which keeps an edge tap on the face's own last texel instead of teleporting it to the
opposite edge under Wrap. **No cube address-mode convention is invented and none is asserted**: the
fixture requires only that no mode produces an off-palette fetch (legs K and K4 pass, 0 off-palette
each, Clamp-vs-Wrap and Clamp-vs-Mirror both 0 differing), and the mode the game set is carried in
the trace so the boundary stays visible rather than silently absorbed.

### Software cube trace

New env-gated `CNA_SOFTWARE_CUBE_TRACE` (=1 summary, =2 one line per env-map fragment, bounded by
`CNA_SOFTWARE_CUBE_TRACE_LIMIT` default 64 and filtered to one draw by `CNA_SOFTWARE_CUBE_TRACE_DRAW`)
prints both ends of the pipeline: the captured public `slot0=`/`slot1=` descriptions against the
`eff=` description the cube sample really ran under, plus draw id, command family, destination pixel,
reflection direction, selected face, face-local u/v, stored level count, lambda, chosen level(s) and
mip weight, within-level filter, addressed texel, **measured** texel-fetch count, sampled RGBA and
the final effect contribution (truncated exactly as the framebuffer store truncates). Texel fetches
are counted at the fetch site itself, so the cardinality below is measured, not derived.

Over REMED-GFX-173's fixture:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cubeSamples` | 72544 | 72544 |
| `texelFetches` | 72544 | 160072 |
| `fetchesPerSample` | 1.0000 | 2.2066 |
| `distinctCaptured` | **12** | **12** |
| `distinctEffective` | **1** | **8** |

**Twelve public slot-1 descriptions reached exactly one cube behaviour.** At one destination pixel,
with an identical reflection direction, face and face-local coordinate:

```
BEFORE draw=1 slot1=(filter=1,Clamp,Clamp) eff=(within=Point,addr=Clamp/Clamp,mip=Point)
              levels=1 mip=[0,0] texel=(1,1) fetches=1 sample=(91,224,246,255) out=(91,224,246)
BEFORE draw=3 slot1=(filter=0,Clamp,Clamp) eff=(within=Point,addr=Clamp/Clamp,mip=Point)
              levels=1 mip=[0,0] texel=(1,1) fetches=1 sample=(91,224,246,255) out=(91,224,246)
AFTER  draw=1 slot1=(filter=1,Clamp,Clamp) eff=(within=Point,addr=Clamp/Clamp,mip=Point)
              levels=1 mip=[0,0] texel=(1,1) fetches=1 sample=(91,224,246,255) out=(91,224,246)
AFTER  draw=3 slot1=(filter=0,Clamp,Clamp) eff=(within=Linear,addr=Clamp/Clamp,mip=Linear)
              levels=1 mip=[0,0] texel=(1,1) fetches=4 sample=(105,185,201,255) out=(104,185,201)
```

On the mipmapped cube, ordinals 0..8 all reported `levels=6 mip=[0,0]` before — six stored levels,
one reachable.

### Fetch cardinality — the canonical minimum, measured

| effective description | level(s) | fetches | samples |
|---|---|---|---|
| within=Point, mip=Point | [0,0] | **1** | 41160 |
| within=Point, mip=Linear | [0,0] | 1 | 2112 |
| within=Linear, mip=Point | [0,0] | **4** | 2112 |
| within=Linear, mip=Linear | [0,0] | 4 | 26368 |
| within=Point, mip=Point | [2,2] | **1** | 288 |
| within=Linear, mip=Point | [2,2] | **4** | 144 |
| within=Point, mip=Linear | [1,2] | **2** | 144 |
| within=Linear, mip=Linear | [1,2] | **8** | 216 |

Point with mip-Point performs **exactly one** final texel fetch; mip-Point selects **exactly one**
level; mip-Linear uses **exactly the two adjacent** levels and no more; a single-level resource
degenerates to one within-level sample rather than two. The 2D trace independently reports
`fetchesPerPointSample=1.0000 fetchesPerLinearSample=4.0000` over the whole run. Zero allocation per
sample (`CubeFaceSurface` is a stack object owning nothing), zero extra draw, pass, frame, wait,
readback or texture copy, zero CPU preprocessing, and the 12→8 gap between captured and effective
descriptions is entirely the declared address-mode collapse plus `Anisotropic(2)` resolving to Linear
like every other Linear ordinal.

### Why `distinctEffective` is 8 and not 12

Magnifying draws (one stored level, `lo = 0`) give four combinations of
(min/mag component, mipmap component): `(P,P)` from ordinals 1 and 6, `(P,L)` from 4 and 5, `(L,P)`
from 3 and 8, `(L,L)` from 0, 2 and 7. Minifying draws on the six-level cube give the same four with
the MINIFICATION half instead: `(P,P)` from 1 and 8 at level [2,2], `(P,L)` from 4 and 7 at [1,2],
`(L,P)` from 3 and 6 at [2,2], `(L,L)` from 0, 2 and 5 at [1,2]. 4 + 4 = 8, fully accounted for.

### Oracle and results

REMED-GFX-173's 104-check fixture is reused **unweakened**: **SOFTWARE 66/100 → 100/100** (leg L
skipped — this backend supports no `RenderTargetCube`). Filter ordinals 0..8 are all classified: the
four Point-magnifying ones (1,4,5,6) are byte-exact stored texels and agree byte-for-byte, the four
Linear-magnifying ones (0,3,7,8) interpolate and agree byte-for-byte, and `Anisotropic(2)` is
asserted only for its magnification class — the same per-backend boundary REMED-GFX-170 declared.
`TextureFilter::Anisotropic` resolves through the same min/mag/mip table as every other ordinal on
this backend and is **not** silently point sampling. Point and Linear cube filtering, mip-Point,
mip-Linear, all six faces, all eight draw paths and four repeated frames are green; face selection
and orientation are byte-identical to before the change on every Point leg.

A new `examples/envmap_cube_sampler_state_test.cpp` (25 checks on Software, 24 elsewhere) covers what
a lost sampler state can ALSO fail: returning to a previous sampler (N1), interleaving with an
ordinary `BasicEffect` draw (N2), sweeping all nine slot-0 ordinals with slot 1 fixed (N3) and all
nine slot-1 ordinals with slot 0 fixed (N4), the magnification partition of the public enum (N5),
create/sample/destroy lifetime at recycled addresses plus re-filtering a live cube with no upload
(N6), a degenerate zero normal (N7), a declared-but-unwritten mip chain (N8), and RenderTargetCube
classification (N9). **SOFTWARE 21/25 pre-fix → 25/25 post-fix**; the four that move (N1b, N5c, N5e,
N6b) are exactly the ones that need slot 1 to reach the cube, and the other 21 pass either way —
which is what shows the leg set is not a second copy of the same measurement.

### RenderTargetCube — classified, not skipped silently

Software creates a `RenderTargetCube` object but **refuses to bind a face**
(`SetRenderTargets: this backend does not support RenderTargetCube.`), because
`CreateRenderTargetCube` keeps `IGraphicsBackend`'s nullptr default — cube render targets are an
explicit v1 boundary in `plan_software.md`. No cube render target can therefore ever hold content to
sample here, and the refusal is a clean exception rather than a silent no-op or a fabricated sample
(leg N9 asserts that shape; REMED-GFX-173's leg L skips with the same message). This was **not**
expanded into RenderTargetCube remediation.

### Resource lifetime

Three create/sample/destroy rounds, each cube filled from a **different** palette block, each sampled
and then destroyed, with a draw on a surviving cube after every destruction: 0 anomalies, 3/3 exact —
so a recycled allocator address shows the new generation's texels and never the previous one's. A
slot-1 change alone re-filters a **live** cube with no upload and no recreation (1024 differing
pixels). Level storage stays the cube's own: `CubeFaceSurface` holds a reference and owns nothing.
ASan reports **zero** leaks and zero errors at device teardown for both fixtures.

### False-positive audit

**Nine Software-registered fixtures drive `EnvironmentMapEffect`, and all nine passed on the unfixed
backend. Not one of them ever sets `SamplerStates[1]` to something DIFFERENT from `SamplerStates[0]`**
— that single fact is the whole blind spot.

| `deferred_scissor_capture_test` | 1x1 cube, `EnvironmentMapAmount = 0`, slot 1 never set |
| `deferred_viewport_capture_test` | 1x1 cube, amount 0, slot 1 never set |
| `spritebatch_3d_order_test` | 1x1 cube, amount 0, slot 0 == slot 1 |

## REMED-GFX-172 — WebGPU bound ONE sampler to the TWO texture views of both multi-texture families (2026-07-31)

### The ticket, and where its scope was already right

The ticket names `DualTexture3D`. A later scope update widened it to `EnvironmentMap3D` "same
backend, same layout/WGSL root cause, same fix shape". **Both halves are right, and the two families
turned out to be the IDENTICAL defect rather than two similar ones** — which is worth stating,
because REMED-GFX-173 (SDL_GPU) had the opposite outcome: there the two families diverged and one
fixture split into separate causes.

### The authoritative slot mappings — measured, not assumed

The task brief explicitly required establishing the DualTexture mapping from source rather than
assuming it matches the EnvironmentMap numbering. It was read from FNA's own HLSL:

| Effect | resource | declaration in FNA HLSL | public sampler slot |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DualTextureEffect` | `Texture` | `DECLARE_TEXTURE(Texture, 0)` | `SamplerStates[0]` |
| `DualTextureEffect` | `Texture2` | `DECLARE_TEXTURE(Texture2, 1)` | `SamplerStates[1]` |
| `EnvironmentMapEffect` | `Texture` | `DECLARE_TEXTURE(Texture, 0)` | `SamplerStates[0]` |
| `EnvironmentMapEffect` | `EnvironmentMap` | `DECLARE_CUBEMAP(EnvironmentMap, 1)` | `SamplerStates[1]` |

They DO agree. Cross-checked against CNA's own `DualTextureEffect::FillGpuDrawParams`, which assigns
`Texture -> params.texture0` and `Texture2 -> params.texture1`.

### The exact pre-fix shape, classified against the brief's own A–E options

**Both families were A *and* D at the same time, and B, C and E were all FALSE.**

| layer | `DualTexture3D` | `EnvironmentMap3D` |
|---|---|---|
| WGSL sampler declarations | ONE, `@group(1) @binding(0) var texSampler: sampler` | ONE, same declaration |
| WGSL texture declarations | `tex0`/`tex1`, both `texture_2d<f32>` | `tex`, `texture_2d<f32>`; `envMap`, `texture_cube<f32>` |
| both `textureSample` calls | pass `texSampler` | pass `texSampler` |
| bind-group layout entries | 3 (sampler, view, view) | 3 (sampler, view, cube view) |
| pipeline layout | group 0 `coloredBindGroupLayout_` + group 1 | group 0 UBO layout + group 1 |
| command sampler fields | ONE `textureFilter/addressU/addressV/maxAnisotropy` | ONE, same names |
| queue-time capture | `slotSamplers_[0]` only | `slotSamplers_[0]` only |
| replay-time selection | one `GetOrCreateSlotSampler` call, used twice | one call, used twice |
| bind-group cache key | **there is no bind-group cache** | **there is no bind-group cache** |

Two of those rows decided the shape of the fix:

* **There is no bind-group cache to key, invalidate or grow.** Bind groups are created per draw with
  `wgpuDeviceCreateBindGroup` and pushed onto `pendingBindGroupReleases_`. The brief asked for
  cache-key correctness; the honest answer is that the cache does not exist, and the new trace prints
  `bgcache=none` so that stays measured rather than implied. Nothing was added — adding a cache would
  have been scope the ticket does not carry.
* **`slotSamplers_` is already a 16-slot array and `ApplySamplerState` already fills every slot.** The
  public state was reaching the backend the whole time; only the two `Queue*Draw` functions never read
  index 1. So the missing pieces were capture, declaration and binding — never state tracking.

### Reproduction, before anything was fixed

| fixture | WebGPU pre-fix |
|---|---|
| `envmap_cube_sampler_contract_test` (unchanged, 104 checks) | **74/104**, leg C1 failing exactly as declared |
| `stock_effect_sampler_contract_test` (unchanged, 65 checks) | **64/65**, the declared leg M3 |
| `dualtexture_slot_sampler_contract_test` (new, 106 checks) | **58/106** |

Leg C1 reads `changing SamplerStates[0] does not alter the CUBE's contribution (differing=1024)` —
every pixel moved, which is inheritance rather than a missing sampler. The new DualTexture fixture
shows the same thing from both sides at once: `y-variation=0` whenever only slot 1 is Linear, and
`y-variation=128` whenever only slot 0 is.

### The new fixture, and why its oracle is stronger than isolation

`examples/dualtexture_slot_sampler_contract_test.cpp` does not measure one slot at a time. Slot 0's
texture varies along **X only**, slot 1's along **Y only**, and the shader's `(tex0*2) * tex1 * tint`
with `tint = 0.5` is exactly `A(x) * B(y)` — a separable product. So `XEdgeVariation` reads slot 0's
magnification filter and `YEdgeVariation` reads slot 1's **in the same image**, and "changing one
sampler affects only its own sampled resource" becomes a direct measurement rather than an inference.
A byte-exact second oracle backs it up: with a white partner, `(2*A)*1*0.5` and `(2*1)*B*0.5` are both
exact in 8-bit, so "an interpolated colour appeared" is decidable with no tolerance.

Thirteen legs, covering all twelve scenarios the brief required: PAL preconditions, A red-first, B the
slot-0 regression gate, C the full independence matrix (both-Point, both-Linear, each cross, change
only 0, change only 1, swap, and return to an earlier pair reproducing it byte-for-byte), D all nine
ordinals on EACH slot, E resource-vs-sampler identity, F the deferred snapshot, G all eight public
draw paths, H repeated frames, I interleaving with another textured family, J mip, K address modes,
L the stride-24 vertex-colour shader module, M the unset-slot default.

One fixture defect of my own was found and fixed mid-task: the mip legs originally used `uvMax = 4`,
giving lambda exactly 2.0, where mip-POINT and mip-LINEAR select the same single level and agree by
definition — a backend ignoring the mipmap component would have passed. `uvMax` is now 3.

### The trace

`CNA_WEBGPU_MULTITEX_SAMPLER_TRACE` emits one bounded row per multi-texture draw: public order,
replay position, both views, both captured descriptions, `statesDiffer`, the sampler BOUND for each
resource, the sampler slot 1's description WOULD resolve to, `sharedSampler`, `slotMismatch`, the
layout, the pipeline layout, `bgcache=none`, the bind group and its entry count.

| | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| DualTexture3D rows | 97, **all** `sharedSampler=YES`, `entries=3` | 97, `entries=4`, **0** `slotMismatch=YES` |
| ...of which `statesDiffer=YES` | 69, **all** `slotMismatch=YES` | 69, **all** `slotMismatch=no` |
| EnvironmentMap3D rows | 86, **all** `sharedSampler=YES`, `entries=3` | 86, `entries=4`, **0** `slotMismatch=YES` |
| ...of which `statesDiffer=YES` | 43, **all** `slotMismatch=YES` | 43, **all** `slotMismatch=no` |

The capture landed one commit BEFORE the binding, deliberately and inertly (both fixtures scored
identically with and without it), because the trace cannot prove "one native sampler serves two
resources whose public descriptions DIFFER" until both descriptions exist to compare.

Post-fix `sharedSampler=YES` survives on 28 and 43 rows — exactly the draws whose two slots genuinely
hold the same state. That is the REMED-GFX-170 sampler cache returning one handle for one description,
not a shared binding.

### The fix

One independently bound sampler per public sampler slot, at `@binding(3)` in both group-1 layouts.
Binding 3 is APPENDED rather than the views renumbered, so `tex0`/`tex1` keep the binding numbers
every other WebGPU 3D family uses.

* `dual_texture3d.wgsl` and its stride-24 vertex-colour sibling: `tex0Sampler` at binding 0,
  `tex1Sampler` at binding 3, each `textureSample` using its own. **Both modules had to change** —
  they are separate shader modules with separate pipeline caches, which is what leg L measures.
* `env_map3d.wgsl`: `envMapSampler` at binding 3, used by the cube's `textureSample`.
* Both group-1 bind group layouts: 3 entries -> 4.
* `IssueDualTextureDraw` / `IssueEnvMapDraw`: resolve the second sampler from the command's own
  captured description through the **existing** `GetOrCreateSlotSampler`. No second translation table
  was created; REMED-GFX-170's remains the only one.
* The cube's fallback 1x1 white default is filtered by slot 1 as well — a missing resource does not
  change which sampler slot owns that binding.

The WGSL is an inline `static constexpr char[]` in `WebGPUGraphicsBackend.cpp`, not a generated
artifact, so no generation step ran and no generated blob was hand-edited. No shared shader artifact
exists for WebGPU and no other backend consumes it.

### Layout and pipeline cache invalidation

Changing a bind-group layout can strand pipelines built against the old one. It cannot here, and this
was verified rather than assumed: `DestroyDualTextureResources` and `DestroyEnvMapResources` release
and `clear()` every pipeline in `dualTexturePipelines_`, `dualTextureColoredPipelines_` and
`envMapPipelines_` **before** releasing the layouts, and `Create*Resources` calls `Destroy*Resources`
first. So the layouts and the pipelines built from them are recreated together, always. No layout
version had to be added to any key, and no unrelated WebGPU pipeline is rebuilt per draw.

### Results

| fixture | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `dualtexture_slot_sampler_contract_test` | 58/106 | **106/106** |
| `envmap_cube_sampler_contract_test` | 74/104 | **104/104** |
| `stock_effect_sampler_contract_test` | 64/65 | **65/65** |

Filters 0–8 are classified on BOTH slots independently (legs D1–D4): for every ordinal, the measured
magnification of the swept slot matches `MagnifiesByPoint` and the OTHER slot's held-Point answer is
unchanged, which is the part a shared sampler could never satisfy. Mip-point and mip-linear are
classified per slot (J1–J6), including that changing slot 0's mipmap component leaves slot 1's
contribution byte-identical. Address modes likewise (K1–K4).

## REMED-GFX-180 — the render-target -> Present lifecycle, and what `SdlGpu_RenderState` was really doing (2026-07-31)

### The ticket is right that it aborts, and wrong that nothing ran

The recorded symptom was `System::InvalidOperationException: Cannot present while render targets are
bound`, "deterministic — 3/3 standalone runs, zero `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]` lines emitted, so nothing in its
own try/catch around `RunAll` is ever reached."

The abort is real. The inference is not. `Check()` used `std::printf` without a flush, stdout is
**block-buffered when it is a pipe**, and `std::terminate` discards that buffer. Re-run under
`stdbuf -o0`, the same binary prints **eleven `[PASS]` and five `[FAIL]` lines** before it dies. The
try/catch around `RunAll` was reached, executed, and reported — its output was thrown away by the
very failure it was describing.

That is why every print in both fixtures is now flushed. A test whose diagnostics cannot survive its
own failure mode is not diagnosable.

### The exact pre-fix outcome

| | |
|---|---|
| exit | **134 — SIGABRT, core dumped** |
| thread | main; no other thread exists |
| first visible line | `[FAIL] threw during RunAll: The requested primitive range exceeds the bound vertex buffer. (Parameter 'primitiveCount') Actual value was 2.` |
| checks actually reached | **11 PASS, 5 FAIL** (A, B, C×2, G×2, H, D×3 pass; E×2 and F×2 fail) |
| last line | `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'System::InvalidOperationException'` / `what(): Cannot present while render targets are bound` |
| the fixture's first intended check | `Check(true, "all RenderState checks render with no exception")` — it *did* run, as its `Check(false, "threw during RunAll: …")` branch |

### The chain, in two stages

**Stage 1 — the primary exception the ticket said was masked.** `fillTriangleGreenVb_` is created
with **three** vertices (`SetData(fillTriangleVerts, 0, 3)`), and `RunFillModeChecks` drew it through
a helper called `DrawFullQuad` whose body hardcoded `DrawPrimitives(PrimitiveType::TriangleList, 0,
2)` — **six** vertices. REMED-GFX-113's range guard in `GraphicsDevice::DrawPrimitives`
(`GraphicsDevice.cpp:686-699`) rejects exactly that: `vertexStart + consumed` must fit the bound
buffer.

The intent was never ambiguous. The buffer's own comment says *"Centroid = (0,0) — render target
centre"*, and Check E needs a **triangle** specifically: a quad's centre lies **on** the shared
diagonal edge, so WireFrame would fill it and the check would be meaningless. One primitive is what
Check E was always asking for.

**Stage 2 — the reported exception.** The rejection unwound past `RunFillModeChecks`' own
`SetRenderTarget(nullptr)`, so `Draw` returned with `rtFillSolid_` still bound. Then:

```
Game::Tick  ->  Game::EndDraw  ->  GraphicsDeviceManager::EndDraw  ->  GraphicsDevice::Present
                                                                        └─ renderTargetBound_ == true  ->  throw
```

The fixture never calls `Present` itself. The call is **framework-driven** — not explicit, not
fixture cleanup, not `GraphicsDevice` teardown, not screenshot/readback infrastructure. Nothing
caught the throw, it left `main`, and `std::terminate` raised SIGABRT.

### Public state vs backend state at the abort

| | |
|---|---|
| public `renderTargetBound_` | **true** |
| public `GetRenderTargets()` | **one** entry — `rtFillSolid_`, the target `RunFillModeChecks` bound |
| SDL_GPU logical destination | that target; one open `PassSegment` carrying the queued `Clear(Magenta)` and zero draws |
| native pass / command buffer / swapchain | **untouched by the refusal** |

The last row is the important one. `SdlGpuGraphicsBackend::Present()` is nothing but
`EnsureFrameRendered()`, and **it is never reached** — the shared public guard throws first. No
native pass is left open, no command buffer is left unsubmitted, no swapchain texture is acquired and
abandoned. There is no stale backend state to find, no pending deferred bind cycle, and no
disposed-target question: the target wrapper is alive throughout. **SDL_GPU is not implicated at
all** — any backend aborts identically on this sequence. The fixture is merely SDL_GPU-registered.

### The authoritative contract: A — reject, never auto-unbind

Read from FNA, not assumed:

* `FNA/src/Graphics/GraphicsDevice.cs:619-631` and `:633-641` — **both** `Present` overloads throw
  `InvalidOperationException("Cannot present while render targets are bound")` when
  `renderTargetCount > 0`.
* `FNA/src/Game.cs` `EndDraw()` -> `FNA/src/GraphicsDeviceManager.cs:574-581` -> `graphicsDevice.Present()`.
  **No unbind anywhere in that path.**

CNA reproduces both halves verbatim, down to the message string. So the framework does **not** return
to the backbuffer on the application's behalf, and `Game.EndDraw` guarantees nothing of the sort:
ending a frame with a binding is an application error, and it is reported. Option B and option C are
both wrong for this codebase.

Nothing here was weakened. No target is auto-unbound at Present, no guard was removed, and the
`Present` call was not deleted from the fixture — the fixture never had one.

### Production or fixture: **fixture**, and it is A/B-proven

With **only** the REMED-GFX-113 range guard short-circuited and nothing else changed, the
**unmodified** fixture runs **16/16 and exits 0** — precisely its pre-guard behaviour. So:

* the fixture was written at `827cd036` (2026-07-15) already asking for six vertices out of three;
* the guard arrived at `0cdd7ee5` (2026-07-26);
* between those dates **Check E passed while reading past the end of its own vertex buffer**, and
  GFX-113 turned that latent out-of-range request into the deterministic public rejection this task
  traced.

The fixture moved, not the guard. Both guards — the range check and the Present refusal — are correct
and both are load-bearing, so **no production file was changed by this task.**

### The repair

| | |
|---|---|
| **0 visible checks + SIGABRT** | **-> 18/18 PASS, exit 0** |

Four changes, all in `examples/sdlgpu_renderstate_test.cpp`:

1. the primitive count is a **parameter** of `DrawGeometry`, named at every call site through
   `DrawFullQuad`(2) and `DrawTriangle`(1), so a helper's name and its geometry cannot drift apart
   again;
2. `Check()` flushes stdout;
3. `RunAllGuarded` reports a thrown group as a **FAIL carrying its message** and always returns to
   the backbuffer, so a future failure stays a legible check instead of becoming an abort. Frames
   2..120 ran outside any handler at all, and the closing `"120 frames …"` check was an
   **unconditional `Check(true)`** — it is now a real assertion naming the frame that threw;
4. Check E's WireFrame half is made positive (below).

**All sixteen original checks are retained unchanged.** 16 -> 18.

### The blind spot inside the subject itself

Check E's WireFrame half asserted only an **absence** — the triangle's centre must stay background —
and an absence is satisfied just as well by a draw that never happened. Its Solid half could not
cover that, because it runs under a **different** `RasterizerState`. So a silently dropped WireFrame
draw would have passed.

Two positive checks close it, counting lit pixels over the whole target rather than depending on
which exact pixels a driver's line rasterizer picks: WireFrame must light **something**, and far less
than Solid. Measured **wire = 64 edge pixels, solid = 240** — a 3.75x margin against a 2x threshold.

### The new contract fixture

`examples/present_lifecycle_contract_test.cpp` — **22 process-isolated legs, 82 checks**, registered
on SDL_GPU, Vulkan, EasyGL, WebGPU, Bgfx, Software and Headless. Run with no arguments it is a
**supervisor** that re-execs itself once per leg and classifies each child as PASS / FAIL / ABORT /
CRASH-with-the-signal-named / TIMEOUT / SKIP / exec-failure.

Group A covers the fourteen valid lifecycles that must present cleanly — empty bind cycle, Clear
only, draw, A->B->backbuffer, cube face, MRT, MSAA, mid-cycle Clear, backbuffer readback on either
side of a Present, `Reset()`, first frame vs later frame, 120 repeated cycles. Group B is the
**negative Present contract**: the refusal must leave the binding, the cycle's queued work and the
device exactly as they were, the very next Present after an unbind must succeed, and a further full
frame after that must still be exact — a guard that threw the right exception but poisoned the device
fails leg B1.

Group C is GFX-180 itself:

* **C1** asserts each link separately — the range rejection naming `primitiveCount` and the range it
  exceeded; the target still publicly bound afterwards, **identity-checked** through
  `GetRenderTargets()[0]` rather than merely counted; the refusal carrying FNA's exact message;
  recovery by unbinding **alone**; the queued `Clear` surviving both the failed draw and the refused
  Present; and the same buffer **accepted** as one primitive.
* **C2** runs the identical sequence with nothing catching it and the supervisor **requires SIGABRT**.
  The terminate classification is measured, not inferred from message text.
* **C3** is the recovery pattern the repaired fixture now uses, asserted as a contract.
* **C4** hands a live, unbound target to device teardown — and **declares that matrix item 18 as
  literally written is unreachable**: a frame cannot end with a binding, because `EndDraw` presents
  and `Present` refuses. That is what C2 measures, so the gap is named rather than left untested.

### Cardinality

Measured with `CNA_SDLGPU_TRACE_CLEAR_ORDER` over the repaired fixture's full 120 frames:

| | |
|---|---|
| pass segments | **1680 over 120 frames = exactly 14 per frame** |
| frame 1 | also **14** — the two whole-target reads Check E gained cost no pass |
| per frame | 11 render-target segments (one per bind cycle, for 11 targets) + 3 backbuffer |
| segment ids | linear to 2879 — no unbounded growth over 120 frames |
| Presents | one per frame, all framework-driven; the fixture calls none |

**No Present, frame, bind cycle, wait, retry, sleep or dummy target switch was added.** The two extra
`GetData` reads occur on frame 1 only and after the frame's first `GetData` has already flushed, so
they add no pass, submit or frame. No queued draw or Clear is lost, and no target resolve/store
changed — nothing in the resolve path was touched.

### Validation

`VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` **proven inserted** beneath SDL_GPU (`Insert instance layer
"VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation"` — 44 insertions across the 22 legs, 2 on the RenderState fixture),
with `SDL_GPU_DEBUGMODE=1`. **Zero VUIDs and zero validation errors on both fixtures.** No render
pass active at present, no swapchain texture used while a target is bound, no unsubmitted commands at
presentation, no device loss.

### Sanitizers

ASan+UBSan and UBSan-only, both fixtures, runtimes proven linked (`libasan.so.8`, `libubsan.so.1`):
**zero AddressSanitizer errors and zero UBSan runtime errors**, 22/22 legs and 18/18 checks under
each.

The LeakSanitizer residual is **driver-side and pre-existing**: every frame is `<unknown module>`,
**zero CNA frames**, and the untouched `cna_test_sdlgpu_depth_bias` — which this task never touched —
produces the byte-identical 624 B / 6-allocation report and the same non-zero exit. A/B classified,
not waived.

### Regression gates and cross-backend controls

**`ctest -R '^SdlGpu' -j1`: 102/102, zero failures.** This is the **first fully green SDL_GPU shard**
— `SdlGpu_RenderState` is the single failure that was carried through REMED-GFX-127, 143/145, 152,
156, 165, 170, 173, 175 and 176. GFX-143/145 segmentation, GFX-152 lifetime, GFX-156 ordered Clear,
GFX-165 backbuffer proxy, GFX-170 sampler translation, GFX-173 EnvironmentMap samplers and GFX-176

The new fixture on every registered backend, **22/22 legs each**:

| backend | checks | shortfall |
|---|---|---|
| SDL_GPU | 82 | — |
| Vulkan | 82 | — |
| EasyGL | 82 | — |
| Bgfx | 82 | two declared boundaries (below) |

Every shortfall is a **runtime-declared** boundary printed by the leg that hit it, never a silent

### Bgfx's two boundaries

* **Leg A14** reached Bgfx's **documented** per-frame ordered view-segment ceiling after **96** of

### False-positive audit

**The "hardcoded primitive count fed a foreign buffer" shape.** Six fixtures share it. The other five
were **verified**, not assumed: every buffer they can be handed holds exactly six vertices, matching
their hardcoded two primitives — `backbuffer_pass_order_test` (`std::array<…, 6>`),
`sdlgpu_rendertarget_viewport_test`, `sdlgpu_rendertarget_scissor_test`,
`sdlgpu_rendertarget_blendfactor_test` (all literal 6), and `sdlgpu_pass_boundary_upload_test` (a

`graphicsdevice_depth_contract_test` and `easygl_rendertargetcube_depthformat_test` — build their own
six-vertex array **inside** the helper, so name and geometry cannot drift apart there at all.
`sdlgpu_renderstate_test` was the only one where a helper named for a quad was handed a triangle.

**The Present-refusal contract.** Two pre-existing fixtures already assert it, both correct and both
narrower:

| fixture | what it covers | what it did not |
|---|---|---|
| `easygl_device_validation_test` check 4 | the refusal happens | EasyGL only; type only, not the message; no assertion that the binding survives or that the device stays usable |
| `bound_target_lifetime_test` leg P1 | the refusal is identical for a live and a **destroyed** bound target, on 7 backends | no MRT/cube binding shape; no "queued work survived"; no recovery-then-full-frame |

**Neither asserts anything false, so neither was changed or weakened** — the gap was coverage, closed
by legs B1/B2/B4/C1. `rendertarget_effect_source_test` already documented this exact abort in a
comment and defended against it with a per-leg unbind; GFX-180 turns that habit into an asserted

**One genuine blind spot found, inside the subject itself** — Check E's absence-only WireFrame half,
described above and now closed.

### New findings

**One. REMED-GFX-184** — Bgfx aborts the **process** by SIGTRAP when a `RenderTarget2D` is created
with both a multisample count and a real `DepthFormat`. `bgfx.cpp(5116): ASSERT isOk() ->
ErrorAssert: 0x02006762 'Frame buffer depth MSAA texture cannot be resolved. It must be created with
either BGFX_TEXTURE_RT_WRITE_ONLY or BGFX_TEXTURE_MSAA_SAMPLE flag.'` —
`BgfxRenderTargetBackend`'s constructor (`BgfxGraphicsBackend.cpp:896-898`) creates the MSAA depth
attachment with `msaaFlag` alone, and that attachment is never sampled, so `BGFX_TEXTURE_RT_WRITE_ONLY`
is what it is missing. `RenderTarget2D(dev, w, h, false, Color, Depth24, 4, …)` is entirely legal
XNA, and this is an abort rather than a catchable exception, so leg A9 declares it through a
`constexpr` boundary and drops the depth attachment on Bgfx only — an abort cannot be caught. No
existing fixture reached it because REMED-GFX-168's leg D1, the only other multisampled target in the
suite, passes `DepthFormat::None`: **MSAA alone is safe; it is MSAA combined with a depth format that
aborts.** Recorded against its own ID, not investigated further.

## REMED-GFX-193 — SDL_GPU one-level render-target mip finalization (DONE 2026-08-01)

### Contract

FNA's `Texture.CalculateMipLevels` starts at one and increments only while the largest extent is
greater than one. `RenderTarget2D` forwards `mipMap` unchanged to its `Texture2D` base, independently
of the requested MSAA count. Therefore `RenderTarget2D(1, 1, mipMap=true, ...)` correctly exposes
`LevelCount == 1`, whether MSAA applies or not. FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver makes the corresponding native
rule explicit: `SDLGPU_ResolveTarget` returns when `num_levels <= 1`; otherwise it generates mips
after the render pass has resolved MSAA into level 0.

### Fix

`SdlGpuRenderTarget2DState` now stores the exact `num_levels` used to create the sampleable,
single-sample colour texture. The deferred pass-finalization path uses that native allocation fact:
it calls `SDL_GenerateMipmapsForGPUTexture` only when `mipMap && levelCount > 1`, for both the primary
target and an MRT extra attachment. A 1×1 target continues through its normal pass/resolve and level-0
content path, but never issues SDL's invalid one-level mip-generation command. A 2×2-or-larger target
still records the same mip-generation call after pass end. No frame, Present, retry, CPU mip generation,
allocation, fence, wait, or MSAA-resolve behavior changed.

### Coverage and results

The existing process-isolated `rendertarget_msaa_mip_readback_test` already covered the 1×1 real-4×
MSAA route, level-0 `GetData`, 2×2 through 16×16 chains, A→B→A rebinds, six create/render/read/dispose
cycles, immediate disposal, and a target retained through device teardown. It now adds H10: a 1×1
`mipMap=true`, non-MSAA route using the same public LevelCount, guarded level-0 readback, and rejected
level-one probe. That re-arms the exact SDL assertion without suppressing it.

Real SDL_GPU debug mode plus Khronos validation: **52/52 legs, 630/630 checks**, zero FAIL lines,
zero `Cannot generate mipmaps for texture with num_levels <= 1!` assertions, and zero VUID/validation
messages. Loader diagnostics separately proved `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` was inserted for the 1×1
MSAA leg. ASan ran the complete **52/52, 630/630** matrix with zero AddressSanitizer errors (leak
detection disabled only for the established driver-only residual); focused UBSan H10/H1/H2/G1/G2/G3
ran **75/75** with zero runtime errors. Public `LevelCountTest` and mip-level validation tests: **9/9**.

Representative untouched controls ran the same focused legs: EasyGL **75/75**, Software **41/41**
(its declared higher-mip refusal), and Headless **35/35** (its declared readback refusal). All runs
used the existing `cmake-build-sdlgpu`, `cmake-build-sdlgpu-asan`, `cmake-build-sdlgpu-ubsan`,
`cmake-build-debug`, `cmake-build-software`, and `cmake-build-headless` trees, ccache, and one build
job at a time. GPU tests were serial. The package reached 83–88 °C during the matrix and work paused
repeatedly until it cooled; no other compilation lane was active.

### Scope kept

Only SDL_GPU production, the shared regression fixture, and these two remediation ledgers changed.
Vulkan, Bgfx, EasyGL, WebGPU, Software, DirectX, and every other production backend are untouched;
`audit/` is untouched. REMED-GFX-190 was not begun.

## REMED-GFX-190 — Vulkan MRT mip-chain finalization (DONE 2026-08-01)

### Contract and root cause

An MRT producer has the same finalization obligations as a single-target producer. After its render
pass ends, every bound colour attachment whose level 0 was produced and whose native allocation has
more than one mip level must regenerate its descendants from that completed level 0. When MSAA is
active, the render-pass resolve into the single-sample level 0 happens first; mip generation consumes
that resolved image. A one-level attachment has no descendant and must issue no generation command.
Binding order is public draw state and remains unchanged.

Vulkan's single-target routes already did exactly this. Their deferred destination is a
`VulkanTargetPassEXT`, and `RecordCommandBuffer` invokes its `MaybeGenerateMips` immediately after
`vkCmdEndRenderPass`. The MRT route replaces those destinations with one `VulkanMRTProxy`. That proxy
inherited `VulkanRTSource`'s empty hook, so the same post-pass call stopped at the proxy and never
reached any member attachment. This explains the discriminating pre-fix observation: level 0 was
byte-exact, a single-target cycle regenerated the same resource correctly, and only an MRT cycle left
the primary level 1 entirely transparent zero.

### Fix

`VulkanMRTProxy` now retains each normalized attachment's immutable shared target-pass record while
constructing its native attachment arrays. The records are stored in the same loop and order as the
public colour bindings. A 2D binding contributes `VulkanRenderTargetBackend::PassEXT()`; a cube-face
binding contributes that face's existing pass record. Missing metadata is rejected alongside the
existing missing-view checks rather than leaving a partially defined producer.

The proxy overrides `MaybeGenerateMips` and delegates to those records after its render pass has
ended. The existing target-pass implementation remains the sole mip generator and its first guard is
still `mipLevels <= 1 || mipImage == VK_NULL_HANDLE`, so mixed mipmapped/non-mipmapped MRT sets need no
special case and one-level resources issue no blit or barrier. The vector belongs only to this
producer proxy, so no unbound/untouched resource is visited. Shared ownership also preserves
REMED-GFX-166's rule when a public target is disposed after unbind but before deferred recording.

No render-pass attachment, draw, clear, resolve, or public binding order changed. Because delegation
is still after `vkCmdEndRenderPass`, MSAA resolves precede mip generation. There is no additional
frame, Present, submit, wait, retry, dummy bind, CPU mip generation, or public API.

### Discriminating matrix

The REMED-GFX-186 fixture's Vulkan carve-out was deleted, not flipped. Before the fix its I1 leg
passed the boundary with **64/64 primary level-1 texels equal to `(0,0,0,0)`** while level 0 and the
single-target positive control were exact. After the fix I1 is **15/15**, and its full process matrix
is **52/52 legs, 637 checks**.

The new Vulkan-only `vulkan_mrt_mip_finalization_test` is one ordinary `Game` frame and calls no
public `Present`. Its **408/408** assertions cover:

- primary and secondary attachment contents independently, using an explicit all-attachment Clear
  plus a stock location-0-only draw;
- both attachments mipmapped, and each ordering of one mipmapped plus one non-mipmapped attachment;
- non-MSAA and real device-applied 4x MSAA, proving resolve-before-generation;
- reversed public bindings and six alternating bind/unbind cycles;
- level 0, level 1, every intermediate level, and the final 1x1 level;
- full and rectangular `GetData`, `startIndex = 7`, oversized capacity, protected prefix and suffix;
- `level == LevelCount` refusal, an untouched destination, and a valid final-level read afterward;
- disposal after unbind but before the deferred producer records, with the dying resource in each
  attachment position;
- an unrelated mipmapped target remaining byte-exact across MRT work;
- mipmapped cube-face attachment finalization once the shared producer is selected; and
- three live targets retained through explicit `Game::Dispose` / device teardown.

The backend diagnostics prove exactly one normal `Game::EndDraw` frame submit and one normal Present.
`VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` is asserted active in-process; the captured validation-message vector
is empty, the CTest destruction-time fatal regex sees no VUID/warning/sync hazard, and explicit device
teardown is clean.

### Regression, sanitizer, and backend controls

The fully relinked serial Vulkan selection is **18/18**: MRT MSAA resolve, mixed formats, 2D/cube mip
chains, cube plural binding/MRT, cube GetData/MSAA face/sample-after-unbind, target lifetime,
backbuffer consumer, GFX-140 pass boundaries, GFX-144 sync validation, GFX-151 producer/consumer
(plain and MSAA), GFX-189/191/192 invalid and per-mip reads, the 52-leg MSAA/readback matrix, and the
new subject. No validation message was emitted.

ASan and UBSan use the existing stable Vulkan sanitizer directories; `libasan.so.8` and
`libubsan.so.1` were independently confirmed linked. The task-specific matrix is **408/408** in both,
with zero AddressSanitizer errors and zero UBSan runtime errors. ASan leak checking was disabled only
for REMED-GFX-189's already A/B-proven LLVM/driver residual of 368 bytes in four allocations. The full
ASan control selection is **5/5**, including all 52 legacy legs and 637 checks. Under heavy unrelated
host compilation, the UBSan legacy supervisor intermittently reported only
`SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_VIDEO) failed: x11 not available` before device creation; across its runs
every leg executed, and each environmentally missed leg was rerun alone after cooling and passed with
no UBSan report. The new MRT subject itself passed in one process on every sanitizer run.

The rebuilt shared-fixture I1 control passes on EasyGL **14/14**, SDL_GPU debug **15/15**, and Bgfx
**14/14**. Software and Headless each pass their explicit unsupported-MRT boundary **1/1**. Their
production code is untouched.

All builds reused `cmake-build-*`, were incremental with ccache, and used at most two local jobs.
GPU tests were serial. Other compilation lanes were counted; work paused at the 84–85 °C limit and
resumed only after cooling. No temporary build tree or destructive Git command was used.

### New finding and scope kept

**One new finding: REMED-GFX-194.** A direct Vulkan `RenderTargetCube::GetData(face, ...)` does not
flush a pending MRT producer containing that face. Cube readback seeds dependency selection with the
face's `VulkanTargetPassEXT`, while the queued destination is a `VulkanMRTProxy`; the proxy has a
`ContainsResolveTargetEXT` bridge for a 2D `VulkanRenderTargetBackend` only, not a cube face/pass. The
direct read therefore returns the previous completed cycle. Reading a 2D member of the same MRT
records the shared producer, after which every cube mip is exact. That separates dependency selection
from this ticket's now-correct post-pass finalization. The fixture pins the prior-cycle boundary so a
future GFX-194 fix turns it red. GFX-194 production was not changed or begun.

Only Vulkan production, the Vulkan-only matrix registration/fixture, the re-armed shared fixture, and
these two ledgers changed. GFX-187, GFX-188, and every other ticket were not worked. `audit/` is
untouched. No recommended next ticket was begun.
