## REMED-GFX-194 — Vulkan cube-face pending-producer identity (DONE 2026-08-01)

### Contract and root cause

A direct `RenderTargetCube::GetData(face, level, ...)` must record every still-pending producer of
that exact subresource before its copy. For an MRT producer, identity includes the target resource,
cube face, requested mip chain, public colour-attachment slot, and the binding cycle that created the
producer. The shared-depth closure from GFX-142 remains intentionally broader for direct cube passes,
but it cannot replace this exact bridge from a face read to an MRT proxy.

The queued MRT destination is a frame-lifetime `VulkanMRTProxy`, while the old readback bridge
accepted only a concrete `VulkanRenderTargetBackend` and compared resolve image views. That covered
2D targets but provided no cube-face equivalent. Cube readback therefore seeded only its face pass,
missed the proxy, and copied the previous completed cycle. Reading a 2D member happened to close the
shared MRT pass first, demonstrating that GFX-190's post-pass mip generation was already correct and
that this defect was dependency selection alone.

### Fix

Every MRT proxy already owns the normalized immutable `VulkanTargetPassEXT` records in the same order
as its native/public colour attachments, and every proxy instance represents exactly one binding
cycle. `FindColorAttachmentSlotEXT` now validates the requested level against the supplied pass's
mip count and uses exact retained-pass identity to return the public MRT slot, or no match. Both 2D
and cube readback pass their exact target-pass record and requested level into
`FlushDeferredRenderTarget`.

The flush scans retired and current proxies, admits a match only when that exact proxy group still
owns a pending segment, and seeds the existing transitive dependency closure with those proxy-cycle
groups. Test-only internal diagnostics report the matched `(segment id, public slot)` pairs; they do
not participate in selection or replay. Resolve-view matching and parent-cube matching were removed
from this path. The pre-existing ascending public-segment replay, command-buffer recording, one
submission/wait, and consumed-segment removal are unchanged.

No render-target binding order, draw order, clear, render pass, resolve, or mip-generation order
changed. No public frame, Present, retry, dummy bind, submission, or wait was added. GFX-190's target
pass remains the sole mip generator after pass end, including resolve-before-generation for MSAA.

### Discriminating matrix

The new Vulkan-only `vulkan_cube_face_readback_dependency_test` runs inside one ordinary `Game` frame
and calls no public `Present`. Its **153/153** checks cover all six faces, face zero and nonzero faces,
direct single-target rendering, a cube face as primary and secondary MRT attachment, reordered public
bindings, two different cubes, three pending A/B/A cycles, level zero and valid lower mips, full and
rectangular reads, `startIndex = 9` with protected prefix/surplus/suffix, immediate reads after
producer work, disposal of another attachment before read, target disposal, and explicit device
teardown with two cubes still live.

The A/B/A leg is the identity discriminator: reading A.face0 matches exactly the first and third
proxy cycles at slot zero, in public segment order, and does not select the intervening cycle that
writes a different face of the same parent A cube. The intervening B-face cycle remains independently
readable and reports its own one-cycle/slot-zero match. The re-armed GFX-190 boundary now reads the
new reordered cube-primary producer directly instead of the prior completed cycle.

### Validation, sanitizers, and controls

The final regular GFX-194 matrix is **153/153** and GFX-190 remains **408/408**. Both assert
`VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` active, capture zero validation messages, use exactly the ordinary
`Game::EndDraw` frame submit and Present, and complete explicit device teardown. Producer-consumer
passes **44/44** in plain, real-MSAA, and synchronization-validation modes with zero hazards or other
messages; the bound-target lifetime supervisor passes **18/18**. The focused serial Vulkan shard also
passes **11/11**, covering cube plural MRT, producer closure, GFX-140 pass boundaries, GFX-144 sync,
GFX-151 plain/MSAA producer-consumer, GFX-166 lifetime, GFX-190 finalization, and GFX-191 per-mip
readback/invalid-level behavior.

ASan and UBSan used the existing `cmake-build-vulkan-asan` and `cmake-build-vulkan-ubsan` directories;
`libasan.so.8` and `libubsan.so.1` were confirmed linked. Each sanitizer passes GFX-194 **153/153**,
GFX-190 **408/408**, producer-consumer **44/44**, and lifetime **18/18**, with zero AddressSanitizer
errors and zero UBSan runtime errors. ASan leak detection was disabled only for GFX-189's established,
A/B-proven 368-byte LLVM/driver residual.

Representative untouched backend controls pass the public cube GetData contract: EasyGL **55/55**,
SDL_GPU **55/55**, Bgfx **55/55**, Software **21/21** with its declared no-cube boundary, and Headless
**55/55** with its declared readback limits. Only Vulkan production changed.

All builds reused stable `cmake-build-*` directories and ccache, with at most two local jobs and the
final sanitizer/regular refreshes at one job. GPU tests were serial. Host compiler lanes and Tctl were
observed throughout; new work paused above the thermal gate and resumed only at or below 75 °C, while
already-running one-job builds were allowed to finish as required.

### Scope and new findings

preserved. No other backend's production was modified; GFX-187, GFX-188, every other ticket, and the
recommended next ticket were not begun. `audit/` is untouched.

**No new findings were created.**

## REMED-GFX-122 — EasyGL instanced draw offsets and step rate (DONE 2026-08-02)

### Recorded status, reproducer and authoritative contract

Both remediation ledgers were read before production was edited and recorded GFX-122 as **OPEN**,
MEDIUM/GRAPHICS/P2. The exact current-HEAD reproducer
`InstancedDrawRangeTest.EasyGLStockInstancedPathIgnoresOffsetsAndTheInstanceStream` passed **1/1**
against the wrong result: a request for slots 3-4 with `baseVertex=6`, `startIndex=3` and three
instances lit element-zero geometry in slot 0/band 0, left slot 3 dark, and produced zero pixels in
later bands. With only the production correction applied, that old pin failed in the opposite,
expected direction: slot 0 became 0 pixels, slot 3 became 2470 lit pixels, and the later bands
became 9874 lit pixels. The pin was then replaced by the positive permanent oracle.

The repository's public `GraphicsDevice::DrawInstancedPrimitives` API and `VertexBufferBinding`
define `startIndex` in index elements, `baseVertex` added to each decoded index once,
`VertexOffset` in vertex elements, and `InstanceFrequency` as the number of instances sharing one
instance element. The accepted FNA/FNA3D OpenGL reference multiplies a binding's vertex offset by
its declaration stride only when constructing the byte pointer, uses `startIndex * indexElementSize`
for the index pointer, applies either native base vertex or pointer rebasing but not both, and passes
the exact instance frequency as the attribute divisor. Its D3D11 and SDL GPU controls use the same
start/base/step contract. Completed GFX-113, GFX-118 and GFX-119 establish the matching exact-range
rule; GFX-125 supplies the packed declaration/stride boundary. GFX-147's render-target orientation
contract remains unchanged.

### Proven mechanism and narrow correction

The defect spanned the native draw and attribute-construction stages. The stock EasyGL branch
always gave `draw_elements_instanced` a null index pointer, never applied `params.baseVertex`, and
never bound `params.instanceVb`, so only topology-derived `primitiveCount` survived. The custom
`ShaderEffect` branch bound its instance declaration from byte zero with divisor 1, regardless of
the public binding. The shared payload carried none of the mesh offset, instance offset or frequency,
and singular `SetVertexBuffer` left the prior plural binding vector available as stale state.

`GpuDrawParams` now carries the two element offsets and the exact step rate. The public draw guard
validates the mesh window after binding offset plus base vertex, and validates the number of instance
elements as `1 + (instanceCount - 1) / InstanceFrequency` after its binding offset. EasyGL performs
the stride multiplication only while constructing declaration-accurate GL attribute pointers,
preserving integer versus normalized packed formats. It uses `startIndex * 2` or `startIndex * 4`
for the native index pointer and `glDrawElementsInstancedBaseVertex` only when a nonzero base is
required. Custom effects append the instance declaration after the mesh declaration. All twelve
stock 3D program variants share an optional four-column instance transform at locations 12-15,
leaving locations 0-11 available to the mesh within the GLES/XNA 16-attribute limit; an ordinary
draw keeps the uniform gate disabled.

After each instanced draw the instance attributes are disabled, their divisors reset, any temporary
mesh offset pointers restored, and the stock instance gate cleared. A singular vertex-buffer bind
also clears the old plural layout. This preserves cached VAO and buffer ownership while making
instanced→ordinary→previous-layout transitions deterministic. No CPU geometry rewrite, per-draw
instance duplication/repacking, public frame, `Present`, retry, sleep, wait, or other backend's
production was added.

### Offset and lifetime matrix

The permanent EasyGL instanced suite passes **17/17**. Its asymmetric slot/band data distinguishes
the first index, base vertex, mesh offset, instance offset, frequency, and previous-draw state:

| Axis | Covered values/routes |
|---|---|
| Mesh binding offset | 0 and 3 vertex elements; custom route 4 elements |
| Index range | `startIndex` 0 and nonzero, independently and with nonzero `baseVertex` |
| Base vertex | 0 and nonzero, applied exactly once |
| Index format | 16-bit and 32-bit; start remains an element offset |
| Instances | counts 1, 2, 3 and 4; asymmetric transforms/bands |
| Instance binding | offsets 0 and 1 element; frequencies 1 and 2 |
| Streams and storage | mesh plus instance streams; static and dynamic vertex/index/instance buffers |
| Reuse | first/middle/final ranges, A→B→A, instanced→ordinary→same instanced layout |
| Destinations/order | backbuffer, `RenderTarget2D`, viewport/scissor and ordered target transitions |
| Lifetime | source update, buffer disposal, device teardown and VAO reuse |

EasyGL exposes only the indexed public instanced entry point; no non-indexed instanced production
route exists. Ordinary indexed and non-indexed paths remain their controls. The strengthened public
custom-`ShaderEffect` fixture combines mesh `VertexOffset=4`, `baseVertex=1`, `startIndex=3`, instance
`VertexOffset=1`, two distinct transforms and declaration-contiguous instance attributes; its two
readbacks are exactly white `(255,255,255,255)` and gray `(64,64,64,255)`.

### Regression, diagnostics, sanitizers and controls

- Relevant indexed/non-indexed range, binding, validation and packed-layout tests: **89/89**.
- Seven ordinary stock-effect golden tests: **7/7**.
- Relevant EasyGL CTest shard, run serially: **21/21**, including buffer, layout/custom-effect,
  render-target, ordering and teardown fixtures.
- EasyGL OpenGL diagnostic: clean GLES 3.2 context with no Mesa/OpenGL diagnostic message.
- Combined AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: dedicated suite **17/17** plus the custom
  fixture, with no address or undefined-behaviour report. Leak-enabled ASan identified only an
  external Mesa/libdrm shutdown residual (51,136 bytes in 68 allocations, no CNA frame), so the
  clean required run disabled leak detection only and retained `halt_on_error=1` for ASan/UBSan.
- Vulkan instanced control with Khronos validation: **16/16**, zero validation output. Representative
  SDL_GPU **43/43**, Bgfx **43/43**, WebGPU **42/42**, Software **40/40**, and Headless **30/30**
  controls passed without modifying those backends' production.

Every persistent `cmake-build-*` directory was reused with incremental builds and ccache; no build
tree was created. Maximum compilation parallelism was **-j8**. Approximate peak temperature was
**90 °C** during an early build, so a cooling pause was required and later compilation was reduced.
Graphics/display tests were serial. Only exact session-owned processes were controlled.

### Scope, commits and findings

Production changed only the shared instanced draw payload/public binding handoff and EasyGL. Focused
coverage changed only the existing instanced suite and existing EasyGL custom-effect fixture, plus
these two ledgers. GFX-113, GFX-118, GFX-119, GFX-125, GFX-147, ordinary drawing, exact primitive
ranges, packed declarations, VAO/buffer lifetime, render-target orientation and ordering remain
green. `audit/` is untouched. Signed implementation commit:

- `a5f415a9 fix: honor EasyGL instanced draw offsets`

**No new findings were created.** GFX-121 and GFX-123 remain OPEN and untouched. The recommended
next ticket is **REMED-GFX-123**; it was not begun.

## REMED-GFX-148 — Software complete Additive blend equation (DONE 2026-08-02)

### Reproduction and authoritative contract

Both remediation ledgers were read before production changed and still recorded GFX-148 **OPEN**, severity
**MEDIUM**, category **GRAPHICS**. On starting HEAD `fd658b588172be333e9718b9f5eb93781ce3eacc`,
the existing mid-tone probe reproduced the exact record: source `(64,96,32,255)` over destination
`(36,92,173,255)` stored source-only `(64,96,32,255)` instead of `(100,188,205,255)`. The final
focused fixture, run against the unmodified implementation, was **5/28**: opaque Additive expected
`(72,60,142,255)` but got `(61,29,87,255)`; partial Additive expected `(36,44,106,67)` but got
`(33,36,92,102)`; zero destination expected `(25,13,51,16)` but got `(25,13,51,64)`; saturation,
repeated accumulation, mixed-colour accumulation, state transitions and every indexed/non-indexed public
draw route likewise exposed the hard-coded over equation. The asymmetric values distinguish source-only,
destination-only, wrong RGB/alpha factors, wrong premultiplication, stale destination loading and early
saturation/conversion.

The oracle comes from CNA's current `BlendState::Additive` definition, CNA's public `Blend` component
definitions, FNA's accepted preset, FNA3D's OpenGL/D3D controls and the existing `BlendStateTest` contract:
colour source/destination are `SourceAlpha`/`One`, alpha source/destination are independently
`SourceAlpha`/`One`, and both functions are `Add`. Therefore, in normalized components:

- `RGB = clamp(src.rgb * src.a + dst.rgb)`;
- `A = clamp(src.a * src.a + dst.a)`;
- only then does Software use its established `static_cast<uint8_t>(component * 255)` RGBA8 conversion.

`AlphaBlend` is the premultiplied `src*One + dst*(1-srcA)` contract; `NonPremultiplied` is
`src*srcA + dst*(1-srcA)`. Those independent controls prevent the failing Software output from defining
the expected Additive equation.

### Exact mechanism, classification and correction

This is a **production defect plus same-mechanism fixture correction**. `SoftwareGraphicsBackend::ApplyBlendState`
collapsed the four blend factors and two functions to one `blendEnabled_` boolean: exact Opaque was false and
every other public state was true. `WriteShadedFragment` then used `src.rgb*srcA + dst.rgb*(1-srcA)` and
`srcA + dstA*(1-srcA)` for every non-Opaque state. Thus the responsible stage was **BlendState translation**:
source/destination colour factors, source/destination alpha factors and separate colour/alpha functions were
all discarded. Destination-pixel addressing/loading was correct, as were texture sampling, target producer/
consumer storage, channel layout, draw order, state ownership and backbuffer/RenderTarget2D selection.

The narrow correction replaces the boolean with the six captured ordinals plus the device `BlendFactor`.
Software validates the state once, snapshots it by value once per public SpriteBatch/non-indexed/indexed draw,
loads the current destination bytes for each passing fragment, evaluates source and destination terms with
separate colour and alpha functions, clamps after the function, and retains the existing final byte conversion.
The exact Opaque identity keeps its existing replacement path. No public API, frame, Present, retry, sleep,
image copy, texture sampler, render-target producer/consumer mechanism or other backend production changed.
The effects and ColorWrite fixtures had encoded the obsolete simplified equation: their AlphaBlend sources are
now correctly premultiplied and require exact `(128,0,126,255)` and masked `(201,20,54,40)` results. The old
Software-only Additive `SourceOnly` declaration is now `SourcePlusDestination`.

### Pixel matrix, ordering and targets

The dedicated Software result is **28/28 across three frames**. Opaque, partial, zero-alpha and full-alpha
sources; zero and saturated destinations; two repeated Additive draws; two different colours accumulated in
sequence; Additive versus AlphaBlend/Opaque/NonPremultiplied; Additive -> Opaque -> Additive; caller-state
mutation after `SpriteBatch::Begin`; and two distinct adjacent destination pixels are pixel-exact. Repeated
Additive yields `(61,57,157,83)` and the mixed-colour sequence yields `(54,100,136,95)`. The partial result is
RGB `(36,44,106)` and alpha `67`, proving separate colour/alpha factors; the zero-destination alpha is `16`,
proving alpha is `srcA*srcA`, not straight-over `srcA`.

`DrawPrimitives`, `DrawIndexedPrimitives`, `DrawUserPrimitives`, `DrawUserIndexedPrimitives` and SpriteBatch
all produce the identical `(36,44,106,67)` oracle. RenderTarget2D producer/direct readback is exact before
explicit disposal. Backbuffer reads are exact on frames 1, 2 and 3. Source disposal, target disposal and ordinary
game/device teardown are clean. The ordinary state/order controls remain green: effects **7/7**, ColorWrite
**17/17**, colour-space **17/17**, SpriteBatch/3D public ordering **86/86**, and BlendState/default-state unit
tests **48/48**.

### Sanitizers, shard and cross-backend controls

The existing Software ASan tree is linked to `libasan.so.8`. Direct serial runs pass the dedicated matrix
**28/28**, effects **7/7**, ColorWrite **17/17**, colour-space **17/17** and SpriteBatch/3D ordering **86/86**
with no address report. Leak checking alone was disabled because LeakSanitizer itself terminates under this

The complete Software CTest shard ran serially under `DISPLAY=:101` and is **59/60**. Every blend, effect,

`cmake-build-vulkan`, `cmake-build-sdlgpu`, `cmake-build-bgfx`, `cmake-build-webgpu`,

## REMED-GFX-197 — Bgfx Task 952 cube-depth fixture correction (DONE 2026-08-02)

### Reconciliation and exact recorded sequence

Both remediation ledgers were read before any production edit. Task 952 was recorded only as a
remaining Bgfx shard failure and had no assigned `REMED-GFX` identifier. The next unused canonical
identifier, `REMED-GFX-197`, was therefore assigned once; no duplicate ticket was created.

The recorded test was reproduced on signed HEAD `40bf0bf8` in its own process because the native
Bgfx path can abort. It requested OpenGL and reported active **OpenGL 2.1**. For each of
`DepthFormat::None` and `DepthFormat::Depth24Stencil8`, its exact public producer sequence was:

- `RenderTargetCube(device, 32, false, SurfaceFormat::Color, depth, 0,
  RenderTargetUsage::DiscardContents)`; requested/applied MSAA was **0/0**;
- bind `CubeMapFace::PositiveZ`;
- `Clear(Target | DepthBuffer, (0,0,0,255), 1.0, 0)`;
- draw a near green full-face quad at z=.2, then a far red quad at z=.8; depth testing was enabled;
- unbind, clear the backbuffer to `(10,10,10,255)`, sample the cube through
  `EnvironmentMapEffect`, then call `GetBackBufferData` for its centre texel.

Both depth choices returned the untouched observer clear `(10,10,10)`. The `None` route was not
asserted and the D24S8 route finished **0/1**, expecting near green. Before production was changed,
a temporary direct face `RenderTargetCube::GetData` diagnostic was inserted between unbind and
sampling. It returned exact far red for `None` and exact near green for D24S8. This separated the
producer from its observer: colour rendering, the D24S8 attachment and actual near/far depth
rejection were already correct, while the later sampling draw never affected the backbuffer.

### Exact mechanism and narrow correction

The observer had been changed earlier to use
`Matrix::CreateLookAt(Vector3(0,0,5), Vector3::Zero, Vector3::Up)` so its reflection vector was not
degenerate, but retained an Identity projection. Its sampling quad at world z=0 was consequently at
view-space z=-5, outside Identity's clip volume. Replacing only the projection with
`CreateOrthographic(2,2,0.1,100)` made the draw land, but its centre was only `(2,0,0)` for `None`
and `(0,2,0)` for D24S8. The fixture had also left `EnvironmentMapEffect`'s lighting and Fresnel
defaults active. Full ambient light, disabled directional lights, Fresnel factor 0, alpha 1 and fog
disabled produce the exact sampled cube colours.

Task 952 is therefore the “another exact mechanism” branch: a stale test observer. It is not cube
depth-attachment creation, D16/D24/D24S8 native format selection, colour/depth sample compatibility,
the single shared depth attachment, framebuffer ownership, face framebuffer construction,
depth/stencil Clear flags, resolve/finalization or capability negotiation. The narrowest complete
correction changes the Bgfx regression fixture and its registration comment only. No production
file, public API, public frame, Present, retry, sleep, dummy bind, readback workaround, or wait was
added. Requested public depth, stencil, usage and MSAA values remain production-owned and unchanged.

### Direct functional coverage

The replacement `Bgfx_RenderTargetCube_DepthFormat` fixture passes **519/519** internal assertions
plus its explicit device-teardown assertion. It constructs
`RenderTargetCube(device,24,false,Color,depth,requested,PreserveContents)` for every combination of
`None`, `Depth16`, `Depth24`, `Depth24Stencil8` and requested 0/4x MSAA. It prints and asserts the
active renderer, exact requested and applied count, public colour/depth formats and usage. The
applied count is derived from the established active-renderer capability policy; supported 4x is
required to remain active. Native diagnostics assert matching colour/depth MSAA flag fields,
requested depth presence, and six valid face framebuffers.

All six faces are produced in a nontrivial order with Target+Depth+Stencil Clear, near geometry
followed by overlapping far geometry, then unbound. `None` must expose the later far draw; every
depth format must retain the near draw. A face A / face B / partial face A cycle asserts face
isolation and preserved bands. All six corrected `EnvironmentMapEffect` consumers are queued before

D24S8 has separate non-MSAA and supported-MSAA legs. A depth-only Clear must accept a later far
probe while preserving existing colour. A stencil stamp followed by an Equal gate must change only

through explicit `GraphicsDevice` teardown and must be disposed before backend destruction.

## REMED-GFX-179 — Bgfx render-target/view capacity (DONE 2026-08-01)

### Exact reproduction and mechanism

The failure reproduced on the signed GFX-195 baseline before production was edited. The existing
`Bgfx_DescriptorCapacityContract` reached **28/29** and its render-target leg threw
`Bgfx: exhausted view ids (more concurrently-live render targets than bgfx supports views)`. The
dedicated boundary probe then isolated construction itself: **63** simultaneously live, never-bound
`RenderTarget2D`s succeeded; constructing number **64** threw. Counts 65, 66 and 96 therefore failed
at the same allocation boundary. No Clear, draw, bind, Present, readback or frame advance was needed
to trigger it.

The exact source was `Detail::AllocateRtViewId()`. Every `BgfxRenderTargetBackend` and
`BgfxRenderTargetCubeBackend` called it from its constructor, and an MRT set took another ID while
its temporary framebuffer lived. The allocator's free list worked: destruction returned the ID and
the pre-existing sequential create/destroy workload passed. Its new-ID cursor, however, was limited
to `[1, kFirstSegmentViewId)`, and `kFirstSegmentViewId` was 64. Thus IDs 1 through 63 were persistent
object descriptors even for resources that had never been used.

This was a CNA partition, not bgfx's native view limit. The build has
`BGFX_CONFIG_MAX_VIEWS == 256`; CNA had reserved `[64,255)` for REMED-GFX-065/018/155's ordered
per-frame target, viewport, transform and Clear segments, with view 255 separately reserved for
readback/backbuffer flush. The fixed 256-entry framebuffer-binding mirror and view-order membership
array merely cover legal bgfx view state and were not exhausted. Native texture/framebuffer handles
were also not the source: they remained valid below the boundary, and disposal/recreation reused
their IDs. The failure was therefore exactly a **fixed view-ID partition plus the wrong lifetime**:
simultaneously live objects, rather than distinct view states used during one frame.

### Narrow correction

Render-target and cube objects no longer allocate, store or release a view ID. Binding selects only
the native framebuffer and consumes no ID. The first real Clear/draw on that binding lazily receives
the next ordered view, as do later target/backbuffer cycles, viewport or SpriteBatch-transform
changes, and the internal GFX-195 cube publication step. View 0 is retained only for the first
backbuffer operation in a frame. Every other public/internal ordered state draws monotonically from
`[1,255)`, and the existing reserved readback/flush view 255 is never returned.

The allocator refuses before 255 rather than wrapping, so same-frame state cannot collide with or
redirect an earlier operation. A run of compatible draws reuses its current view: draw count does
not grow the cursor. Every actual `bgfx::frame()` path calls `EndFrameSegments()`, which resets the
cursor to 1 and clears order membership; a target still bound in the next frame receives a new
per-frame ID only when it does real work. The physical limit is now at most 254 distinct ordered
non-initial-backbuffer states **used in one frame**, not 63 objects alive across arbitrary frames.

Separating every MRT bind cycle onto its real ordered view exposed an old masking effect: the prior
MRT base ID was released and immediately reused, so the next attachment set repointed that base
last-wins and the earlier set never retained its own framebuffer state. Once public order was
correct, OpenGL's legacy single `gl_FragColor` output was visible on every attachment bgfx exposed as
a draw buffer. CNA's Bgfx shader inventory has exactly one colour output. The MRT path now keeps a
paired temporary framebuffer: the Clear framebuffer exposes every colour attachment as writable,
while the draw framebuffer exposes only slot 0 and keeps later slots attached without inventing
shader outputs. Clear and a following draw receive distinct ordered views. This preserves
all-attachment `ClearOptions::Target`, the established single-output pipeline, the attachment-set
boundary, and the newly restored public order. Both temporary framebuffers are destroyed on the
next target transition or device teardown; no persistent view/resource list or per-frame retry
queue was added.

There is no public frame, `Present`, retry, sleep, dummy bind or wait in the correction. Readback's
existing synchronous frame completion is unchanged. No public API or another backend's production
was modified.

## REMED-GFX-195 — Bgfx per-face multisample colour preservation (DONE 2026-08-01)

### Recorded evidence and exact public boundary

Both ledgers were read before production was changed. They recorded one current Bgfx boundary left
after signed GFX-138 commit `d26a8e3a`: the re-armed usage oracle drew face A, drew face B, partially
redrew A, and read four correct marker texels plus **60/64** stale texels from B. Immediate resolved
reads and a single-face preserve/rebind were exact. GFX-138 had not investigated or changed this
failure, and GFX-141 had changed the corresponding storage shape only in EasyGL, Vulkan and SDL_GPU.

The current-HEAD reproduction used exactly the public construction
`RenderTargetCube(device, 8, false, SurfaceFormat::Color, depth, 4,
RenderTargetUsage::PreserveContents)`. The dedicated direct-result fixture reproduced the canonical
**4/64 exact, 60 contaminated** result and found **0/6 exact** faces. It reproduced with `DepthFormat`
`None`, `Depth16`, `Depth24`, and `Depth24Stencil8`; the single-sample control was exact. Creation,
binding, Clear, unbinding, sampling, and `GetData` all completed. The corrupt state was introduced
while rendering a partial update after switching back to a previously used face. MSAA was necessary.

FNA's public `RenderTargetUsage::PreserveContents` contract explicitly preserves render-target
contents across binding, and the cube constructor publicly accepts the requested depth format and
multisample count. The operation is therefore supported. CNA/FNA models one shared cube depth
attachment; this remediation preserves that shape.

### Root cause and narrow correction

bgfx's active OpenGL implementation allocates one hidden multisample renderbuffer per texture, not
per cube layer. All six framebuffers for the old multisampled cube texture consequently attached the
same colour producer. Switching A -> B replaced A's producer state; a later partial A draw wrote its
markers over B. bgfx then resolved the selected face correctly, and direct readback correctly exposed
that resolved result. This was neither a capability-declaration, native depth-attachment,
framebuffer-compatibility, resolve, sampling, nor GetData defect.

The public image remains one single-sample cube texture. Only the multisampled route now creates six
independently resolving 2D colour targets, one per face. When an active cube segment has recorded
work, the existing ordered view mechanism switches away from that producer framebuffer so bgfx
performs its native resolve and mip generation, then copies every resolved level into the selected
layer of the public cube through `bgfx::blit`. Subsequent public producer/consumer views retain
monotonic ordering. The one shared depth texture remains attached to every face framebuffer exactly
as before.

The requested colour/depth formats and applied sample count are not changed. A renderer that applies
MSAA but lacks texture-blit capability receives a deterministic `NotSupportedException` during
construction. Single-sample cubes retain the old direct-to-cube attachment path. No public frame,
Present, retry, sleep, wait, readback, dummy public bind, CPU copy, or cross-backend production change
was added.

### Direct-result regression coverage

`Bgfx_GFX195_RenderTargetCube_Preserve` is a dedicated registration of the exact shared public
fixture and passes **33/33**. It covers a non-MSAA control; the canonical A/B/partial-A sequence; all
six faces; `PreserveContents`, `DiscardContents`, and `PlatformContents`; a single face; two cubes;
cube-to-RenderTarget2D and cube-to-backbuffer transitions; repeated bind/draw/read cycles; disposal
and recreation; normal device teardown; `None`, `Depth16`, `Depth24`, and `Depth24Stencil8`; and
repeated direct `GetData`. Its asymmetric colours and marker rectangle reject flat, zero, stale,
aliased, and wrong-face results. The post-fix canonical result is **64/64 exact with zero foreign
texels**, and the simultaneous face result is **6/6 exact**. The usage fixture's former Bgfx boundary
is re-armed as exact.

### Validation, sanitizers, and controls

The dedicated GFX-195 fixture, GFX-138 fixture, cube usage/MSAA-face/depth/mips/sampling/GetData
fixtures, GFX-154/155/157/158/163/181 ordering and attachment controls, RenderTarget2D controls, and
Bgfx diagnostics are green. Diagnostics report GFX-138 **416/416** with ordered views, explicit
sampler bindings, and completed readback; no new diagnostic class appeared.

The complete Bgfx CTest shard ran serially and finished **172/176** in 478.12 seconds. The four

OpenGL-fallback `RenderTarget2D_MsaaResolve`, the corresponding Vulkan-request ClearOptions control,

GFX-195 and every relevant regression gate passed inside the same shard.

The existing Bgfx ASan and UBSan trees were confirmed linked to `libasan.so.8` and `libubsan.so.1`.

## REMED-GFX-123 — D3D11 and D3D12 instanced draw offsets (DONE 2026-08-02)

### Recorded status, reproducer and authoritative contract

Both ledgers were read before production was edited. `REMEDIATION_INDEX.md` recorded GFX-123 as
**OPEN**, MEDIUM/GRAPHICS; `REMEDIATION_PROGRESS.md` recorded it MEDIUM/P2, depending on
REMED-GFX-118's cross-backend controls, with the reproducer *"measured on D3D11 (Wine + DXVK) by
temporarily widening REMED-GFX-118's regression guard: **3/16**, with a `startIndex`-only request
rendering the element-zero prefix"* and D3D12 *"inspection-only (runtime blocked by
REMED-BUILD-012)"*. GFX-118's own record additionally noted that no red test was ever committed for
it, and that D3D9 already honours both offsets in its own instanced path (REMED-GFX-060), making
this the one D3D path the earlier offset tasks did not cover.

The authoritative contract is the one GFX-106/107/118 established and `GraphicsDevice::
DrawInstancedPrimitives` validates: `startIndex` is an index **element** offset; `baseVertex` is
added to each decoded index exactly once; `primitiveCount` fixes the consumed index count;
`minVertexIndex`/`numVertices` are hints; `instanceCount` never widens or narrows the geometry range
and the range never changes the instance count; `VertexBufferBinding.VertexOffset` is a vertex
**element** offset on each stream independently; and `InstanceFrequency` is the number of drawn
instances that share one per-instance record.

### The ticket named one symptom; the two backends do not share a root cause

The recorded symptom — `DrawIndexedInstanced(indexCount, instanceCount, 0, 0, 0)` — was real on
both. Classifying them independently (as required) showed the shared symptom sits on a **different
mechanism per backend**, and that each backend additionally dropped three offsets the ticket never
named. Nothing here was inferred from the other backend's code.

| Axis | D3D11 before | D3D12 before |
|---|---|---|
| `startIndex` | `StartIndexLocation` literal `0` | `StartIndexLocation` literal `0` |
| `baseVertex` | `BaseVertexLocation` literal `0` | `BaseVertexLocation` literal `0` |
| per-vertex `VertexOffset` | `IASetVertexBuffers` offsets array literal `{0, 0}` | no offset field exists on a `D3D12_VERTEX_BUFFER_VIEW` at all — a whole-buffer view was bound |
| per-instance `VertexOffset` | same literal `{0, 0}` | same whole-buffer view |
| instance stride | hardcoded `kInstanceStride = 64`, ignoring the bound stream's own | correct already (`GetViewEXT()` reports `stride_`) |
| `InstanceFrequency` | `InstanceDataStepRate` baked as `1` into **one** cached `ID3D11InputLayout` | baked as `1` into **one** cached PSO |
| byte/element | the two are the same object in D3D11 (a byte offset), so the conversion had no home | ditto, via `BufferLocation` |
| device teardown | no cache-clearing recovery path exists in this backend (unchanged) | `RecreateDeviceEXT` reset the single PSO |

Two further axes were **measured correct and left alone**: D3D11 sets viewport, scissor, blend,
depth-stencil and rasterizer state eagerly in its setters rather than per draw, so the instanced path
inherits them correctly (`InstancedDrawRespectsViewportAndScissor` and
`InstancedDrawAppliesExplicitStateWithoutChangingItsRange` both pass); and the ordinary D3D11 draw
rebinds slot 0 and its own input layout, so the instanced draw leaves nothing behind that a later
ordinary draw can read (asserted by the middle leg of the new binding oracle).

### The correction

`startIndex`/`baseVertex` now reach both native draws, exactly the model REMED-GFX-020 established
for these backends' ordinary indexed path. Both binding element offsets are converted to bytes with
**each stream's own stride, exactly once, only at the native binding** — a D3D11
`IASetVertexBuffers` byte offset, and on D3D12 a new `AdvanceVertexBufferView` that moves
`BufferLocation` forward and shrinks `SizeInBytes` by the same 64-bit byte count so the view never
claims to run past the resource. `InstanceFrequency` becomes `InstanceDataStepRate`, and the D3D11
input-layout cache and the D3D12 instanced-PSO cache are keyed on it (`std::unordered_map<UINT, …>`,
one or two entries in practice) so an alternating frequency can neither reuse a stale rate nor build
a native object per draw. D3D11 also takes the per-instance stride from the bound stream, which is
the same quantity the element→byte conversion needs. `StartInstanceLocation` stays `0` on both: the
per-instance stream's start is already in its binding, and adding it again would apply one public
offset twice. D3D12's `RecreateDeviceEXT` clears the whole PSO map, not one entry.

No CPU repacking, no duplicated geometry, no per-draw native object, no extra submission, no added
frame, `Present`, retry, sleep or wait, no shader or bytecode change, no public API change, and no
other backend's production touched.

### Runtime classification and A/B

**D3D11 — measured, 3/17 → 17/17.** Same binary, same fixture, production reverted per file with
`git checkout HEAD -- <two files>` and rebuilt (never a stash, never a tree checkout). The pre-fix
3/17 reproduces GFX-118's recorded 3/16 exactly, one test wider. The pre-fix failure signatures
separate the mechanisms by hand rather than lumping them:

- `InstancedDrawHonorsNonzeroStartIndex` — slots 4-6 requested, **slots 0-2 rendered**: 7405 lit
  pixels inside the excluded columns `[0,457)`, first at `(171,24)`. That is *wrong first index*
  (element-zero prefix), not a wrong base vertex and not a missing draw.
- `D3DHonorsBindingOffsetsAndInstanceFrequency` — one cell map naming three defects at once:

  ```
  band 0: 0 0 0 0 0 0 2468      slot 6 = the MESH PREFIX DECOY  -> per-vertex VertexOffset ignored
  band 1: 0 0 0 0 0 0 2468      four bands lit, not two         -> step rate 1, not 2
  band 2: 0 0 0 0 0 0 2468      band 3 lit                      -> instance VertexOffset ignored
  band 3: 0 0 0 0 0 0 2468         (record 0 = RowTranslation(3))
  ```

  Post-fix the same request lights slot 3 in bands 0-1 only. A byte-vs-element mix-up cannot produce
  that: reading offset `3` as *bytes* lands three quarters of the way through one 16-byte vertex.

**The runtime route was Wine's builtin D3D11, not DXVK — stated plainly rather than glossed.**
DXVK 2.6.0's `dxgi` still aborts SDL's video init under Xvfb (`readMonitorEdidFromKey: Failed to get
EDID reg key size` → `SDL_InitSubSystem(SDL_INIT_VIDEO) failed: No displays available`), and `:0` was
forbidden this session. This is the environment, A/B-proven three ways: the **untouched, known-good**
`cna_test_d3d11_smoke.exe` fails identically; SDL initialises and creates its window the moment
`dxgi` is Wine builtin (failing later only at `CreateSwapChainForHwnd`, as expected without native
DXGI); and `DXVK_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME=llvmpipe` does not help, confirming it is GPU-independent.
Injecting a valid 128-byte EDID into the Wine registry and onto the Xvfb RandR output both failed to
persist — Wine rewrites `BAD_EDID` from an X server that exposes none. **No DXVK-backed D3D11 result
is claimed.** Under Wine's own D3D11 the offsets, base vertex, first index, instance offset and step
rate are nevertheless genuine Direct3D 11 input-assembler semantics, which is what this ticket is
about.

**D3D12 — inspection plus a clean cross-build; runtime still blocked, A/B-proven.** The offscreen
D3D12 route works here (`cna_test_d3d12_smoke.exe` is ALL PASS through real vkd3d-proton 3.1.0), but
the windowed `GraphicsDevice` route that the instanced suite needs dies immediately after device
init (exit 5). **The same test with this task's two D3D12 files reverted to HEAD and rebuilt dies at
the identical point with the identical exit code** — REMED-BUILD-012, pre-existing, not this change.
D3D12 therefore gets a correct-by-inspection classification and a clean cross-build, and is reported
as such.

### Coverage

The permanent suite now compiles for D3D11 and D3D12 (17 tests each). REMED-GFX-122's
`EasyGLHonorsBindingOffsetsAndInstanceFrequency` **keeps its name**; its body moved into a shared
fixture oracle so the new `D3DHonorsBindingOffsetsAndInstanceFrequency` asserts the identical
contract instead of a paraphrase of it. The oracle is compiled only for the backends actually
corrected to honour binding offsets (EasyGL, D3D11, D3D12) — asserting it on the others would be
declaring a contract nobody has measured. The instance axis gained count **3**, the value that tells
an off-by-one in a step-rate or instance-offset conversion apart from a power-of-two coincidence.

| Required axis | Where it is asserted |
|---|---|
| zero / nonzero vertex offset | 16 shared tests at 0; oracle at 3 |
| zero / nonzero `startIndex` | zero-offset control; `…HonorsNonzeroStartIndex`; oracle at 9 |
| zero / nonzero `baseVertex` | zero-offset control; `…HonorsNonzeroBaseVertex`; `…StartIndexAndBaseVertexTogether` |
| 16-bit / 32-bit indices | `…ThirtyTwoBitIndicesHonorTheSameElementRange` vs the rest |

| `InstanceFrequency` 1 and 2 | 1 throughout the suite; 2 in the oracle |
| multiple vertex streams | every instanced draw binds two |
| static and dynamic buffers | `InstancedDynamicBuffersHonorRangeAndInstances`; oracle mixes a static mesh with a dynamic instance stream |

| instanced → ordinary → instanced | oracle's three legs |
| backbuffer and `RenderTarget2D` | `InstancedDrawIntoRenderTargetKeepsItsRangeAndInstances` |
| disposal and device teardown | `DisposingAfterQueuedInstancedDrawsIsSafe`; `SourceUpdatesAfterAQueuedInstancedDrawDoNotAlterIt`; D3D12 `RecreateDeviceEXT` clears the PSO map |

The oracle distinguishes every failure mode the task required: element-zero geometry (slot 6/slot 0
prefix decoys), wrong base vertex vs wrong first index (separated by the two single-axis tests plus
their combination), ignored instance offset (band 3), byte/element confusion (offset 3 read as bytes
cannot land on a vertex boundary), stale layout/PSO (the A→B→A leg), and wrong step rate (four lit
bands instead of two).

## REMED-GFX-200 — `VertexBufferBinding.VertexOffset` on the ordinary draw routes — DONE 2026-08-02

### The recorded scope was right, and the loss point is exactly where it said

`GraphicsDevice::DrawPrimitives` and `DrawIndexedPrimitives` each build a fresh `GpuDrawParams`, call
`FillGpuDrawParams`, set only their own arguments, and never read `currentVertexBuffers_`. Only
`DrawInstancedPrimitives` read binding 0's `VertexOffset`. The offset was therefore lost in the shared
public layer, above every backend — no backend was at fault, and no backend-local fix could reach it.

### Reproduced first, on unfixed HEAD

The new shared oracle ran **2/17 on EasyGL before any production change**, and the two that passed were
exactly the two zero-offset controls. The failing frames named the mechanism directly:

```
VertexOffset=3, startIndex=0        band 3: 0 0 0 0 0 0 330   <- the PREFIX DECOY (slot 6)
                                    byte-identical to its own zero-offset control
VertexOffset=3, startIndex=9        band 0: 0 0 330 0 0 0 0   <- slot 2, one offset-width left of 3
VertexOffset=3, baseVertex=9        band 0: 0 0 330 0 0 0 0   <- slot 2, same displacement
instanced leg, VertexOffset=6       band 0: 0 0 0 0 330 0 0   <- slot 4, CORRECT (REMED-GFX-122)
```

The instanced leg being correct in the same binary is the asymmetry the ticket named, measured.

### One shared correction, not a per-backend sweep

Both ordinary routes now read binding 0 through a single `GraphicsDevice::CurrentVertexBufferOffset()`
— the identical rule `DrawInstancedPrimitives` already applied inline, now single-sourced with no
behavioural change there — and carry the offset in the element-unit field each route already owns:
`vertexStart` for the non-indexed route, `baseVertex` for the indexed one.

That is a contract statement, not a shortcut. `VertexOffset` shifts the stream base; `vertexStart` and
`baseVertex` index that same stream. All three are whole vertex elements against the same declaration
stride, and `Draw*PrimitivesEx` hand a backend **exactly one** per-vertex stream. Their sum is
therefore the first record fetched, and delivering it through that channel reaches every backend's
already-remediated single stride multiplication at the native binding (REMED-GFX-020/060/117/119), in
elements, with that stream's own stride, applying each of the two exactly once.

- `startIndex` is untouched — it selects index elements, which a binding offset never displaces.
- `GpuDrawParams::vertexBufferOffset` stays **0** on the ordinary routes, and its contract is now
  documented at the backend boundary. Populating it *as well* would apply the public offset twice on
  EasyGL/D3D11/D3D12. The instanced route keeps that field because its per-instance stream carries an
  independent offset `baseVertex` cannot express.
- REMED-GFX-113's and REMED-GFX-118's range validation now counts the offset, matching what the
  instanced route has done since REMED-GFX-118.

No backend production changed. No public API, shader or bytecode changed.

### The oracle

`tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/OrdinaryDrawBindingOffsetTests.cpp` — a two-axis cell map where
the **column** says which records a draw consumed and the **band** says which bytes those records were.
Each defect lights a different cell: a dropped offset → slot 6 band 3 (or one width left); a doubled
`baseVertex`/`startIndex` → slot 6 band 0; a byte-for-element multiply → 48 records into a 24-record
buffer, so nothing lights at all; a wrong stream → band 2; stale contents after an update → band 0
where band 1 was written; a stale previous offset → the previous leg's slot.

Every assertion is `requested cell lit AND frame total == that cell's count`, so geometry landing
between cells is rejected too — no colour tolerance, no process-survival fallback. The zero-offset
controls assert the prefix decoy's **own cell** rather than "nothing rendered", so they fail if the
fixture ever stops rendering.

Coverage: offset 0 and nonzero; offset×`startIndex`; offset×`baseVertex`; all three at once; 16- and
32-bit indices; static and dynamic buffers; a rewrite between draws; two streams with different
offsets; A→B→A reuse; ordinary→instanced→ordinary; return to a previous layout; disposal with handle
reuse and device teardown; both `SetVertexBuffer` overloads; the offset-inclusive range gate;
backbuffer **and** RenderTarget2D destinations.

## REMED-GFX-201 — ordinary multi-stream vertex input — DONE 2026-08-03

### The authoritative contract, from source

Read before writing any code, and it changed the design twice.

`Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.GraphicsDevice.SetVertexBuffers(params VertexBufferBinding[])`
accepts up to 16 bindings (`FNA/src/Graphics/GraphicsDevice.cs:1143`, ceiling
`vertexBufferBindings.Length`), and `VertexBufferBinding`
(`FNA/src/Graphics/Vertices/VertexBufferBinding.cs`) is `(VertexBuffer, vertexOffset,
instanceFrequency)`. The decisive evidence is that **the ordinary and instanced routes use the same
code path**: `DrawPrimitives` calls `PrepareVertexBindingArray(0)`
(`GraphicsDevice.cs:1301`), `DrawIndexedPrimitives` calls `PrepareVertexBindingArray(baseVertex)`
(`:1242`) and `DrawInstancedPrimitives` calls `PrepareVertexBindingArray(baseVertex)` (`:1274`) —
all three then hand the driver the **complete** binding array
(`GraphicsDevice.cs:1649-1670`), one `FNA3D_VertexBufferBinding` per slot carrying that stream's
buffer, declaration, stride, element offset and instance frequency. Multi-stream ordinary input is
not an edge case in XNA; it is the same mechanism instancing already uses.

The per-stream arithmetic, from both reference drivers:

- OpenGL (`FNA3D/src/FNA3D_Driver_OpenGL.c:2486-2494`):
  `basePtr = vertexDeclaration->vertexStride * (bindings[i].vertexOffset + baseVertex)`, then
  `ptr = basePtr + element->offset`. **Per stream, with that stream's own stride.**
- D3D11 (`FNA3D/src/FNA3D_Driver_D3D11.c:2226-2248`): `offset = bindings[i].vertexOffset * stride`,
  `IASetVertexBuffers(i, 1, &handle, &stride, &offset)` — the binding index **is** the native input
  slot; `d3dElement->InputSlot = i`, `AlignedByteOffset = element->offset` (stream-local),
  `InputSlotClass`/`InstanceDataStepRate` from that binding's own `instanceFrequency`
  (`:960-971`).
- `vertexStart` is not folded into any binding: `DrawPrimitives` passes `baseVertex = 0` and
  `FNA3D_DrawPrimitives(primitiveType, vertexStart, primitiveCount)` reaches `glDrawArrays`'s
  `first`, which advances **every** enabled array by that many of **its own** elements.

Composition is by **SEMANTIC, not by position** — the fact that reshaped this task. Both drivers
track every claimed `(usage, usageIndex)` pair across the bindings in slot order; a later element
repeating a claimed pair is pushed to the next free index for that usage, and
`MOJOSHADER_*GetVertexAttribLocation` then returns `-1` — *"Stream not in use!"* — so it is skipped
entirely (`FNA3D_Driver_OpenGL.c:2500-2527`, `FNA3D_Driver_D3D11.c:901-950`). A second stream that
merely repeats stream 0's declaration therefore contributes **nothing**; it is not the second half
of a vertex.

Answers to the questions this task had to settle:

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum public binding count | 16 (`kMaxVertexStreams`), enforced by `SetVertexBuffers` already |
| Must slots be contiguous | Not required; CNA compacts, preserving each stream's public slot number |
| Empty/null slot | `SetVertexBuffers` throws `ArgumentNullException` — a half-described vertex can never reach a draw |
| Is binding 0 mandatory | Yes on the ordinary routes: `currentVertexBuffer_` *is* binding 0 |
| VertexOffset units | Vertex ELEMENTS, multiplied by **that stream's own** stride exactly once |
| vertexStart | Applies to **every** per-vertex stream, each in its own elements |
| baseVertex + index | Applies to **every** per-vertex stream, each in its own elements |
| startIndex | Index elements only; no binding offset ever displaces it |
| `InstanceFrequency != 0` on an ordinary draw | Legal in XNA — the divisor is applied and a 1-instance draw simply stays on that stream's element 0. CNA excludes such a binding from the per-vertex layout and does not advance it with `baseVertex` |
| Mixed per-vertex/per-instance | Only `DrawInstancedPrimitives` consumes the per-instance stream; that route is untouched here |
| Duplicate semantics | The later stream's elements are dropped ("Stream not in use!") |
| Incompatible declarations | A stream repeating *some but not all* of an earlier stream's usages has no expressible stride-keyed layout and throws `NotSupportedException` |
| State persistence | `SetVertexBuffer` collapses the set to one binding; `SetVertexBuffers` replaces it wholesale — both already true, now asserted |

### The pre-fix loss point, proven

`GraphicsDevice::DrawPrimitives`/`DrawIndexedPrimitives` passed
`currentVertexBuffer_->GetBackend()` — which `SetVertexBuffers` defines as binding 0 — into
`IGraphicsBackend::DrawPrimitivesEx`/`DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx`, whose signatures take exactly
**one** `const IVertexBufferBackend&`. `currentVertexBuffers_[1..15]` were read by nothing on those
routes; the only multi-stream channel in the whole codebase was the instanced route's separate
`GpuDrawParams::instanceVb`, found by scanning for `InstanceFrequency > 0`.

The loss is **shared and backend-independent**, and it is deeper than the ticket recorded: the
declaration itself never reaches eight of the nine rasterizing backends. Only EasyGL stores it —
`Vulkan`, `WebGPU`, `SdlGpu`, `Bgfx`, `D3D11`, `D3D12`, `D3D9`, `Software` and `Headless` all
declare `void SetVertexDeclaration(const VertexDeclaration&) override {}` and infer their native
input elements from the **byte stride** alone (`D3DCommon::InputElementsForStride` and the
equivalent per-backend tables). A second stream had neither a binding to arrive on nor a layout to
be described by.

### Red-first, on unfixed HEAD

`tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/OrdinaryDrawMultiStreamTests.cpp` (new, committed first at
`272c2261` with production still at `75b61fa4`) measured **3 of 19 passing on EasyGL**. The three
were the two pure public-API contract cases and REMED-GFX-113's existing stream-0 range gate.
**Every pixel case rendered nothing at all — `total lit: 0`** — because binding 1 reached no backend
and binding 0's 12-byte stride matches no layout anywhere; and **both** secondary-stream range gates
let an out-of-range request straight through.

The oracle is three-axis. Stream 0 is POSITION only (12-byte stride); stream 1 is COLOUR only
(4-byte stride); their concatenation is byte-for-byte
`CNA::Internal::Graphics::PositionColorStream`, the packed 16-byte layout every backend already
recognizes — so the combined vertex needs no new shader anywhere, while **no rendered pixel of it
can be produced from stream 0 alone**. The column says which records stream 0 supplied, the band
says which bytes those were, and the colour says which records **stream 1** supplied. Colour codes
are the six `{0,255}` RGB corners, 255 apart in at least one channel, so the nearest-corner
classifier is exact rather than tolerant and a non-corner pixel classifies `unknown` and fails.

### Architecture

`GpuDrawParams` gains `std::array<GpuVertexStreamBinding, 16> vertexStreams`, `vertexStreamCount`
and `combinedVertexStride`. `GpuVertexStreamBinding` is CNA's `FNA3D_VertexBufferBinding`: public
slot, backend buffer, that stream's own stride, its own `VertexOffset`, its `InstanceFrequency`, its
vertex count, and `combinedByteBase` — where its declaration begins inside the combined vertex.
Fixed capacity, captured **by value**, no heap allocation on any draw, no pointer into mutable
`currentVertexBuffers_`.

`combinedByteBase` is the bridge between the two worlds: CNA's backends describe a layout by byte
stride, so their element tables use *combined* offsets, while FNA3D takes `AlignedByteOffset`
straight from the *per-stream* declaration. `MapCombinedOffsetToStream()` converts one to the other
and **degenerates to the identity for a single stream**, which is what lets a backend route its
existing stride-derived layout through it with no behavioural change until a second stream appears.
`CombinedVertexStrideOr()`, `HasMultipleVertexStreams()` and `VertexStreamByteOffset()` degenerate
the same way.

### The offset fold

The ordinary routes fold the **smallest** per-vertex binding offset into `vertexStart`/`baseVertex`
and hand each stream the non-negative remainder:

```
non-indexed: stream k's first element = stream[k].vertexOffset + params.vertexStart
indexed:     stream k's fetched element = stream[k].vertexOffset + params.baseVertex + index
             where params.vertexStart/baseVertex already include min_k(binding[k].VertexOffset)
```

Substituting gives `binding[k].VertexOffset + publicVertexStart` for every k, because the folded
term and the remainder are both multiplied by **that stream's own** stride exactly once — by the
native draw's start-vertex and by the native binding's byte offset respectively. Folding binding
**0**'s offset instead (REMED-GFX-200's rule) would make a stream whose offset is smaller carry a
**negative** byte offset, which Vulkan/D3D12/WebGPU offsets cannot express; the minimum is the only
split that keeps every one non-negative. With a single stream the fold is the whole offset and the
remainder is 0, so **every single-stream native binding is byte-identical to its REMED-GFX-200
form** — which is why GFX-200's 17/17 stayed 17/17 on all eight of its backends.

### Validation

REMED-GFX-113's gate widened from stream 0 to every per-vertex stream, in that stream's own
elements against that stream's own capacity, naming the offending slot. A **short secondary stream
is now rejected even when stream 0 is long enough** — the case that cannot be expressed at all
without per-stream ranges, and one of the two gates that were red pre-fix. Argument validation runs
**before** the capability gate so an out-of-range request reports the same public exception on every
backend. No O(vertex-count) scan was added. Software additionally bounds its own addressing gate by
the **shortest** bound stream.

### Capability boundary — the honest part

`GraphicsCapability::MultiStreamVertexInput` is the **one entry whose default is `false`**. Binding a
second per-vertex stream is real per-backend work — re-slotting a stride-derived element table
across several native bindings — so a backend must opt in **by name**; defaulting to true would let
a backend that silently renders from stream 0 alone claim otherwise, which looks like a correct draw
of the wrong data. `GraphicsDevice::ValidateVertexStreamCapability` rejects a multi-stream ordinary
draw on a backend that does not claim it, and an over-wide binding set on one whose
`GetMaxVertexStreams()` is below 16 — deterministically, before native submission, never by
truncating the list or collapsing streams.

`UnsupportedBackendRejectsMultiStreamDeterministically` asserts that boundary **in both directions
on every backend**, and flips to the positive assertion the moment a backend claims the capability,
so the skips cannot outlive the gap they describe.

| Backend | `MultiStreamVertexInput` | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EasyGL | **true** | implemented |
| Software | **true** | implemented |
| Vulkan | false | 16 pipeline builders each bake one `VkVertexInputBindingDescription` at binding 0 with combined-layout attribute offsets |
| Bgfx | false | one `bgfx::VertexLayout` per stride, submitted through `setVertexBuffer(stream 0)` |
| WebGPU | false | one `WGPUVertexBufferLayout` per pipeline |
| SDL_GPU | false | one vertex buffer description per pipeline |
| D3D11 | false | `D3D11InputLayoutCache` is keyed on `(variant, stride)`; every element is `InputSlot = 0` |
| D3D12 | false | `InputElementsForStrideD3D12` is baked into the PSO with `InputSlot = 0` |
| D3D9 | false | `GetOrCreateVertexDeclarationEXT(stride)` emits `D3DVERTEXELEMENT9.Stream = 0` |
| Headless | false | rasterizes nothing; claiming it would fabricate success |
| SDL_Renderer / Canvas / Ascii / DX3 | false | 2D-only, report false for every capability |

CNA public maximum 16; EasyGL/Software tested maximum 3 (the three-stream fixture); no backend
reports a lower `GetMaxVertexStreams()` yet.

### Backend implementations

**EasyGL.** Every per-vertex stream is bound into the VAO the named buffer owns, at attribute
locations continuing after the previous stream's — the same "location N == Nth field of the ported
HLSL input struct" convention `ApplyLayout()` uses for one stream and `DrawInstancedPrimitivesEx`
already uses to append a per-instance one — each with its own VBO, stride and byte offset.
`glDrawArrays`'s `first` and `glDrawElementsBaseVertex`'s `baseVertex` then advance all of them by
the same element count, each by its own stride. Stream 0's attributes are rewritten **only** when it
carries a residual offset, so the common case leaves `ApplyLayout()`'s work untouched; after the
draw the VAO is restored to exactly what `ApplyLayout()` built, so a later single-stream draw
through the same buffer cannot inherit a foreign VBO on a stale location. No VAO is created per
draw. A bound stream with no `VertexDeclaration` throws rather than drawing from stream 0 alone.
REMED-GFX-122's instanced path is untouched.

**Software.** `BuildGenericClipVertex` now reads through a `CombinedVertexReader` that resolves each
combined-layout byte offset to the stream that owns it, so every attribute is fetched from its own
buffer with that buffer's own stride and binding offset. **No interleaved temporary, no per-vertex
allocation** — `recordBase[0]` is the same pointer the old `raw` was and `At(n)` is byte-for-byte
the old `raw + n` for a single stream. REMED-GFX-119/124/150/182 untouched.

### Cardinality

Per public draw, single-stream: unchanged in every count — same one native draw, one pass, one
submit, one `GpuDrawParams` on the stack, same layout-cache key (`combinedVertexStride` **==**
`vb.GetStride()`), same native binding bytes. Per additional stream: exactly one native binding
operation (EasyGL: one VBO bind plus that stream's attribute pointers; Software: one extra base
pointer). **No extra draw, pass, submit, frame, wait or Present; no stream interleaving copy; no
temporary vertex buffer; no heap allocation per draw or per vertex; no new cache and no unbounded
growth** — the stream list is a fixed 16-entry array inside the same stack-constructed
`GpuDrawParams` that already carried 18 KB of bone transforms.

### False-positive audit

One found, and it was a **real design error caught by an existing test**, not a weak assertion.
REMED-GFX-200's `MultipleStreamsUseOnlyTheGeometryStreamsOwnOffset` binds two *complete*
`VertexPositionColor` streams and asserts only binding 0's data is used. The first implementation
concatenated declarations positionally, making that a 32-byte combined vertex, and the test failed
on Vulkan. Reading FNA3D's duplicate-usage handling showed the test was right and the design wrong:
XNA composes by semantic and drops a repeated `(usage, usageIndex)`. The rule was corrected, the
test went green unmodified, and it is now a genuine oracle for semantic dedup. Its assertion was
strengthened by nothing and needed nothing — it was already the strongest statement available.

No other test in the tree binds several buffers to an ordinary draw at all, so there was no second
candidate to strengthen. The exact prior blind spot was structural rather than assertional: **no
fixture could express a split-stream declaration end to end**, which is why the ticket was
`UNMEASURED AT RUNTIME`.

### Ordinary versus instanced

Deliberately kept distinct. `DrawInstancedPrimitives` leaves `vertexStreamCount` at **0** and keeps
its established `vb` + `instanceVb` + `vertexBufferOffset` + `instanceVertexOffset` channel
(REMED-GFX-118/122/123), so no backend's instanced path can double-apply an offset through the new
representation and every instancing gate is untouched. `HasMultipleVertexStreams()` is false there
by construction. Per-instance bindings that appear in an *ordinary* draw's binding set are recorded
with their own frequency, excluded from the per-vertex combined layout, and not advanced by
`baseVertex` — matching XNA, where such a binding simply stays on its element 0 for a one-instance
draw. Extending the shared stream description to the instanced route is **REMED-GFX-202**.

Seven backends still report `MultiStreamVertexInput = false`. Each is a real, separately verifiable
piece of work in a different native input-layout model, and each is ticketed rather than swept:

- **REMED-GFX-202** — extend the shared `GpuVertexStreamBinding` list to `DrawInstancedPrimitives`
  so the instanced route stops carrying its own parallel two-stream channel.
- **REMED-GFX-203** — Vulkan ordinary multi-stream input.
- **REMED-GFX-204** — Bgfx ordinary multi-stream input.
- **REMED-GFX-205** — WebGPU ordinary multi-stream input.
- **REMED-GFX-206** — SDL_GPU ordinary multi-stream input.
- **REMED-GFX-207** — D3D11 and D3D12 ordinary multi-stream input.
- **REMED-GFX-208** — D3D9 ordinary multi-stream input.
- **REMED-GFX-209** — `GraphicsDeviceCapabilityTest.DoesNotSupportWireFrame` asserts EasyGL's
  wireframe gap unconditionally and therefore fails on every backend that *does* support wireframe
  (measured failing on Software). Pre-existing, unrelated to this task, found while classifying the
  Software full suite.

**REMED-GFX-199 remains OPEN and untouched.** It is a D3D12 PSO render-target-format cache-key
defect with no relationship to vertex input; nothing in this task touched
`GetOrCreateInstancedPsoEXT` or any format cache key.
